author: cybottm
body:
## Summary
- **First slice** of the `jira_client.py` (2,852 LOC) god-class decomposition — pivoting now that `openproject_client.py` is down 78% (Phases 2a–2y, 19 services).
- Five project-domain methods move from `jira_client.py` into a new `JiraProjectService` exposed as `self.projects`.
- Done by a sub-agent in worktree isolation; pure mechanical move, no security fixes needed (HTTP only, no Ruby script generation).
- `JiraClient` keeps a thin delegator for each method so existing callers work unchanged.

## Methods moved
- `get_projects`
- `get_issue_types`
- `get_project_roles`
- `get_project_permission_scheme`
- `get_project_metadata_enhanced` (the `@cached(ttl=3600)` decorator travels with the method)

## Notable observations (sub-agent verbatim)
- `jira_client.py` uses an unusual `except A, B:` comma syntax (pre-existing, lines 109/115/132/923). Python 3.14 happens to parse the operands as a tuple; preserved the exact pattern in the moved `get_project_roles`. **Not addressed in this PR** — separate cleanup PR planned.
- The service imports `JiraClient` symbols at module load. The reverse direction (`jira_client.py` importing `JiraProjectService`) is deferred until inside `__init__` to avoid a load-time circular dependency — same pattern `openproject_client.py` uses.
- No security-sensitive paths: HTTP only (no Ruby, no shell). `project_key` flows into URL paths exactly as before; nothing new introduced.

## Numbers
- `jira_client.py`: **2,852 → 2,610 LOC** (−242)
- `jira_project_service.py`: **0 → 316 LOC** (new)

## Verification
- `pytest tests/unit`: 953 passed
- `mypy src/`: clean (118 files)
- `ruff check` / `ruff format`: clean

## Test plan
- [x] All 6 required CI checks must pass.
- [ ] Copilot review acknowledged & comments resolved before merge.

This pull request introduces several improvements and additions to the vintrace-sdk codebase, focusing on developer guidance, new skills documentation, type/schema enhancements, and expanded test coverage. The most notable changes are the significant rewrite and clarification of `AGENTS.md`, the addition of two OpenCode skills, new Zod schemas and types, and new unit tests for API endpoints. There are also minor dependency and configuration cleanups.

**Documentation and Guidance Updates:**

* Major rewrite of `AGENTS.md` to provide clearer, more concise guidance for agentic coding, including updated project structure, conventions, error handling, method patterns, and testing instructions. This makes onboarding and contribution easier for new developers.

* Added `.opencode/skills/git-commit/SKILL.md` and `.opencode/skills/grill-me/SKILL.md` to document new OpenCode skills for committing changes and design interviews, respectively. **Types, Schemas, and Exports:**

* Added new Zod schemas and types for `UpdateMetrics` and `UpdateMetricsResponse` in `src/validation/schemas.ts`, supporting new API capabilities.

author: svm94
body:
### 💡 What
Added a "Skip to main content" link that allows keyboard and screen reader users to bypass repetitive navigation and jump straight into the primary page content.

### 🎯 Why
This is a standard accessibility (a11y) requirement known as "Bypass Blocks" (WCAG 2.4.1). It saves keyboard users from tabbing through global navigation links on every page load.

### 📸 Before/After
Before: Keyboard users would have to tab through the full app structure to reach the content.
After: Pressing "Tab" immediately upon page load reveals a highly visible button offering a skip action directly to `<main id="main-content">`.

### ♿ Accessibility
- Added skip link with correct target (`href="#main-content"`).
- Target area correctly receives focus (`tabIndex={-1}`).
- Link uses `focus-visible` to only show to keyboard users, remaining hidden to mouse users.
- Smooth visual transition handled safely using CSS hardware accelerated `translate` instead of janky `top` positional changes.

### Motivation
- Provide a polished, minimal, dark UI with consistent spacing, typography, and component layout while keeping the downloader workflow intact.  
- Replace the insecure/awkward client-side password gate with a maintainable, configurable server-side auth and session so access persists across refreshes.  

### Description
- Implemented a full frontend redesign and refactor by replacing the old home page with three clear stages: `PasswordPage`, `LoadingPage`, and `DownloaderPage`, plus improved CSS tokens, card styles, buttons, spacing, and responsive layout in `client/src/pages/home.tsx` and `client/src/index.css`.  
- Moved auth to the server with session-backed endpoints `POST /api/auth`, `GET /api/auth/status`, and `POST /api/auth/logout` and integrated `express-session` to persist access (changes in `server/routes.ts` and `server/index.ts`).  
- Switched Roblox version retrieval to the backend endpoint (`/api/roblox-version`) and updated the frontend hook to call it (`client/src/hooks/use-roblox-version.ts`).  
- Added clear configuration and documentation: updated `.env.example` to include `SITE_PASSWORD` and `SESSION_SECRET`, and documented password usage in `README.md`.  

### Testing
- Ran typecheck with `npm run check` and it completed successfully.  
- Built production server bundle with `npm run build:server` (frontend build + server bundle) and the build completed successfully.

## Summary

`zerog-storage.ts` の SHA-256 stub を `@0gfoundation/0g-ts-sdk` の real `Indexer.upload` に差し替え、playLog と AgentSafetyAttestation を 0G Galileo testnet (chain id 16602) に upload。`0g://{rootHash}` URI を ENS text record `agent.safety.attestation` と iNFT `storageCID` metadata に伝播させ、judge が 0G storage explorer で実データを検証できる状態に格上げ。

## 実装の柱

- **SDK 統合**: `@0gfoundation/0g-ts-sdk@1.2.8` (npm 公開、`@0glabs/...` フォールバック不要)。Vite bundle は **dynamic import で 4 chunk に分離**、メイン bundle 影響 **+3KB のみ** (game-end 時にロード)。
- **chain id 修正**: live RPC で `eth_chainId = 0x40da` (= 16602) を確認、既存コードの **16601 → 16602** を全 5 箇所 (chains.ts / App.tsx CHAIN_LABELS / foundry.toml / wagmi.ts / README) で同期。
- **chain switch シーケンス**: Sepolia → 0G Galileo (upload) → Sepolia (ENS write) を `walletClient.switchChain` で順次。各 switch reject / 失敗で日本語 friendly error。
- **viem ↔ ethers ブリッジ**: SDK が ethers v6 `Signer` を要求、orchestrator で `BrowserProvider` を dynamic import して viem WalletClient → ethers Signer 変換。
- **フェイルセーフ**: 0G upload 失敗 / 未保有 testnet ETH → `sha256://{hex}` stub にフォールバック、ENS write は継続。

## 5 役割並列実装の成果物

| Role | 成果物 |
|------|--------|
| 仕様 | docs/specs/2026-05-01-zerog-storage-real.md |

## QA Critical の判定

- **#1 chain id 16601 残存** → 残存は migration 説明コメント 1 行のみで false positive。修正済の確認 OK
- **#2 rootHash front-running** → content-addressed なので攻撃成立しない (subname owner 衝突は前 PR の pre-flight ownerOf check で既に対策済)
- **#3 merkleTree main thread block** → follow-up (Web Worker 化)
- **#4 env URL injection** → follow-up (CSP allowlist 検討)

| Prize | Score |
|-------|-------|
| 0G Storage (Autonomous Agents / iNFT) | **3** (stub → real demo) |
| 0G iNFT (memory embed の客観証明) | **2** (storageCID が real 0G CID に格上げ) |
| ENS Identity / Creative | 1 (URI スキームが `sha256://` → `0g://` に格上げ) |

## Summary

Closes 7 CodeRabbit findings from the [PR #91](https://github.com/zerofog/cortex/pull/91) review (parent ticket [ZF0-1453](https://linear.app/zerofog/issue/ZF0-1453) — Panel header chrome). Decomposed into 4 cohesive sub-issues by file-coupling rather than severity. All implementer + reviewer rounds tracked via the ship-task pipeline.

Linear: [ZF0-1474](https://linear.app/zerofog/issue/ZF0-1474/coderabbit-follow-ups-from-zf0-1453-pr-91-review-8-items)

## Items closed

| # | Sev | File | Sub-issue | Commit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Major | `Panel.tsx:382` drift recompute on buffer mutation | A (ZF0-1477) | 3410692 + 38d2ad0 |
| 2 | Major | `override.ts:50` staleSources per-(source, property, pseudo) keying | B (ZF0-1478) | dcc344b |
| 3 | Major | `override.ts:734` timer-driven TTL sweep for evictStalePendingEdits | C (ZF0-1479) | dc9b754 |
| 4 | Minor | `SizingControls.tsx:52` min/max stale prop wiring | B (ZF0-1478) | dcc344b |
| 5 | Minor | `StagingDriftBanner.tsx:25` edge-trigger dismissed reset | A (ZF0-1477) | 3410692 + 38d2ad0 |
| 6 | Minor | `cortex-app.test.tsx:1141` falsifiable hmr-applied propagation | D (ZF0-1480) | c540d89 |
| 7 | Minor | `override.test.ts:1472` escaped CSS selector assertion | D (ZF0-1480) | c540d89 |

Item #8 from the original ticket was a duplicate of major #1 — already fixed inline in PR #91 commit `13fabaf`.

## Sub-issue decomposition

- **Sub A — Drift state machine**: exposed `version: number` on `StagingBufferHandle`, added `buffer.version` to Panel.tsx:382's reconcile dep array (so drift recomputes on buffer mutation, not just HMR). Banner edge-trigger reset uses `useRef` prev-tracking with strict-`>` comparison — banner stays dismissed across count decreases / no-change.
- **Sub B — Stale-tracking reshape**: `staleSources: Set<string>` (source-keyed) → `staleEntries: Set<string>` (per-tuple via existing `priorValuesKey(source, property, pseudo)` helper). Public `onStale` listener signature preserved via `staleSourcesFromEntries` projection helper. Wired `stale={stale}` to all 6 NumericInputs in SizingControls.
- **Sub C — Timer-driven TTL sweep**: added `private sweepTimerId` + `armStaleSweep`/`disarmStaleSweep` helpers. 5s sweep period (1/7 of 35s TTL). Arms when `pendingEdits.size > 0`, disarms when `=== 0` or on `clearAll`/`dispose`.
- **Sub D — Test hardening**: tightened 2 unfalsifiable tests (hmr-applied propagation seeds an intent + asserts banner text; CSS selector assertion matches the serialized `a\\:1\\:1` form).

Plus 2 cross-task fixes:
- `840e41e` — aligned a stale doc comment with Sub-issue B's rename (`staleSources` → `staleEntries`)
- `135c2a4` — memoized `useEditStagingBuffer`'s return wrapper on `version` (caught by `/review`'s adversarial pass — Sub-issue A's spread-at-return broke memoization on Panel.tsx:320/347/708 consumers)

## Pipeline review trail

8 independent passes, all green or with deferred-not-gating findings:

- **Per-task** (Step 3): spec ✅ + quality ✅ for each of A/B/C/D (Sub A needed 2 spec rounds — 3 HIGH falsifiability findings caught + fixed; B/C/D each landed in 1 round)
- **Final code reviewer** (Step 3f, Opus, fresh context): APPROVED with composed-flow trace clean
- **Compressed Steps 4-6** (architecture + simplification + security + silent-failure-hunter): 0 findings across all 3 dimensions
- **Step 7 Preflight**: tsc clean, build success, actionlint clean, pattern scan 0 new findings
- **Step 8 E2E** (Playwright): 11/11 pass in 5.3s — override-canonicalization, override-divergence-card, override-retry-window all preserved
- **Step 8.5 Test Meaningfulness Audit**: 0 HIGH, 3 MEDIUM (deferred — see below), 4 LOW
- **Step 9 Success Criteria**: 7/7 verified with citations
- **Step 10 Ship Readiness**: SHIP verdict with Performance/Security/Experience all STRONG, Maintainability ACCEPTABLE
- **Step 10.5 /review** (Claude adversarial + Codex cross-model): 1 real perf regression caught + fixed (135c2a4); 5 false positives; 2 architectural pre-existing patterns deferred
- **Final test surface**: 2729 + 33 skipped (Step 3f), 11 E2E, 193 across affected files post-`135c2a4` — all pass

## Items deferred to follow-up tickets

The following are advisory findings from Step 8.5 and /review that the pipeline reviewers identified as worth noting but not gating for this ship:

**MEDIUM (test-quality polish — not regressions)**
- `tests/browser/override.test.ts:~1700` Sub C dispose test inspects `sweepTimerId` as an implementation detail. Consider behavioral assertion via `vi.getTimerCount()` in a follow-up.
- `tests/browser/hooks/use-edit-staging-buffer.test.tsx:481-525` 4 version-increment tests differ only by mutation method (append/remove/clear). Per cortex CLAUDE.md "One test per branch, not per input" — could collapse into `it.each` (4 tests → 2).
- `tests/browser/components/staging-drift-banner.test.tsx` repeats 8-line `<StagingDriftBanner ...>` JSX across 13 tests. A `renderBanner({ intent, stale })` helper would shrink each test ~70%.

**MEDIUM (architectural — pre-existing patterns, not regressions)**
- Sub-issue B's per-(source, property, pseudo) reshape correctly fixed the internal state collapse, but the public `onStale` listener still projects to a source-set for backward compatibility. This means StagingDriftBanner's `staleOverrideCount = staleSources.size` can't distinguish "stale-property-A resolved, stale-property-B emerged on same source" from "no change" — the dismissed banner won't reopen for that within-source transition. Same observable behavior as before this PR; full fix needs a different signal (per-tuple count or generation marker on `onStale`).
- StagingDriftBanner's `dismissed` state is component-local; on remount with the same non-zero count, it resets. Pre-existing pattern. Full fix would lift `dismissed` to the parent.

**LOW (defense-in-depth advisories)**
- `cortex-app.test.tsx:1033-1054` — describe-level `afterEach` doesn't clear localStorage; new test self-clears at start AND end, but a mid-test failure between line 1138 and 1172 leaks the staged-buffer seed. Mitigated by being the last test in the file.
- `cortex-app.test.tsx:1126-1133` — inline PendingEdit literal could use `makeEdit()` factory from `tests/core/helpers.ts` to centralize shape maintenance.
- `override.ts:237-243` — pseudo-asymmetry: `remove(source, undefined, '::before')` clears `::after` stale entries too (one-direction over-clearing relative to the pseudo-aware `priorValues` cleanup). Internally consistent with its own doc comment, not a correctness bug.
- `override.test.ts:1700` — pre-dispose assertion `expect(internalBefore).not.toBeNull()` passes when field is `undefined` (rename-fragile). Tighten to `expect(typeof internalBefore).toBe('number')` for both-sides falsifiability.

**Production context**
- `SENTRY_AVAILABLE: false` for this pipeline run — no production-error baseline diff was available. Flag for incident-attribution awareness if regressions surface post-deploy.

Per the Linear ticket's acceptance criteria #2, replies must be posted to each CodeRabbit comment thread on PR #91 referencing this ticket's resolution commits:

author: jiayi-ong
body:
## Summary

  Three independent bug clusters, each preventing `scripts/run_episode.py` from
  completing a full planning episode:

  - **Hydra config double-nesting** — all 12 group config YAML files had both a
    `@package X` directive and an explicit `X:` wrapper key, double-nesting every
    field (e.g. `cfg.logging.logging.level` instead of `cfg.logging.level`).
    Removed the outer wrapper to match the already-correct pattern in
    `react_mcts.yaml` / `ppo_mcts.yaml`.

  - **`.env` never loaded** — `OPENAI_API_KEY` was set in `.env` but no entry-point
    script called `load_dotenv()`, so litellm never received the key. Added
    `load_dotenv()` to all four `scripts/*.py` entry points (before any library
    import touches `os.environ`). Also fixed the date constraint value in
    `request_template.json` from a `{"start":…,"end":…}` dict to the
    `"YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD"` string format expected by the constraint engine.

  - **Episode terminated at step 0** — three root causes in `react_agent.py`:
    1. `tool_call is None` (parse failure) was indistinguishable from `Action: DONE`,
       so the ReAct loop broke immediately after the first LLM call.
       Fixed by returning an explicit `is_done` bool from `_parse_response()` and
       adding a `_call_and_parse()` helper that retries up to `max_retries_per_action`
       times with a format reminder before recording a parse-failure error.
    2. The `action_match` regex stopped at the first `\n`, discarding multi-line
       JSON arguments that GPT-4o-mini frequently produces.
       Fixed with `Action:\s*(DONE|\w+\(.*?\))` + `re.DOTALL`.
    3. The full context (including the `[SYSTEM]` block) was sent as a single
       `role: user` message. OpenAI models follow format instructions far more
       reliably via a proper `role: system` message.
       Fixed in `_call_llm()` by splitting on `\n[USER REQUEST]`.

`context_composer.py` `_build_core_layer()` now weights skills by utility:

composite = match_score × 0.6 + utility_factor × 0.4

author: jason-vaughan
body:
## Summary

Chunk 1 of 3 for #103 — backend wiring for opt-in silent prime delivery. Replaces the `tmux.sendKeys` paste of the prime prompt with a Claude Code `SessionStart` hook that reads `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/.tangleclaw/session-prime.md` and emits it as hidden model context (no scrollback noise).

End-state for an enabled project: launched session shows an empty `>` prompt — no visible prime turn, no first-tool-call churn — while the methodology, last-session summary, active learnings, and eval-audit state are all in the AI's context.

## What

- **`data/hooks/sessionstart-prime.sh`** — 10-line bash script: cats the prime file, exits 0 silently if missing
- **`lib/engines.js`** — new `_buildBaselineHooks(projConfig, engineProfile)` + `_mergeHookObjects(a, b)`; `syncEngineHooks` now **appends** engine-baseline hooks to methodology hooks (Prawduct's existing SessionStart governance entry coexists with the prime entry)
- **`lib/sessions.js`** — new `_writePrimeFile(projectPath, primeText)`; `launchSession` derives `silentPrime` from `projConfig.silentPrime && engineProfile.capabilities.supportsSilentPrime` and skips `tmux.sendKeys(primeText)` when set
- **`data/engines/claude.json`** — `capabilities.supportsSilentPrime: true`
- **`lib/store.js`** — `DEFAULT_PROJECT_CONFIG.silentPrime: false` (opt-in until proven)

Other engines (Codex, Gemini, Aider) keep the typed-prime path. UI toggle is chunk 2; polish + final Critic is chunk 3.

## Why

Even after #101 (TC owns `.tangleclaw/project-version.txt`) and #102 (slim prime), 5–15 lines of prime + the AI's first response are still visible in the user's scrollback at every session start. SessionStart hook injection eliminates the scrollback churn entirely — Claude Code injects hook stdout silently into the model's context.

## Critic findings

0 BLOCKERs / 2 MAJORs / 4 MINORs / 4 NITs. Both MAJORs addressed in-chunk:

- **M1** — `_buildBaselineHooks` was reading `projConfig.silentPrime` only, ignoring the engine capability — would have written an orphan SessionStart hook for engines that can't use it. Now takes `engineProfile` and gates on both flags symmetrically with `launchSession`.
- **M2** — Existing `syncEngineHooks` describe block in `test/engines.test.js` shared a single `projectDir` across all 7 tests via `before/after`. Flipped to `beforeEach/afterEach` for full per-test isolation now that baseline-hooks merging makes shared state load-bearing.

The 4 MINORs and 4 NITs are deferred to chunk 3 (CHANGELOG bullet split, hook-script `set -u`, prime-file cleanup on silent→typed transition, comment polish, profile-validator allow-list — already confirmed safe).

## Test plan

- [x] `node --test 'test/*.test.js'` — 1656 passing, was 1627 (29 new tests)
- [x] `_buildBaselineHooks` returns `{}` when capability gate fails (silentPrime=true but engine missing supportsSilentPrime)
- [x] `_mergeHookObjects` concatenates entries under same eventName, methodology first then baseline, deep-cloned
- [x] `syncEngineHooks` produces both methodology + baseline `SessionStart` entries on disk when Prawduct + silentPrime
- [x] `_writePrimeFile` round-trip; missing-dir create; non-throwing failure path
- [x] `launchSession` writes prime file when both gates pass; skips when either fails
- [x] Hook script: cats prime when present; exit 0 silently when prime file missing or `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` unset; byte-exact multi-line preservation
- [ ] **Manual smoke (deferred to chunk 3):** flip a project's `silentPrime: true`, launch a Claude Code session, verify empty `>` prompt with full context (methodology question lands correctly)

Refs #103

author: copilot
body:
Store purchases only checked and deducted from a single coin pool, so a player with e.g. 200 Transferable Coins + 100 regular Coins could not buy a 300-coin offer even though they had sufficient total balance.

## Changes

- **`canPayForOffer`** — when `coinType == Transferable`, check the combined total of both coin pools instead of only transferable:
  ```lua
  -- Before
  return self:canRemoveTransferableCoins(coinsToRemove)
  -- After
  return (self:getTransferableCoins() + self:getTibiaCoins()) >= coinsToRemove
  ```

- **`makeCoinTransaction`** — when `coinType == Transferable`, exhaust transferable coins first then draw the remainder from regular coins:
  ```lua
  local transferableToUse = math.min(transferableCoins, price)
  local regularToUse = price - transferableToUse
  if transferableToUse > 0 then self:removeTransferableCoins(transferableToUse) end
  if regularToUse > 0 then self:removeTibiaCoins(regularToUse) end
  ```

## Unaffected paths

- Coin transfers (`parseTransferableCoins`) — still enforces transferable-only balance, intentional.
- `CoinType.Coin` offers — still deduct exclusively from regular coins.

author: dengzhaofun
body:
## 背景

`pnpm run deploy` 在 server 上构建失败：

```
✘ [ERROR] Could not resolve "@better-auth/core/utils/async"
   ../../node_modules/.pnpm/@better-auth+api-key@1.6.9_.../@better-auth/api-key/dist/index.mjs:13:30
```

## 根因（双因素）

1. `apps/server/package.json` 把 `@better-auth/core` 钉死在 `1.6.2`，但 `@better-auth/api-key` 的 caret 范围 `^1.6.2` 实际解析到 `1.6.9`。1.6.9 plugin 引用了 `@better-auth/core/utils/async`（1.6.9 才有的 export），1.6.2 的 dist 里压根没这个文件。
2. `apps/server/wrangler.jsonc` 早就为 `@better-auth/core/utils/*`（wildcard export，esbuild 不解）显式 alias 过 `id` / `json` / `ip` / `error-codes` 这几个子路径，但新增的 `async` 没补上。

升完 core 之后还撞到第二层坑：`@better-auth/cli@1.4.21`（dev dep，发布节奏跟主包脱节）通过 `better-auth@1.4.21` 的 transitive 把 `better-call@1.1.8` + `@better-auth/utils@0.3.0` 拽进 server 的 peer 上下文，导致升级后的 `core@1.6.9` 在 `dist/api/index.mjs` 找不到 `kAPIErrorHeaderSymbol`（这个 symbol 是 `better-call@1.3.5+` 才有的）。用根 `pnpm.overrides` 把链路钉死。

## 改动

**修 build 错误**
- `apps/server/package.json`: `@better-auth/core` `1.6.2` → `^1.6.9`、`@better-auth/api-key` `^1.6.2` → `^1.6.9`、`better-auth` `^1.6.2` → `^1.6.9`
- `apps/server/wrangler.jsonc`: alias 表补一条 `@better-auth/core/utils/async`
- `package.json` 根：加 `pnpm.overrides`，固定 `@better-auth/utils: 0.4.0` + `better-call: 1.3.5`

**顺手做的 patch/minor 升级**
- server: `ai` ^6.0.172、`zod` ^4.4.1
- admin: better-auth 系列同步到 1.6.9；`@tanstack/*` 全套从 `latest` tag 解到具体 caret 范围（react-router 到 1.169.1，消掉 router-plugin 的 peer 警告）；`@ai-sdk/react`、`@c15t/react`、`@cloudflare/vite-plugin`、`@inlang/paraglide-js`、`@openrouter/ai-sdk-provider`、`@rive-app/react-webgl2`、`@sentry/cloudflare`、`@sentry/react`、`ai`、`nanoid`、`recharts`、`shadcn`、`use-stick-to-bottom`、`zod` 等

**未升（major，留给单独 PR）**
TypeScript 5→6、ESLint 9→10、Vite 7→8、Vitest（admin）3→4、`@types/node` 22→25、`@vitejs/plugin-react` 5→6、`@sentry/vite-plugin` 4→5、`@sentry/cli` 2→3、`marked` 15→18、`lucide-react` 0→1、`jsdom` 28→29、`vite-tsconfig-paths` 5→6 —— 都有 breaking change，不在本 PR 范围内。

## 验证

- `pnpm --filter=server exec wrangler deploy --minify --dry-run`：通过（3475 KiB / gzip 854 KiB）
- `pnpm --filter=admin build`：通过
- `pnpm --filter=server check-types`：通过
- `pnpm --filter=server test`：88 files / **1187 tests 全过**
- `pnpm --filter=server lint` / `pnpm --filter=admin lint`：通过
- `pnpm install`：无 peer warning
- `pnpm-lock.yaml` 净减 950 行（多余的 `better-auth/utils@0.3.x`、`better-call@1.1.8` 链路被 override 移除）

## Reviewer notes

- `pnpm.overrides` 是全局生效的。`@better-auth/cli@1.4.21` 自身依赖期望 `@better-auth/utils@0.3.0`，被 override 抬到 `0.4.0`。cli 只在跑 `pnpm --filter=server auth:generate` 时用，不进 worker bundle；如果以后跑这个 codegen 报错，可以临时 unpin override 或用 `npx @better-auth/cli@x.y.z` 跑一次性命令。
- `@better-auth/core` 现在写成 `^1.6.9`（不再钉死 patch），跟 `better-auth` / `@better-auth/api-key` 的 caret 一致，避免再次出现 plugin 抢跑、core 落后的版本错位。
- `wrangler.jsonc` 里 `@better-auth/core/utils/*` 这套 alias 是为了绕过 esbuild 不支持 wildcard exports 的问题；将来 better-auth 再开新的 `utils/<name>` 子路径还得手工补一条。

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter=server exec wrangler deploy --dry-run`
- [x] `pnpm --filter=admin build`
- [x] `pnpm --filter=server test`（1187 用例）
- [x] `pnpm --filter=server check-types` / `pnpm --filter=admin check-types`
- [x] `pnpm --filter=server lint` / `pnpm --filter=admin lint`
- [ ] 实际部署到 Cloudflare Workers（合并后由 CF Workers Builds 触发）

author: railway-app[bot]
body:
## Problem

On Railway, the app is deployed with rootDirectory set to apps/api, so the container only contains that subdirectory at /app/. The resolved path of config.py is /app/app/core/config.py, which only has parents at indices 0–3. Accessing parents[4] raises an IndexError on startup, preventing the app from ever serving the /health endpoint.

## Solution

Replaced the hard-coded parents[4] with min(4, len(_parents) - 1) so the index is clamped to the deepest available ancestor. Locally the behaviour is unchanged (deep path still resolves to parents[4]). On Railway the index safely falls back to the filesystem root, and since Railway injects env vars directly, pydantic-settings simply skips the missing .env file and reads from the environment as intended.

### Changes
- **Modified** `apps/api/app/core/config.py`

### Context
- **Deployment**: [#09be52](https://railway.com/project/ed48ef39-095c-4583-8481-d8c8a0d9cb72/environment/b18f30bb-7209-4271-86b4-9760909d3df0/deployment/09be52e3-aa39-4123-849c-0b66dd4e575d)

body:
## Summary

Remove the IndexedDB workflow provider's runtime fallback for runs whose `next_signal_sequence` is missing or non-positive.

The production data in `gitlab-peach-street` / `terra-east4` was manually backfilled before this change:

- `runs` checked: 1069
- runs needing repair: 61
- rows updated: 61
- remaining missing/non-positive `next_signal_sequence`: 0

## Interface / Contract

No public RPC or manifest interface changes.

Storage contract before:

```diff
- if run.next_signal_sequence <= 0:
-   sequence = 1
-   run.next_signal_sequence = 2
```

Storage contract after:

```diff
+ if run.next_signal_sequence <= 0:
+   return FailedPrecondition("workflow run has invalid next_signal_sequence")
+ sequence = run.next_signal_sequence
+ run.next_signal_sequence += 1
```

Example canonical run state:

```json
{
  "id": "run_123",
  "next_signal_sequence": 1
}
```

Example invalid state now rejected:

```json
{
  "id": "run_legacy_or_corrupt",
  "next_signal_sequence": 0
}
```

## Tests

- `go test ./... -count=1` in `workflow/indexeddb`

Note: local test setup used a detached latest `gestalt` main worktree at `/Users/hugh/src/.codex-worktrees/gestalt` so the module's existing `replace github.com/valon-technologies/gestalt/sdk/go => ../../../gestalt/sdk/go` resolves to the current SDK.

body:
When a student gets a low Rend the save flow opens an "EVALUACIÓN DIAGNÓSTICA INTERDISCIPLINARIA" dialog. The dismiss button lives in the master page (Cerrar más tarde / BTNCERRARMASTARDE_MPAGE) and offsetParent returns null for fixed-position MPAGE elements so the previous detector missed it.

Improvements:
- isVisible(el) replaces the offsetParent check, using bounding rect plus computed display/visibility/opacity. Catches MPAGE buttons and any fixed-position dialog.
- popupVisible() falls back to scanning every element with id matching POPUP|Popup|DIAG|Diag|MODAL|Modal so we pick up custom containers.
- findPopupConfirmButton() now also includes dismiss IDs (BTNCERRARMASTARDE_MPAGE, BTNCERRARPOPUPDIAG, BTNCERRARPOPUP, BTNSALIR_MPAGE, BTNVOLVER, BTNREGRESAR) and accepts dismiss-style text (Cerrar / Más tarde / Saltar / Omitir / Salir / Volver / Cancelar) as a secondary fallback after the affirmative patterns.
- When no button can be found we dump the popup outerHTML to the DevTools console so unknown popups can be diagnosed.

Bump manifest to 0.9.0.

author: leondavi
body:
## v0.2.8 — Pluto coordination, three ways

This release adds **PlutoMCPFriend**, a brand-new MCP-server adapter that lets Claude Code call Pluto operations as native tool calls (no curl, no copy-pasted tokens), plus a **deterministic injection format** for PlutoAgentFriend so agents that parse the wire format can do so unambiguously.

### Highlights

- **New: `PlutoMCPFriend.sh`** — MCP-server adapter for Claude Code with a guided setup wizard, dynamically discovered slash commands, and event-driven inbox delivery. Registers with Pluto on startup, holds the session token transparently, and auto-renews held locks at TTL/2 in the background.
- **New: deterministic `<S<PLUTO seq=N>>{json}<E<PLUTO seq=N>>` injection format** for PlutoAgentFriend, opt-in via `--inject-format=deterministic`. The natural-language path remains the default — fully backwards compatible.
- **17 MCP tools, 14 slash prompts, 4 resources** auto-registered for any Pluto operation Claude Code might want.
- **Three-mode inbox delivery**: tool-result piggyback (`_pluto_inbox` field on every Pluto tool response), explicit drain (`pluto_recv`), and event-driven long-poll (`pluto_wait_for_messages` with `asyncio.Event` — sub-second fanout from broadcast to delivery).
- **Tests: 55 → 85**, all green. Plus an in-process MCP-client integration smoke test for the adapter.

### PlutoAgentFriend — deterministic injection format

```
<S<PLUTO seq=42>>
{"event":"task_assigned","from":"orchestrator","seq_token":42,...}
<E<PLUTO seq=42>>
```

- New `--inject-format=natural|deterministic` CLI flag (default: `natural`, so existing roles keep working).
- One frame per non-noise message that has a `seq_token`; markers carry the same `seq` (= `seq_token` from `/agents/peek`).
- Parser regex tolerates the PTY's whitespace-flattening behaviour: `<S<PLUTO seq=(\d+)>>\s*(\{.*?\})\s*<E<PLUTO seq=\1>>`.
- Spec lives in [`library/protocol.md` §7](library/protocol.md); agent-facing usage in [`agent_friend_guide.md`](agent_friend_guide.md).
- Wrapper still owns ack on echo confirmation; agents *may* ack early/idempotently themselves.

### PlutoMCPFriend — Pluto over MCP for Claude Code

#### What's exposed

**17 tools** (each is a thin wrapper around a `PlutoHttpClient` method; the adapter injects the session token transparently):

| Group | Tools |
|---|---|
| Messaging | `pluto_send`, `pluto_broadcast`, `pluto_recv`, `pluto_wait_for_messages`, `pluto_publish`, `pluto_subscribe` |
| Discovery | `pluto_list_agents`, `pluto_find_agents`, `pluto_set_status` |
| Locks | `pluto_lock_acquire` (auto-renews at TTL/2), `pluto_lock_release`, `pluto_lock_renew`, `pluto_lock_info`, `pluto_list_locks` |
| Tasks | `pluto_task_assign`, `pluto_task_update`, `pluto_task_list` |

**14 slash commands** (auto-discovered by Claude Code):

| Group | Slash commands |
|---|---|
| Quick actions | `/pluto-check`, `/pluto-watch`, `/pluto-status` |
| Roles | `/pluto-role-{specialist, orchestrator, reviewer, qa, deployer, evaluator, experiment-runner, data-steward, ssh-bridge}` |
| Reference | `/pluto-protocol`, `/pluto-guide` |

**4 resources** (`@`-mention from inside the agent for an on-demand snapshot): `pluto://inbox`, `pluto://locks`, `pluto://agents`, `pluto://server`.

#### Inbox delivery — three paths working in parallel

1. **Piggyback**: every Pluto tool result is augmented with a `_pluto_inbox` field if there are pending messages — the agent picks them up as a free side-effect of any Pluto-related work.
2. **Pull**: `pluto_recv` drains and acks on demand; `/pluto-check` is the slash-command equivalent.
3. **Watch**: `pluto_wait_for_messages(timeout_s)` blocks on an `asyncio.Event` set by the peek loop. The role connection block teaches Claude to spawn this as a background `Task` with `run_in_background=true` — the main conversation stays interactive while a sub-agent watches; on Task completion the messages appear in the parent's next turn. `/pluto-watch` is the one-keystroke launcher.

#### Lock auto-renewal

`pluto_lock_acquire(resource, mode, ttl_ms, auto_renew=True)` registers the granted lock with a background renewer that calls `/locks/renew` at TTL/2 until release or session shutdown. Removes the "remember to renew" burden entirely. Opt out with `auto_renew=False`.

#### Guided setup wizard

Run with no arguments for the interactive wizard:

```bash
./PlutoMCPFriend.sh
```

Walks through 4 steps: server check (offers to start it if down), agent ID, Claude Code presence check, summary + confirm. After launch, prints a "Skills API" banner listing every slash command, resource, and tool the user has access to inside Claude — dynamically built from `library/roles/`, so adding a new role file shows up automatically.

Expert mode skips the wizard:

```bash
./PlutoMCPFriend.sh --agent-id coder-1 --role specialist --wait-timeout-s 600
```

#### Configurable watcher cycle (`--wait-timeout-s`)

A single launcher flag controls how long `pluto_wait_for_messages` blocks. It propagates everywhere consistently:
- Embedded into the role connection block's recommended `pluto_wait_for_messages(N)` call
- Embedded into the `/pluto-watch` slash prompt body
- Set as the tool's argument default and shown in its description

Default 300s. Validated as a positive integer; bad input fails fast before the venv bootstrap.

#### Claude Code only

`PlutoMCPFriend` relies on Claude's `--mcp-config` and `--append-system-prompt` for the role auto-injection path. Cursor, Aider, and Copilot don't have stable equivalents, so the launcher is honest about its scope: **Claude Code only**. For other agents, the README and `docs/guide/index.md` direct users to `PlutoAgentFriend.sh`, which works universally via PTY injection.

`--framework` was removed; passing it now prints a clear deprecation message pointing to `PlutoAgentFriend.sh`.

### Files & dependencies

- **New package**: `src_py/agent_mcp_friend/` (`server.py`, `tools.py`, `prompts.py`, `resources.py`, `inbox.py`, `lock_manager.py`, `pluto_mcp_friend.py`).
- **New launcher**: `PlutoMCPFriend.sh`.
- **New tests**: `tests/test_mcp_friend.py` (30 new tests covering noise filtering, piggyback semantics, lock manager scheduling, prompt assembly, capability registration, custom timeouts, and the watcher event flow).
- **New runtime dep**: `mcp>=1.27,<2` (the official Anthropic Python MCP SDK), pinned in `requirements.txt`. Auto-installed into `/tmp/pluto/.venv` by the launcher on first run — no system Python pollution; sidesteps PEP 668.
- **New user docs**: `docs/guide/pluto-mcp-friend.md`. README and `docs/guide/index.md` updated to surface the new entry point.
- **Per-user `.mcp.json`** is gitignored.

### Bug fixes along the way

- macOS bash 3.2 fix: `set -u` + empty-array `"${arr[@]}"` raised "unbound variable" and aborted the launcher between writing `.mcp.json` and `exec claude`. Fixed at all three call sites with the bash-3.2-safe length-check idiom.
- ANSI colour vars in launcher heredocs are now real escape bytes (defined via `printf '\033...'` so `cat <<EOF` substitution produces sequences the terminal interprets, not literal `\033[...]` text).

### Verification

- `python3 -m unittest tests.test_agent_friend tests.test_mcp_friend` → **85 tests, all green** (1 integration test skipped — needs live Pluto server).
- Wizard end-to-end driven via `expect`: section headers render correctly; `.mcp.json` is generated with the right port (9201) and `--wait-timeout-s` flag; no bash-3.2 unbound-variable regression at the launch transition.
- Smoke-tested `--no-launch` config-only mode and `--framework` deprecation message.

### Version markers

`v0.2.7` → `v0.2.8` in `VERSION.md`, `src_erl/include/pluto.hrl`, `src_erl/src/pluto.app.src`, `src_erl/rebar.config`, and the `library/protocol.md` header.

### Motivation

- Provide a safe one-time endpoint to create or upgrade a superadmin account so an operator can log in to the super-admin dashboard without modifying the DB manually. 
- Ensure the account matches the authentication flow which requires `role = 'super_admin'` and an active `status` to be routed to the super-admin dashboard.

author: ryanklee
body:
## Summary

Codex shipped a synchronous-RPC + observability stack for its `cx-*` lanes that Claude Code's greek-named lanes (`alpha`/`beta`/`delta`/`epsilon`) had no analogue for. This PR ports the four load-bearing pieces onto the Claude side so the operator can coordinate either interface with one set of idioms.

The motivation is concrete: Claude→Claude coordination today happens through filesystem polling at the 270 s `ScheduleWakeup` cadence, which leaks up to ~5 minutes between writing an inflection and a peer reading it. For load-bearing directives (wind-down, urgent claim, conflict resolution) that latency is not acceptable — Codex solved this with `hapax-codex-send --require-ack`, and Claude needed the same.

## What lands

| Script | Counterpart | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `scripts/hapax-claude-send` | `hapax-codex-send` | tmux paste-and-submit + token ACK file + busy-pane refusal + auto-nudge; foot fallback via wtype/hyprctl |
| `scripts/hapax-claude-smoke-send` | `hapax-codex-smoke-send` | bash-backed throwaway tmux session, verifies stale-prompt clear + ACK delivery |
| `scripts/hapax-claude-health` | `hapax-codex-health` | per-lane tmux/foot presence + claim↔relay-yaml consistency + 8-warning taxonomy + Obsidian dashboard render to `_dashboard/claude-session-health.md` |
| `scripts/hapax-claude` | `hapax-codex` (lighter) | lane launcher: identity envvars, worktree resolution, optional tmux/foot detach so send/health have a target to find |

`CLAUDE.md` gets a "Claude Code multi-session control plane" section paralleling the existing codex-side note.

## Design choices worth noting

- **Names and tunables are deliberately parallel** (`HAPAX_CLAUDE_SEND_*` env vars, identical flag set: `--require-ack`/`--ack-timeout`/`--json`/`--stdin`/`--transport auto|foot|tmux`). One set of idioms across both interfaces.
- **Busy-pane regex is env-tunable.** Claude Code's animated activity verbs ("Working...", "Pondering...", etc.) drift across releases, so the default `HAPAX_CLAUDE_SEND_BUSY_REGEX` is broad and overrideable rather than hard-coded.
- **Strict role allowlist by default** (`alpha beta delta epsilon`) with `HAPAX_CLAUDE_SEND_ROLE_ALLOWLIST` env override so the smoke test can use a throwaway role without weakening the production guardrail.
- **Launcher is intentionally smaller than `hapax-codex`** — Claude Code reads its own `~/.claude/settings.json` and `.claude.json`, so we don't need to baton-pass MCP server config the way the codex launcher does. The launcher's three jobs are: identity envvars, worktree resolution, control-plane visibility.
- **Shared `session-protection.md` registry**: greek lanes can be listed there as bare backticked names (e.g. `` `alpha` ``) for the same operator-override semantics codex lanes use.

## Test plan

- [x] `bash -n` syntax-check on all three shell scripts
- [x] `python3 -c "ast.parse(open('scripts/hapax-claude-health').read())"` — pyparses cleanly
- [x] `scripts/hapax-claude-smoke-send` — passes locally; ACK delivered to tmp, stale prompt cleared, transcript captured (`/run/user/1000/hapax-claude-smoke/claude-smoke.transcript`)
- [x] `scripts/hapax-claude-health` — JSON output validates as JSON, Obsidian render produces a well-formed markdown table with frontmatter
- [x] `scripts/hapax-claude --help` and `--role $ROLE --terminal none` paths exit cleanly without claude in PATH
- [ ] Live end-to-end with a real spawned Claude lane (will exercise as part of the post-merge ramp-up)

## Out of scope (deliberate)

- No new hooks. `relay-coordination-check.sh` and friends already work for Claude lanes.
- No CC-task auto-claim integration in the launcher (Codex's launcher does this; for Claude, `cc-claim` is invoked from inside the running session per the existing protocol).
- No bootstrap-MD injection. Claude already loads `MEMORY.md` + `CLAUDE.md` automatically; the operator dossier is loaded via the auto-memory index.

body:
## Summary

End-to-end fix for the freeradius restart-loop blocker that surfaced on the 2026-04-30 deployment. After PRs #30-#33 fixed the upstream data-plane bugs, the daemon still wouldn't start. Comprehensive audit (DDD/SDD lens) found 3 architectural gaps, all fixed here.

## Three gaps + their fixes

### Gap 1 — Templates exist but the manager doesn't use them
\`site_default.j2\`, \`site_inner_tunnel.j2\` and \`python.j2\` are real Jinja2 templates with proper structure. The manager bypassed them and hand-built the same configs via raw string concatenation in 165 lines of brittle code (\`generate_site_default()\` was 148 lines).

**Fix:** Switched to template rendering. Net -315 lines in config_manager.py.

### Gap 2 — No conditional module references
The hand-built \`site_default\` always emitted \`eap\` and \`orw\` module references regardless of whether those modules were actually generated. With no active server cert, the EAP module is skipped but the site still references it → radiusd fails to parse the site → restart loop.

**Fix:**
- Added \`has_eap\` / \`has_python\` / \`ldap_modules\` / \`realms_enabled\` flags to both site templates.
- The manager computes them from capability detection (\`bool(eap_content)\`, etc.) and passes them in.
- Sites now emit module refs only when those modules are loaded.
- \`inner-tunnel\` is skipped entirely when \`has_eap\` is false (it's meaningless without EAP).

### Gap 3 — rlm_python vs rlm_python3
\`python.j2\` declared \`python orw {\` (Python 2 directive). \`rlm_orw.py\` is Python 3. The Dockerfile installed \`python3-pip\` but not the \`freeradius-python3\` apt package, so rlm_python3 wasn't available either.

**Fix:**
- Changed template to \`python3 orw {\` + corrected python_path quoting.
- Added \`freeradius-python3\` to Dockerfile apt install.
- Added build-time sanity check: \`radiusd -v | grep rlm_python3\` fails the build if rlm_python3 is missing.

## Bonus fixes (caught during audit)

- entrypoint: \`cp\` → \`ln -sf\` for \`proxy.conf\` and \`clients.conf\` so watcher runtime updates take effect on HUP without container restart (was open as #34, now folded in here).
- entrypoint: \`chmod 600\` was globbing \`/certs/server/*.key\` but the manager writes to \`/certs/server.key\` (no subdir) — silent failure on every restart. Fixed to explicit file paths.
- entrypoint: removed unused \`mkdir\`s for \`/certs/{ca,server,crl}\` subdirs that the manager doesn't write to.
- entrypoint: removed the redundant \`ln -sf .../mods-available/python\` line — the for-loop a few lines below handles it via the watcher's generated python config.

## Test plan

- [x] \`python3 -c "import freeradius_config_manager"\` — clean
- [x] \`bash -n freeradius_entrypoint.sh\` — syntax OK
- [x] git diff shows expected scope (6 files, -315 lines net)
- [ ] CI green
- [ ] **Manual on 192.168.0.250 after merge** (this is the critical one):
  \`\`\`bash
  cd /opt/openradiusweb
  # Restore the canonical entrypoint (overwrites all the in-flight sed hacks)
  git checkout -- services/auth/freeradius_entrypoint.sh
  git pull --ff-only
  docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml --env-file .env.production build --no-cache freeradius freeradius_config_watcher
  docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml --env-file .env.production up -d freeradius freeradius_config_watcher
  sleep 30
  docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml ps | grep freeradius
  # Expect: STATUS = Up (X seconds), no Restarting
  docker logs orw-freeradius --tail=20
  # Expect: "Ready to process requests"
  \`\`\`
- [ ] Fortigate Test Connectivity goes from "Can't contact" to "Authentication failed" (= server reachable, just no user backend yet)

## Closes / Replaces

- Closes #34 (cp → ln -sf, folded in)
- Resolves the freeradius restart loop documented in session-2026-04-30-deployment.md Round 10+

## Audit methodology

DDD/SDD-style cross-reference audit by Explore subagent over:
- All \`.get(\` / SQL column references in config_manager vs actual schema (init.sql, 002.sql)
- File path contracts: where manager writes vs where freeradius reads vs entrypoint bridge
- Module-availability contracts: what config references vs what's installed in Dockerfile
- Site→module dependency graph

Report (~500 lines) walks through each bug with file:line + severity + suggested fix. Will be appended to session log post-merge.

author: easierbycode
body:
Cordova-android emits <activity android:name="MainActivity"> (relative).
Android resolves that against the manifest's package attribute at launch
time. The on-device patcher rewrites the package attribute to the new
forged app id, but the DEX classes stay in the placeholder package — so
the relative form would resolve to <new-pkg>.MainActivity, which doesn't
exist, and every forged APK crashed immediately on open with
ClassNotFoundException.

Patch the manifest after `cordova prepare` to use the fully-qualified
placeholder class name. AAPT2 then emits it verbatim into the binary
AXML, the on-device patcher leaves the activity name untouched, and the
launcher always finds the real DEX class.

Strengthen verification accordingly: the JS placeholder verifier now
fails when the FQCN is missing from AndroidManifest.xml, and the CI
self-test greps the aapt2-decoded manifest for it.

## Change

**`api/stripe-webhook.js`** — add `status: sbExtRow.status` to `updatedBooking`:

```js
const updatedBooking = {
  bookingId:  sbExtRow.booking_ref,
  vehicleId:  sbExtRow.vehicle_id || vehicle_id,
  status:     sbExtRow.status,   // ← preserve active_rental through upsert

};
```

`sbExtRow.status` is already validated to be `active_rental | active | reserved` before this object is built, so no additional guard is needed. `autoUpsertBooking` resolves it through `BOOKING_STATUS_MAP` → `"active_rental"`, and `extendBlockedDateForBooking` continues to run against the correct `bookingRef` and new `returnDate`/`returnTime` downstream.

body:
The admin dashboard had a flat, generic look — plain white cards, minimal typography hierarchy, and no visual identity befitting a commercial ERP product. This PR replaces the entire visual layer (`admin-dashboard.component.html` + `.scss`) with a professional, animated design while keeping all data bindings and component logic untouched.

## Hero Header
- Replaced plain white card with a full-bleed **indigo→violet gradient banner** (`#4338CA` → `#7C3AED`)
- Animated floating blob shapes (CSS `@keyframes blobFloat`) add depth without JS
- Eyebrow rewritten to *"Tableau de Bord Opérationnel"* inside a frosted-glass pill
- Title restructured as `SmartERP · Dashboard` at 36 px / 800 weight
- Meta badges (date, live indicator) use `@supports (backdrop-filter)` with opaque fallback for Firefox

## KPI Cards
- **4 px colored top border** per variant (indigo / amber / emerald) replaces the previous uniform 3 px bar
- **52 px gradient icon box** with a decorative oversized background circle
- Added **trend badge** per card (e.g. "Actifs ↗", "Référencés")
- Counter values bumped to 48 px / 800 weight in brand color; `countUp` keyframe drives entry animation

## Quick Actions
- Each action now has a **two-line label + hint** instead of a single label
- Per-color hover state applies background tint + border glow matching the card's accent
- Chevron replaces arrow-right; translates in from left only on hover

## Data Tables & Section Cards
- Cards rounded to 24 px (`$radius-xl`) with heavier shadow on hover
- Table `<thead>` uses an indigo-50 gradient; header border bumped to 2 px indigo-100
- `ref-id` cells are now pill-shaped; status/stock badges have stronger uppercase letter-spacing
- Avatar initials use per-color gradient backgrounds

## Animation system

| Class | Keyframe | Applied to |
|---|---|---|
| `slide-down` | `translateY(-16→0)` | Header |
| `slide-up` | `translateY(20→0)` | All sections (staggered delay) |
| `blobFloat` | translate + scale loop | Decorative shapes |
| `livePulse` | expanding ring | Live activity dot |
| `countUp` | `translateY(8→0)` | KPI values |

## Dark mode
Full `:host-context(.dark)` block updated to match new class names; gradient cards use a deep navy base (`#141B2D`) with indigo-tinted accents.

author: dobesv
body:
Per the CommonMark spec a fenced code block opener may be preceded by 0–3 spaces of indentation; four or more spaces means the line is NOT a fence.  Previously `detect_code_block` called `trim_start()` which stripped all leading whitespace, so indented triple-backtick lines inside bash command output (e.g. Python code with 4-space indent) were incorrectly toggling the code-block state and causing subsequent lines to be rendered as highlighted code instead of plain text.

Fixes #403

Add regression tests:
- `test_detect_code_block`: asserts 0–3 spaces detected, 4+ spaces not
- `indented_backticks_not_treated_as_code_fence`: full render round-trip

author: shadyapoelela-cloud
body:
== The trap ==

apex_finance/lib/core/api_config.dart:12 sets:
  defaultValue: 'https://apex-api-ootk.onrender.com'

That default is INTENTIONAL — production CI's `flutter build web` step bakes the production URL in. So local dev MUST override at run time:
  flutter run -d chrome --web-port 57305 \
    --dart-define=API_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:8000

The existing README Quick Start ended at `flutter run -d chrome` with no override hint. Result: fresh clones silently call live production, "Failed to fetch" appears on the first user action, and the engineer has no useful pointer to the cause. Discovered while live-testing the G-S2 auth-guard fix in a previous Sprint 8 Phase 2 session.

== The fix ==

Pure additions — no source-code changes (api_config.dart unchanged).

1. scripts/dev/ — 4 wrapper scripts:
   - run-backend.{ps1,sh}: port-8000 detection with consent prompt, then `py -m uvicorn app.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --reload`. Path resolution from $PSScriptRoot / $(dirname "$0") so they work from any clone path.
   - run-frontend.{ps1,sh}: cd apex_finance, `flutter run -d chrome --web-port 57305 --dart-define=API_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:8000`. Both wrappers print the underlying command before running it — read once, learn the shape, drop the wrapper if you prefer.

2. LOCAL_DEV_RUNBOOK.md (root, ~200 lines):
   - Architecture text-diagram (Browser:57305 → Flutter → uvicorn:8000).
   - One-shot quick-start (Win + Mac/Linux).
   - Test-user creation via POST /auth/register (shady2 / Aa@123456).
   - Troubleshooting matrix: Failed to fetch, port-in-use, ModuleNotFoundError, 127.0.0.1 vs localhost (with the actual reason — uvicorn binds IPv4-only on 127.0.0.1, while `localhost` on Win11/recent macOS resolves to ::1 IPv6 first → silent connect failure surfaced as "Failed to fetch"), pandas-on-Python-3.14.
   - § "What the scripts do NOT do" to keep scope honest (no migrations, no seed data, no HTTPS, no version pinning).

3. CLAUDE.md — new § "Local Development" between Testing and Common Pitfalls (5 lines, points to runbook + scripts).

4. README.md — 6-line callout after Frontend Setup. The plain `flutter run -d chrome` in Quick Start is preserved (it's still correct shape) but now warns that it talks to PRODUCTION without the dart-define flag, with a redirect to the runbook.

5. APEX_BLUEPRINT/09 § 11 — full G-DEV-1 entry (description, evidence, scope, blast radius, verification, rollback) marked ✅ DONE.

6. PROGRESS.md — Sprint 8 closure entry.

== Verification ==

- run-backend.ps1 live test: spawned uvicorn (PID 22860, python), 168 tables loaded, GET /health → HTTP 200 (318 bytes), clean Stop-Process shutdown.
- run-frontend.ps1 PowerShell AST parse: no errors.
- bash -n run-backend.sh run-frontend.sh: no errors.
- flutter analyze (auth_guard.dart, router.dart, v5_routes.dart, auth_guard_test.dart): No issues found.
- 306 pre-existing flutter-analyze warnings unchanged (zero new ones introduced).

== Out of scope ==

- TESTING_GUIDE_AR.md and app/pilot/README_PILOT.md still use `localhost` and miss --dart-define. Updating those is scope creep for this gap; opens later as a sub-issue if needed. The README and CLAUDE.md redirects catch ~90% of first-time users.

Closes G-DEV-1.
Refs: APEX_BLUEPRINT/09 § 11 G-DEV-1, G-S2 (the session that surfaced this)

The tournament feature had multiple broken or non-functional flows: team registration was creating floating teams with no category/pool link, invitation emails pointed to a non-existent route, self-unregistration was blocked by the wrong guard, and several admin/player UI actions had no backend plumbing or were completely missing.

## Backend

- **#2 Invite URL**: `sendTeamInvitation` now emits `…/tournaments/invite/:token` (was `…/teams/:teamId/invitations/:token/accept`, which matched no route)
- **#3 Self-unregister guard**: Replaced `validateRegistrationEligibility` (designed for joining) with a direct status check — captains can now unregister during any `draft`/`registration` phase regardless of date window

author: daedalus-icarus
body:
## Summary

Closes #922.

Cached OSS fallback UIDs were skipped entirely during DB storage, even when mirror issue discovery later refreshed their top-level issue-discovery fields in the same forward pass.

This change separates cached PR/file payload skipping from aggregate evaluation-row persistence:

- mirror issue discovery now returns UIDs whose issue fetch completed successfully
- successful empty/no-relevant issue responses clear stale issue-discovery fields
- cached UIDs with refreshed issue discovery are written through an evaluation-row-only storage path
- cached PR, issue, and file-change payloads remain skipped

## Why

A GitHub PR-fetch failure can restore a cached evaluation and mark the UID as cached. Mirror issue discovery can still succeed afterward and mutate fields such as:

- `issue_discovery_score`
- `issue_token_score`
- `issue_credibility`
- `is_issue_eligible`
- `total_solved_issues`
- `total_valid_solved_issues`
- `total_closed_issues`
- `total_open_issues`

Before this fix, `bulk_store_evaluation(..., skip_uids=cached_uids)` skipped the whole UID, so emissions could use fresh in-memory issue-discovery values while the DB/dashboard kept stale values.

## Fix

- Thread issue-discovery refreshed UIDs through `forward()`.
- Compute cached UIDs that need only an aggregate evaluation-row refresh.
- Add `DatabaseStorage.store_miner_evaluation()` to persist miner identity + `miner_evaluations` row without re-storing cached PR/file data.
- Extend `bulk_store_evaluation()` with `evaluation_only_uids`.

## Testing

- `uv run pytest tests/ -q`
- `uv run ruff check .`
- `uv run ruff format --check .`
- `uv run pyright`
- `uv run pre-commit run --files gittensor/validator/forward.py gittensor/validator/issue_discovery/mirror_scan.py gittensor/validator/utils/storage.py neurons/validator.py tests/validator/issue_discovery/test_mirror_scan.py tests/validator/test_cached_issue_discovery_storage.py`

author: sam-goodwin
body:
## Summary

Hotfix for a regression introduced by #131. The state-store worker now boots successfully end-to-end.

## What broke

In #131 I added a top-level IIFE in `Cloudflare/StateStore/Api.ts` that resolves the file's own on-disk path so the alchemy CLI's worker bundler can use it as the entry point — fixing the \`[MISSING_EXPORT] \"default\" is not exported by \"bin/alchemy.js\"\` failure when the CLI runs from its bundled \`bin/alchemy.js\`.

The catch I missed: `Api.ts` is also evaluated by the Cloudflare Workers runtime once the bundle is deployed. In that environment `import.meta.url` is undefined, so `fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)` throws on worker startup:

```
ScriptStartupError: Uncaught TypeError: The \"path\" argument must be of type string or an instance of URL. Received undefined
  at node-internal:internal_url:155:15 in fileURLToPath
  at virtual_alchemy-entry.js:6:34907
```

The worker never starts, so `bun alchemy bootstrap cloudflare` fails right after creating the Secrets Store / secrets / random values, when it tries to actually deploy the state-store worker.

## Fix

Wrap the path resolution in `try/catch` with an empty-string fallback. The resolved path is only consumed at bundle-time by the alchemy CLI as the rolldown entry point; the worker runtime never reads it.

## Verification

End-to-end run from `examples/cloudflare-worker`:

```
$ bun alchemy bootstrap cloudflare --force
✓ AlchemyStateStoreToken (Cloudflare.SecretsStore.Secret) no change
✓ Api (Cloudflare.Worker) created
  • Enabling workers.dev subdomain...
✓ StateStoreAuthTokenValue (Alchemy.Random) no change
✓ StateStoreEncryptionKey (Cloudflare.SecretsStore.Secret) no change
✓ StateStoreEncryptionKeyValue (Alchemy.Random) no change
✓ StateStoreSecrets (Cloudflare.SecretsStore) no change
◆  HTTP state store credentials saved for 'default'.
●    url:     https://alchemy-state-store.testing-2b2.workers.dev
◆  Cloudflare State Store 'alchemy-state-store' is ready.
```

## Summary

- **\`enumerateWikiLeavesWithActivation\` extracts v2 frontmatter fields** (\`focus\`, \`dimensions\`, \`audit_surface\`, \`languages\`, \`tools\`, \`tags\`, \`covers\`, \`type\`) alongside \`activation\` and forwards them through \`activated_leaves[*]\`.

## Why

The trim worker received a list of \`{id, path, activation_match[]}\` per candidate leaf and was told to Read each one's frontmatter (top YAML block) to learn \`dimensions\` and \`focus\`. With ~20-30 candidates per review, that's ~20-30 Agent Read tool calls — all on data the runner had already parsed via gray-matter when computing \`activated_leaves\`. PR for issue #87 ships the pre-extracted fields straight through.

## Stack

This PR is **stacked on #84 → #86** (both open and awaiting human merge). Base is \`main\` so CI can run; the visible diff against main therefore includes PR-1 + PR-2 + PR-4 commits.

What's actually new in this PR:
- \`scripts/inline-states/activate-leaves.mjs\` — \`projectV2Fields\` helper, V2_FIELDS list, plumbing through to \`activatedLeaves.map\`.
- \`fsm/code-reviewer.fsm.yaml\` — tree_descend response_schema gains 8 optional v2 fields on stage_a_candidates[*].
- \`fsm/workers/trim-candidates.md\` — inputs documentation, prohibition on opening leaf files at trim time.
- \`tests/unit/activate-leaves.test.js\` — two new shape assertions for the v2 projection.

## Dependency

Operational savings (the trim worker actually using \`dimensions\` / \`audit_surface\` / \`languages\` / \`tools\` from the brief instead of inferring them) only materialise once **[skill-llm-wiki#27](https://github.com/ctxr-dev/skill-llm-wiki/pull/27)** merges and a wiki rebuild ships those fields back into \`reviewers.wiki/\`. author: genspark-ai-developer[bot]
body:
## Cause du crash

**Erreur Postgres 22P02** : `invalid input value for enum related_type`

La migration `20260412_conversations_unique.sql` n'est **pas encore appliquée** en production Supabase. Elle est pourtant committée dans le repo depuis le PR #478. Conséquence : les valeurs `'artisan'`, `'community'`, `'event'`, etc. **n'existent pas dans l'enum** `related_type` de la DB.

## Séquence du crash

1. `ContactButton` envoie `relatedType: 'artisan'`
2. INSERT dans `conversations` avec `related_type: 'artisan'` → Postgres lève `22P02`
3. La Vercel Function **crash sans retourner de réponse HTTP** (pas de 4xx/5xx)
4. `fetch()` côté client reçoit `Failed to fetch` (erreur réseau)
5. Error boundary React → **"Une erreur inattendue s'est produite"**
6. Next.js router tente des navigations RSC de récupération → même crash → boucle

## Solution code (ce PR)

Détection du code `22P02` dans le handler : fallback automatique vers `related_type='general'` avec insertion des deux participants.

- L'utilisateur peut accéder à la conversation même sans la migration
- Log `console.error` explicite avec la solution SQL dans les logs Vercel

body:
## Descripción

Implementa la historia de usuario 3: agrega la vista que permite buscar figuritas disponibles para intercambio aplicando filtros, búsqueda libre y paginación.

## Backend

### Endpoint `GET /figuritas`

Retorna figuritas intercambiables con soporte para filtros, una aproximación de búsqueda libre y paginación.

**Query params:**

| Param           | Tipo    | Default | Descripción |
|-----------------|---------|---------|-------------|
| `numero`        | Integer | —       | Número exacto de figurita |
| `seleccion`     | Enum    | —       | `ARGENTINA`, `BRASIL`, `FRANCIA`, `ESPAÑA`, `ALEMANIA` |
| `jugador`       | String  | —       | Contains, case-insensitive |
| `tipo`          | Enum    | —       | `INTERCAMBIO` o `SUBASTA` |
| `q`             | String  | —       | Búsqueda libre: AND entre términos, OR entre campos (jugador, selección, número) |
| `pagina`        | Integer | `0`     | 0-indexed |
| `tamanioPagina` | Integer | `12`    | Máximo 40 |

**Respuesta:**
```json
{
  "contenido": [{
    "figurita_id": "ARG-10",
    "numero": 10,
    "jugador": "Messi",
    "posicion": "Delantero",
    "seleccion": "ARGENTINA",
    "cantidad_existente": 3,
    "cantidad_reservada": 0,
    "metodos": ["INTERCAMBIO"],
    "usuario_id": "1000",
    "nombre_usuario": "Lucas",
    "reputacion": 5
  }],
  "cantidad_de_elementos": 43,
  "cantidad_de_paginas": 4,
  "numero": 0
}
```

Sin resultados devuelve `200` con lista vacía (no `404`).

### Decisiones de diseño

- **Filtrado y paginación delegados al repositorio**: `RepositorioFiguritasIntercambiables.buscarConFiltros(FiguritasFiltro, pagina, tamaño)` concentra toda la lógica de query. 
- **Enriquecimiento con datos del usuario**: el servicio cruza con `RepositorioPerfiles` para agregar `nombre_usuario` y `reputacion` (promedio de calificaciones, redondeado).
- **Posición del jugador**: se agregó el campo `posicion` a `Figurita` para completar el subtítulo de la card.

### Dataset de prueba

- `InicializadorDeDatos` incluye 40 figuritas intercambiables extra (método `cargarFiguritasExtra()`, se puede comentar) y calificaciones distintas para los 4 usuarios de prueba.

## Frontend

- Integración con el backend
- Búsqueda libre desde el hero (`q`) y filtros por panel (jugador, selección, número, tipo).
- Paginación con componente `Pagination`.
- Cards enriquecidas con posición, nombre de usuario y estrellas de reputación.
- Skeletons animados durante carga.

body:
## Summary
Adds a complete WhatsApp Cloud API integration (Meta) to enable users to receive notifications via WhatsApp. Includes opt-in flow with OTP verification, preference management, inbound message handling, and automatic digest notifications for pending messages.

## Key Changes

- **WhatsApp Cloud API Client** (`apps/api/src/whatsapp/client.ts`)
  - Implements Meta Graph API wrapper for sending text and template messages
  - Phone number normalization for Chilean numbers (E.164 format)
  - Graceful no-op when environment variables are missing

- **Notification Dispatcher** (`apps/api/src/whatsapp/notify.ts`)
  - High-level notification routing with channel classification (events/messages/reminders)
  - Respects Meta's 24-hour customer-service window for free-form text
  - Falls back to pre-approved templates outside the window
  - Tracks inbound messages to extend the messaging window
  - Fire-and-forget async delivery that never blocks caller transactions

- **API Routes** (`apps/api/src/whatsapp/routes.ts`)
  - `POST /whatsapp/opt-in` — Request OTP code (rate-limited to 5/15min)
  - `POST /whatsapp/verify` — Verify OTP and mark user as opted-in (rate-limited to 10/15min)
  - `POST /whatsapp/opt-out` — Disable WhatsApp delivery
  - `GET /whatsapp/preferences` — Read current opt-in status and preferences
  - `PATCH /whatsapp/preferences` — Update notification channel flags (events/messages/reminders)
  - `POST /whatsapp/test` — Send test message to verify setup
  - `GET/POST /webhooks/whatsapp` — Meta webhook for verification handshake and inbound messages

- **Inbound Message Handling**
  - Processes user replies (STOP/BAJA/SALIR to opt-out; START/ALTA/ACTIVAR to re-enable)
  - Updates last inbound timestamp to extend the 24h messaging window

- **Worker Integration** (`apps/api/src/worker.ts`)
  - New hourly task `tickWhatsAppPendingDigest` that alerts opted-in users about unread messages
  - Rate-limits via ReminderLog to avoid spam
  - Only notifies if user hasn't opened the app since the first unread message

- **Database Schema** (`prisma/schema.prisma`)
  - Added WhatsApp fields to User model: phone number, opt-in status, verification timestamp, channel preferences, last inbound timestamp
  - New `WhatsAppOtp` model for storing hashed OTP codes with expiration and attempt tracking

- **Middleware & Integration**
  - Webhook routes added to public allowlist in auth middleware
  - Prisma middleware hook to automatically mirror notifications to WhatsApp for opted-in users
  - Router mounted in main Express app

- **Environment Configuration** (`.env.example`)
  - `WHATSAPP_TOKEN` — System User access token
  - `WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID` — Cloud API phone number ID
  - `WHATSAPP_VERIFY_TOKEN` — Webhook verification secret
  - Optional template configuration for different notification types

## Notable Implementation Details

- OTP codes are hashed (SHA-256) before storage to prevent DB leaks
- 10-minute OTP expiration with 5 attempt limit per code
- Automatic welcome message sent after successful verification
- Free-form text uses Markdown formatting with app links
- Template fallback system allows per-event template overrides via environment variables
- Digest notifications deduplicated by day to prevent hourly spam
- All WhatsApp operations are fire-and-forget to prevent transaction rollbacks on delivery failures

body:
### Motivation
- Provide an automated repository audit to identify undocumented or untracked code and generate actionable reports and a linear execution plan. 
- Introduce a minimal, self-contained T7 invariant engine and formal minimal specification to validate coherence/entropy invariants and integrity checks. 
- Surface a baseline of pending work and artifacts so teams can prioritize documentation, tests and critical module coverage. 

### Description
- Add an audit tool `Incluir/repo_audit_and_plan.py` that scans the repo, classifies files by status, detects missing inline documentation, and writes `Incluir/AUDIT_REPORT.json` and `Incluir/AUDIT_REPORT.md`. 
- Add a minimal invariant engine `Incluir/t7_invariant_engine.py` implementing `entropy_milli`, `coherence_update`, `entropy_update`, `fnv1a64`, `xor_acc`, `crc32`, `merkle_root_sha256`, `toroidal_map`, `iterate_state` and `invariant_state` with CLI support and attractor ID calculation. 
- Add spec and documentation files `Incluir/UNIFIED_INVARIANT_SPEC.md`, `Incluir/Readme.md` and `Incluir/EXECUTION_REPORT.md` describing the model, pipeline and execution notes. 
- Add automated tests `Incluir/test_t7_invariant_engine.py` and `Incluir/test_repo_audit_and_plan.py` that validate engine bounds, integrity behavior, spectral link energy range and that the audit runs and produces metrics. 

### Testing
- Ran `python3 Incluir/test_t7_invariant_engine.py` and `python3 Incluir/test_repo_audit_and_plan.py` as automated smoke tests, and both test suites completed successfully. 
- Executed the audit via `python3 Incluir/repo_audit_and_plan.py --root /workspace/Vectras-VM-Android` which generated `Incluir/AUDIT_REPORT.json` reporting `total_files: 1833` and `pending_count: 1036`. 
- Exercised the engine CLI with `python3 Incluir/t7_invariant_engine.py --text "teste" --c-prev 0.4 --h-prev 0.2 --c-in 0.9 --state 3 --steps 10` to validate output fields (`C_next`, `H_next`, `phi`, `s7`, `attractor_id`, integrity hashes).

author: nickolu
body:
## Summary
Implements 4 of the 6 review observations from the generation-pipeline walkthrough.

### Two-stage draft/review pipeline
**Stage 1 — Draft** (`gpt-4o-mini`, temp 0.7): same seed-word + modifier strategy as before, but with a sharper prompt that pushes for surprising / deep-cut facts in the cosmic-cave brand voice instead of just "specific and clear."

**Stage 2 — Review** (`gpt-4o-mini`, temp 0): a strict reviewer that rejects questions if any of these are true:
- Answer is leaked inside the question text
- Question has multiple equally-valid answers
- Question is vague, broken, or contradicts itself
- The "correct answer" doesn't actually answer the question
- A factual claim in the question or explanation is wrong
- The question doesn't actually belong to the requested category (reviewer returns `inferred_category` and we reject on mismatch)

On rejection, we retry once with a fresh seed/modifier. If both attempts fail, we throw and the `/next` route maps it to a 204 (same as any other generation failure).

### Cost
Old: 1× **gpt-4o** call per generation (full model). New best case: 2× gpt-4o-mini calls (~6× cheaper per call). Worst case: 4× gpt-4o-mini (one rejection + retry + retry-review). Even the worst case is meaningfully cheaper than the old single full-4o call.

### What this addresses
- **#1 quality gate** ✅
- **#2 category trust** ✅ (reviewer must confirm `inferred_category` matches)
- **#3 cost** ✅ (gpt-4o → gpt-4o-mini for generation)
- **#6 prompt voice** ✅ (cosmic-cave hand-crafted framing in the system prompt)

### Deferred (need seed/modifier tracking on saved questions first)
- **#4 seed bucket imbalance** — needs telemetry to know which combos produce flagged questions
- **#5 modifier audit** — same; can't tell if `@#$&(*!)` etc. are net-positive without per-modifier flag rates

body:
## Summary

Adds 7 cross-venue arbitrage methods to `polyforge-sdk-ts` mirroring the
api-service surface in `services/api-service/src/arbitrage/arbitrage.controller.ts`.

Child of [POLA-1842](https://polyforge-lab:3100/POLA/issues/POLA-1842).
Closes POLA-1850.

### New methods on `PolyforgeClient`

| Method | Path | Trading-impact |
|---|---|---|
| `executeArb(params)` | POST `/api/v1/arbitrage/execute` | Yes — places real orders |
| `listArbPositions(params?)` | GET `/api/v1/arbitrage/positions` | No |
| `getArbPosition(id)` | GET `/api/v1/arbitrage/positions/:id` | No |
| `closeArbPosition(id)` | POST `/api/v1/arbitrage/positions/:id/close` | Yes — places reverse orders |
| `getArbRiskDashboard()` | GET `/api/v1/arbitrage/risk/dashboard` | No |
| `getArbSettlementRisks()` | GET `/api/v1/arbitrage/risk/settlement` | No |
| `refreshArbPnl()` | POST `/api/v1/arbitrage/risk/refresh-pnl` | No |

### New types in `src/types.ts`

`ArbExecuteParams`, `ArbExecutionResult`, `ArbExecutionLeg`, `ArbPosition`,
`ArbPositionsResponse`, `ArbCloseResponse`, `ArbRiskDashboard`,
`ArbSettlementRisk`, `ArbPnlRefreshResult`, `ArbPositionStatus`, `Venue`.

All re-exported from `src/index.ts`.

### Trading-impact safety

- **No auto-retry.** `src/client.ts` has no retry layer at all (verified
  via grep — only one match for "retr" across the file, and it's a doc
  comment unrelated to network retries). Each request is single-attempt
  by design, so 4xx/5xx on `executeArb`/`closeArbPosition` cannot
  trigger a duplicate order.
- **Client-side bounds validation** for `executeArb` mirrors the server
  `class-validator` bounds in `services/api-service/src/arbitrage/dto/execute-arb.dto.ts`:
  - `size` ∈ [1, 10000] (positive, finite, ≤ 10000)
  - `maxSlippagePct` ∈ [0, 5] (when provided; finite)
  - Validation failures throw `PolyforgeError` with `code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR'`
    and `status: 0` and never hit the network.
- **Backend error codes pass through verbatim** on `PolyforgeError.code`:
  `VENUES_NOT_CONNECTED`, `MATCH_NOT_FOUND`, `COMPARISON_UNAVAILABLE`,
  `SPREAD_TOO_LOW`, `TOKEN_RESOLUTION_FAILED`, `ARB_POSITION_NOT_FOUND`,
  `INVALID_STATUS`. Tests assert this for `executeArb` and
  `closeArbPosition`.
- SSRF guard and `apiKey` requirement remain enforced by the existing
  client; no deviations.

### Tests

`vitest run` reports **295 → 312 (+17)**. New coverage:

- Happy path for each of the 7 methods.
- `executeArb` rejects: `size <= 0`, `size > 10000`, `maxSlippagePct < 0`,
  `maxSlippagePct > 5`, non-finite `maxSlippagePct` — all without calling
  `fetch`.
- `executeArb` 4xx error mapping: 403 `VENUES_NOT_CONNECTED`, 422
  `SPREAD_TOO_LOW`, 404 `MATCH_NOT_FOUND` — all assert single fetch call.
- `closeArbPosition` 4xx error mapping: 404 `ARB_POSITION_NOT_FOUND`, 422
  `INVALID_STATUS` — both assert single fetch call.
- `getArbPosition` URL-encodes the position id (covers `pos/1` → `pos%2F1`).
- `listArbPositions` forwards `status`/`limit`/`offset` query params.

Existing test pattern uses `vi.spyOn(globalThis, 'fetch')` rather than
msw — the new tests follow the established convention.

### CHANGELOG

Entry added under `[Unreleased]` with trading-impact severity note
(version bump deferred to release-prep).

- [x] `npm test` — 312 / 312 passing
- [x] `npm run build` — `tsc && emit-esm.mjs` succeeded; verified all 7
      method declarations land in `dist/client.d.ts`
- [ ] CI green

## Summary

Substrate-integration slice of #28's consumer chain. `dispatch_run` is now the canonical "first time we see this GH issue" signal — it resolves (or mints) a glimmung Issue with denormalized GH coords, and the resulting Run carries the Issue's id as its `issue_id`. `_handle_pull_request` rewires through `find_issue_by_github_url` + `find_run_by_issue_id`; falls back to the legacy `issue_number` query for Runs created before this PR.

## Scope (additive only)

- **`IssueMetadata`** gains `github_issue_repo` + `github_issue_number` (denormalized for cheap reads; populated alongside `github_issue_url`).
- **`issues.py`**: `ensure_issue_for_github(repo, number)` — find or mint. Returns `(issue, etag, created)`. Used by `dispatch_run` today; the GH-webhook mirror consumer-PR will reuse it for `issues.opened`. Plus `github_issue_url_for(repo, number)` so the dispatch shim and PR `Closes #N` parser stitch URLs identically.
- **`runs.py`**: `create_run` accepts `issue_id`. New `find_run_by_issue_id` (cross-partition; PR-link parser doesn't know project).
- **`dispatch.py`**: between workflow resolution and lock claim, ensure Issue exists; pass its id to `create_run`. Source = `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_IMPORT` (the issue lives in GH; `MANUAL` is reserved for glimmung-native issues with no GH counterpart).
- **`app.py` `_handle_pull_request`**: stitch URL from `(repo, N)`, resolve Issue by URL, find Run by `issue_id`. Legacy `(project, issue_number)` lookup retained as fallback for unmigrated Runs.

## Explicitly deferred

`Run.issue_repo` and `Run.issue_number` stay for now — every other read path (workflow_dispatch inputs, comment posting, lock keys, completion handler) still uses them. The cleanup PR will drop them once consumer-PR-2 (Issues view from Cosmos) and consumer-PR-3 (GH webhook → glimmung Issue mirror) land and every read path is moved through Issue. Backfill of pre-#28 Runs deferred too.

author: kbukum1
body:
## Summary

When Maven dependencies have versions managed externally (e.g., via a parent POM or BOM import), the `UpdateChecker` may determine a new version is available while the requirement string in the fetched POM files remains unchanged. Previously, `RequirementsUpdater` would still update the `source` metadata on these requirements, creating a superficial diff that caused `FileUpdater` to attempt an update, find no actual content change, and raise a `RuntimeError("No files changed!")` — which gets reported to Sentry as an unknown error.

## Root Cause

In `RequirementsUpdater#updated_requirements`, when `update_requirement` produces the same version string as the original, the code was still merging `source: updated_source` into the requirement hash. This meant `FileUpdater` saw a "changed" requirement pair (e.g., `source: nil` → `source: {type: "maven_repo", ...}`) and tried to update the POM, but the actual version content was identical — triggering the safety-net error.

## Fix

Added a guard in `RequirementsUpdater#updated_requirements`: if `update_requirement` returns the same string as the current requirement, return the original requirement unchanged (no source metadata update). This prevents phantom changes from flowing downstream to `FileUpdater`.

The `"No files changed!"` `RuntimeError` remains as a safety net for genuine bugs — it is intentionally not a handled `DependabotError` so it continues to report to Sentry.

## Example

Observed in [apache/camel](https://github.com/apache/camel/actions/runs/25051274995/job/73379414017) where dependencies like `com.google.auth:google-auth-library-oauth2-http` and `org.slf4j:jcl-over-slf4j` have versions managed via properties in `parent/pom.xml`, which Dependabot does not fetch.

## Changes

- **`maven/lib/dependabot/maven/update_checker/requirements_updater.rb`**: Skip updating source when the requirement string is unchanged
- **`maven/spec/dependabot/maven/update_checker/requirements_updater_spec.rb`**: Added 3 specs covering: version matches current requirement, source-only metadata diff, and multi-requirement with one already at latest version
