This pull request adds support for migrating NSubstitute "Received" and "DidNotReceive" verification calls to their Mockolate equivalents in the code fixer, and introduces comprehensive tests to verify this functionality. The main changes include implementing logic to identify and rewrite verification calls, updating the code fix provider to handle these rewrites, and ensuring the correct using directives are added. Additionally, new tests cover various verification scenarios to ensure correctness.

### NSubstitute Verification Migration

* Added `FindAndBuildVerifyReplacements` and related helper methods to identify and rewrite NSubstitute verification calls (`Received`, `DidNotReceive`) to the corresponding Mockolate verification calls (`AtLeastOnce`, `Never`, `Exactly`, `Once`) in `NSubstituteCodeFixProvider.cs`.
* Updated the node replacement logic in `ConvertAssertionAsync` to apply these verification rewrites during code fix application.
* Ensured that the necessary `using Mockolate.Verify;` directive is added when verification rewrites are present.

### Testing

* Added a new test suite `VerifyTests` in `NSubstituteCodeFixProviderTests.VerifyTests.cs` to verify that various forms of NSubstitute verification calls are correctly rewritten to the appropriate Mockolate calls, including argument matchers and count-based verifications.

## Changes provided by this PR

This PR resolves warning **W8917** logged by the ioBroker repository checker.

### What this PR does

This PR adds an ignore rule to the Dependabot configuration in `.github/dependabot.yml` to prevent Dependabot from automatically proposing major version bumps for the `@types/node` package.

The following change is applied to every `updates:` block that specifies `package-ecosystem: npm` and `directory: /` or `directories: ['**/*']`:

```yaml
ignore:
  - dependency-name: "@types/node"
    update-types:
      - "version-update:semver-major"
```

### Why this change is needed

The `@types/node` package provides TypeScript type definitions for the Node.js runtime API. The major version of `@types/node` that an adapter should use is determined by the **lowest** major Node.js version the adapter supports. The lowest supported Node.js version is specified in the `engines.node` field of `package.json`.

Allowing Dependabot to automatically bump `@types/node` to a newer major version would introduce type definitions for Node.js APIs that are not available in the minimum supported Node.js version. This can lead to incorrect type checking and potential runtime errors on older Node.js installations. Therefore, major version updates of `@types/node` must always be reviewed manually and aligned with any intentional change to the minimum supported Node.js version.

### Reference

- [ioBroker Repository Checker – Warning W8917](https://github.com/ioBroker/ioBroker.repochecker)
- [Dependabot ignore configuration](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/working-with-dependabot/dependabot-options-reference#ignore)

### Was dieser PR macht

Dieser PR fügt der Dependabot-Konfiguration in `.github/dependabot.yml` eine Ignore-Regel hinzu, die verhindert, dass Dependabot automatisch Major-Version-Bumps für das Paket `@types/node` vorschlägt.

```yaml

    update-types:
      - "version-update:semver-major"
```

### Warum diese Änderung notwendig ist

Das Paket `@types/node` stellt TypeScript-Typdefinitionen für die Node.js-Laufzeit-API bereit. Die Major-Version von `@types/node`, die ein Adapter verwenden sollte, wird durch die **niedrigste** unterstützte Node.js-Hauptversion des Adapters bestimmt. Die niedrigste unterstützte Node.js-Version wird im Feld `engines.node` in `package.json` angegeben.

Daher müssen Major-Version-Updates von `@types/node` immer manuell geprüft und mit einer bewussten Änderung der minimal unterstützten Node.js-Version abgestimmt werden.

body:
## BugLens AI Fix

**Bug:** [BUG-0035] Burger positioning issue

### Root cause
The burger journey positioning logic is calculating positions for all sections but not properly stopping at the 'journey ends' section (#order/CTA). The issue states the burger should stop at the top-middle position when entering the final section and only move back when scrolling up, but currently it's overlaying content throughout the entire section.

### How this fix works
The bug occurs because the CTA section (#order) has a ScrollTrigger that transitions the burger from the testimonials state to the CTA state, but the trigger points (start: 'top 90%', end: 'center 48%') cause the burger to animate down through most of the section instead of stopping at the top. To fix this, we need to modify the scroll trigger for the CTA section to have the burger reach its final position much earlier (at the top of the section) and stay there. We'll change the end point from 'center 48%' to 'top 20%' so the burger completes its journey to the top-middle position immediately when the section enters and stays pinned there.

### Files changed
- **modify** `assets/js/burger-journey.js`

author: copilot
body:
The existing payment flow created bookings as immediately `PAID` with a fake QR code UI. This replaces it with a real MoMo Sandbox integration: PENDING booking → MoMo gateway redirect → IPN callback confirms payment → tickets created.

## Backend

- **`paymentControllers.js`** — HMAC-SHA256 signature generation, MoMo API call, creates `PENDING` booking with `momoOrderId`; IPN callback verifies MoMo signature before updating booking to `PAID` and inserting tickets; `checkPaymentStatus` endpoint for frontend polling
- **`paymentRouters.js`** — Three rate-limited endpoints: `POST /create-momo-order`, `POST /momo-callback`, `GET /check-status/:orderId`
- **`Booking.js`** — Added `momoOrderId`, `transactionId`, `paymentStatus` fields with index on `momoOrderId`
- **`server.js`** — Registers `/api/payment` route
- **`package.json`** — Added `axios` (latest, no known CVEs) and `express-rate-limit`
- **`.env.example`** — Documents required MoMo Sandbox env vars (`MOMO_PARTNER_CODE`, `MOMO_ACCESS_KEY`, `MOMO_SECRET_KEY`, `MOMO_ENDPOINT`, `MOMO_IPN_URL`, `MOMO_REDIRECT_URL`)

## Frontend

- **`paymentService.js`** — `createMoMoOrder(bookingData, token)` and `checkPaymentStatus(orderId)` fetch wrappers
- **`PaymentPage.jsx`** — MoMo method calls `createMoMoOrder` then does `window.location.href = payUrl`; non-MoMo methods retain existing direct-booking flow; fake QR replaced with MoMo-branded block
- **`PaymentResult.jsx`** — New page at `/payment-result`; backend status is authoritative, URL `resultCode` param used only as fallback when backend is unreachable; shows booking summary on success
- **`App.jsx`** — Adds `/payment-result` route

## Security

- IPN callback verifies MoMo's HMAC-SHA256 signature before mutating any data
- `orderId` uses `Date.now()` + `crypto.randomBytes(4)` to prevent collisions
- User-supplied `orderId` param sanitized to `[A-Za-z0-9]` before Mongoose query
- `resultCode` explicitly coerced to `Number` before comparison

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

## Mục tiêu
Tích hợp thanh toán MoMo Sandbox để thay thế QR code ảo hiện tại. Người dùng có thể đặt vé và thanh toán thực tế qua MoMo.

## Yêu cầu

### Backend (Express.js)
1. **Cài dependencies**: `axios` để gọi MoMo API
2. **Tạo Payment Routes** (`backend/src/routes/paymentRouters.js`):
   - `POST /api/payment/create-momo-order` - tạo order MoMo
   - `POST /api/payment/momo-callback` - webhook nhận callback từ MoMo
   - `GET /api/payment/check-status/:orderId` - kiểm tra trạng thái thanh toán

3. **Tạo Payment Controller** (`backend/src/controllers/paymentControllers.js`):
   - Xử lý tạo signature HMAC-SHA256
   - Gọi MoMo API để tạo payment link
   - Xử lý callback từ MoMo (cập nhật Booking status)

4. **Cập nhật Booking Model** - thêm field:
   - `momoOrderId` - id từ MoMo
   - `transactionId` - transaction id từ MoMo
   - `paymentStatus` - PENDING/PAID/FAILED

5. **.env** - thêm MoMo Sandbox credentials:
   ```
   MOMO_PARTNER_CODE=MOMO
   MOMO_ACCESS_KEY=F8BBA842ECF85
   MOMO_SECRET_KEY=K951B6PE1waDMi640xX08PD3vg6EkVlz
   MOMO_ENDPOINT=https://test-payment.momo.vn/v2/gateway/api/create
   MOMO_IPN_URL=http://localhost:3001/api/payment/momo-callback
   MOMO_REDIRECT_URL=http://localhost:5173/payment-result
   ```

### Frontend (React + Vite)
1. **Tạo Payment Service** (`frontend/src/services/paymentService.js`):
   - `createMoMoOrder(bookingData)` - gọi backend để lấy payUrl
   - `checkPaymentStatus(orderId)` - kiểm tra trạng thái thanh toán

2. **Cập nhật PaymentPage.jsx** (`frontend/src/pages/PaymentPage.jsx`):
   - Thay vì tạo booking ngay, gọi API tạo MoMo order trước
   - Redirect tới `payUrl` từ MoMo
   - Sau khi thanh toán xong, quay về `/payment-result`

3. **Tạo Payment Result Page** (`frontend/src/pages/PaymentResult.jsx`):
   - Hiển thị trạng thái thanh toán (thành công/thất bại)
   - Nút quay về trang chủ

4. **Cập nhật App.jsx**:
   - Thêm route `/payment-result` → `PaymentResult.jsx`

5. **.env.development** - thêm:
   ```
   VITE_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:5001
   VITE_MOMO_SANDBOX=true
   ```

## Flow thanh toán
1. User chọn ghế → Nhấn "Thanh toán" → PaymentPopup chọn MoMo
2. Redirect tới `/payment`
3. Frontend gọi `POST /api/payment/create-momo-order` với booking info
4. Backend tạo signature + gọi MoMo API → nhận payUrl
5. Frontend redirect tới payUrl (MoMo payment gateway)
6. User nhập PIN MoMo → Thanh toán
7. MoMo redirect về `/payment-result` + gọi webhook `/api/payment/momo-callback`
8. Backend cập nhật Booking status = PAID
9. Frontend hiển thị "Thanh toán thành công"

- Dùng **MoMo Sandbox** (test environment)
- Không thay đổi luồng Booking hiện tại, chỉ thêm payment layer
- Giữ payload Booking tương thích với DB hiện tại
- Thêm error handling + loading states

author: bigin
body:
Implements Phase 2 of the [iManager 2.0 plan](https://github.com/bigin/Scriptor/blob/master/docs/imanager-2.0-plan.md) — the architectural foundation everything else will sit on.                                                                                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           
  ## What's in
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           
  ### Exception hierarchy                                   
  - `Imanager\Exception\ImanagerException` marker interface — catch this to handle any iManager error generically.
  - Concrete classes extend the appropriate SPL base:                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
    - `StorageException`, `ValidationException`, `SchemaException`, `NotFoundException` → `\RuntimeException`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
    - `ConfigException` → `\LogicException` (bad config is a programming/deployment mistake, not a runtime condition)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
  - `ValidationException` carries readonly `$field` + `InputErrorCode` for typed error reporting.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  - `NotFoundException` ships named factories (`category()`, `field()`, `item()`) for consistent messages.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           
  ### Enums                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
  - `Enum\FieldType` lists the 17 built-in field types from iManager 1.x with stable string contracts; `sqliteAffinity()` maps each to `Enum\SqliteAffinity` for Phase 4's generated columns.                                                                                                                                                                                              
  - `Enum\InputErrorCode` preserves the integer values from 1.x's `InputInterface` constants (so anything that persisted them numerically still works).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           
  ### Config                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               
  - `Imanager\Config` is `final readonly` with promoted constructor.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       
  - `Config::default()` / `Config::fromArray()` / `Config::merge()` — fail-fast on unknown keys, type mismatches, or out-of-range values (e.g. `maxItemsPerPage: 0`, empty `dataPath`).                                                                                                                                                                                                    
  - ConfigArray PHPDoc-shape acts as the typed contract for both PHPStan and Psalm.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           
  ### Bootstrap                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            
  - `Imanager\Bootstrap::boot($overrides)` returns a `League\Container\Container` with shared `Config` and a PSR-3 `NullLogger`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           
  - All later phases will register their services on the same container.

author: mehdiskouri
body:
Closes Phase 4 follow-up gap on displacement detail recovery and the NF-1.5 200KB ceiling.

## Changes

- **Displacement modifier path.** The realize-path mesh is capped at
  256x256 (PR #40). To return the high-frequency detail we now attach
  a DISPLACE modifier driven by the full-resolution 16-bit heightmap
  PNG, with strength derived from the spec's elevation band.
  - New `mesh.add_displace_modifier` RPC in `scripts/blender/adapter.py`
    (loads the image, creates an IMAGE texture, attaches the modifier).
  - `scene.diff` now exposes `textures` so the new step can be
    postcondition-checked downstream.
  - `RpcMethods.MESH_ADD_DISPLACE` registered, sequence validator
    accepts the new call.
  - `create_terrain_from_heightmap` curated sequence gains the new
    step + inputs; `realize_region` composite forwards them.
  - `forge_mcp/server/tools/generation.py` threads the heightmap PNG
    path and the elevation-band-derived strength into the macro inputs.
- **PNG oversize retry.** The engine already enforced the 200 KB
  ceiling; it now tags the failure with `reason_code='png_oversize'`,
  and the typed `render_preview` facade transparently re-runs the
  macro once with PNG `compression` bumped from 15 to 30 before
  re-raising. Compression is a real macro input now (was hard-coded).

## Verification

- `uv run ruff check .` clean
- `uv run ruff format --check .` clean
- `uv run mypy` strict + disallow_any_explicit clean (100 source files)
- `FORGE_BLENDER_BIN=/usr/bin/blender uv run pytest --cov=forge_mcp --cov-branch --cov-fail-under=90`:
  399 passed, 11 skipped (Blender-host integration), 96.35% branch coverage
- New tests:
  - retry succeeds at compression=30 on first oversize
  - failure propagates with `reason_code='png_oversize'` if retry also overflows
  - sequence validator accepts `mesh.add_displace_modifier`
  - existing engine `png_max_bytes` test asserts `reason_code`

author: razvandimescu
body:
## Summary

Compounding Windows bugs let `numa install` capture a corrupt backup that `numa uninstall` then used to wipe the user's manually-configured DNS, leaving them offline until they edited the registry by hand. Reported and reproduced on Russian Win11 26100 in #160 (independently corroborated by a second user).

- **Filter the deprecated IPv6 site-local stubs** `fec0:0:0:ffff::1/2/3` in `is_loopback_or_stub`. `Get-DnsClientServerAddress` returns these for any IPv6-enabled adapter without explicit DNS, so every VPN/virtual interface ended up with identical garbage in the backup.
- **Drop the `dhcp` field from `WindowsInterfaceDns`.** It was sourced from `Get-NetIPInterface.Dhcp` (IPv4 lease mode), not DNS source — so "DHCP IP + manual DoH resolvers" was stamped `dhcp=true` and the user's manual servers were wiped on uninstall. Decide DHCP-vs-static on `real_servers.is_empty()` instead. Old backup files on disk deserialize fine — the unknown `dhcp` field is silently ignored.
- **Pass ifIndex to netsh instead of the friendly adapter name.** Friendly names fail with `ERROR_INVALID_NAME` on non-English locales (the ru-RU `Ethernet` failure in #160). ifIndex is locale-invariant and resolved live at restore time (`if_index` is `skip_serializing` since it's not stable across reboots). A small `run_netsh_ipv4` helper consolidates the four call sites.
- **Preserve the backup when an adapter isn't currently up at uninstall.** Previously the backup was always deleted, so an offline-during-uninstall adapter could never be recovered. Now the backup is kept and the user is told to re-run `numa uninstall` after reconnecting; only adapters that were successfully restored advance toward backup deletion.

Closes four of the six checklist items in #160: fec0 filter, dhcp misclassification, ru-RU `ERROR_INVALID_NAME`, and the install-side disconnected-adapter guard (already filtered by `Get-NetAdapter | Status -eq 'Up'`; this PR adds the symmetric uninstall-side preserve-on-offline path). Two items remain on the umbrella issue and need a Russian-locale repro: the `netsh` exit-code mismatch on ru-RU, and the three uninstall-hardening sub-items (always-re-enable Dnscache on backup-read failure, force-revert orphan 127.0.0.1 adapters, defer `disable_dnscache` until Numa binds :53).

## Test plan

- [x] `make all` green (lint + build + 380 unit tests + 1 integration test)
- [x] `windows_backup_filters_loopback` extended with the fec0 stub case (Tailscale-style virtual adapter)
- [x] `parse_powershell_servers` (renamed from `parse_powershell_dhcp_and_static`) confirms the stripped JSON shape parses
- [x] `parse_powershell_legacy_backup_without_if_index` confirms pre-fix backups on disk deserialize with `if_index = 0` (re-resolved live at restore time)
- [x] Manual upgrade smoke: en-US Windows, `numa install` over an existing 0.14.2 install upgrades cleanly to 0.14.3 (legacy backup with `dhcp` field is preserved unchanged, no read-side errors)
- [x] Manual install/uninstall round-trip on a Windows box with DHCP IP + manual DNS — verified on a machine carrying a 0.14.2-written backup; 0.14.3 uninstall correctly read the legacy backup, ignored the now-removed `dhcp:true` field, took the `real_servers.is_empty() == false` static branch, and restored Wi-Fi to its original `213.154.124.1, 193.231.252.1` (pre-fix would have wiped to DHCP)
- [ ] Manual install/uninstall on a Windows box with VPN/virtual adapters — verify those interfaces are restored to DHCP rather than pinned to fec0 stubs
- [x] Manual install/uninstall on Win11 with regional settings switched to RU — ifIndex path completed end-to-end for `Wi-Fi` and `Ethernet 4`, both DNS-set and DNS-restore. Caveat: netsh emitted English (system display language fell back to en-US), so the original `Команда выполнена успешно` / `ERROR_INVALID_NAME` reproduction conditions weren't fully present. New code path validated; full ru-RU display-language reproduction still pending.
- [ ] Manual offline-adapter path — disconnect Wi-Fi between install and uninstall, verify backup is kept; reconnect and re-run uninstall, verify restore completes and backup is removed

author: irinanazarova
body:
## Summary

Adds **`/compare/socket-io`** — a methodology-first comparison built around benchmarks of three real configurations at 10,000 concurrent clients on identical Railway infrastructure (Pro tier, 32 vCPU / 32 GB).

The three configurations measured:
- **Default Socket.io** — no opt-ins, in-memory adapter
- **Socket.io + Connection State Recovery** — opt-in feature added in Socket.io 4.6
- **AnyCable** — extended Action Cable protocol with the in-memory broker

Headline numbers (full data on the page):
- **Delivery rate:** 87.4% / 100% / 100%
- **Replay latency p99:** lost / 9.0 s / 1.0 s
- **Idle connection capacity:** AnyCable holds 50,000 idle connections on a single instance using 1.98 GB and ~0.3 vCPU

## Page structure

H2s are analytical takeaway statements so skim-readers get the thesis from the headings alone:

1. *Only AnyCable delivers every message on time*
2. *Every Socket.io deploy severs every connection. This is architectural.*
3. *AnyCable holds 50,000 idle connections on under 2 GB and 0.3 vCPU*

Plus: methodology callout (authorship, reproducibility, customer trust signals), migration code example, three-column feature comparison with citations to both AnyCable and Socket.io docs, FAQ accordion (incl. AnyCable+ managed-tier entry), and CTA linking to docs + customer page.

## Design

Page-scoped under `.compare-page` so styles don't leak elsewhere.

- **Notebook-feel dotted background** continuous across the entire page
- **Rounded white cards** (8 px) for tables and dark-bg code blocks on the dotted surface — tables read as discrete notes pinned to graph paper
- **Sticky right column** so illustrations / tables stay visible while the left text scrolls (resolves the previous "right side empty for thousands of pixels" problem)
- **Inline `<code>` chips** at 0.85 em with subtle background and 4 px radius — reads calm next to body sans-serif
- **Red accent reserved for "worst per metric"** only; not used for emphasis
- **Anchor links on all H2s** (`#delivery`, `#deploys`, `#capacity`, `#migration`, `#faq-heading`) so readers and agents can deep-link
- **FAQ as native `<details>` accordion** — closed by default, narrow centered column

## Mobile

- Hero stacks to single column
- H1 size clamps to 28-64 px responsive
- About-slide right column hidden via existing `mediaMax($tablet)` rule

## Files

- `src/compare/socket-io/index.html` — new comparison page
- `src/modules/blocks/compare.scss` — new page-scoped styles
- `src/modules/blocks/about-slide.scss` — added `-sticky` and `-full` media modifiers + calm inline-code chips
- `src/index.scss` — imports compare.scss
- `src/blog/anycable-vs-socket-io/index.md` — removed (content now lives on the comparison page)
- `.gitignore` — `benchmark/` (lives in its own repo: `irinanazarova/anycable-socketio-benchmarks`)

## Reproducibility

All benchmark numbers come from runs reproducible from the open-source bench repo: <https://github.com/irinanazarova/anycable-socketio-benchmarks>. The bench-runner deploys to Railway and uses internal networking (`*.railway.internal`) to drive 10K-client tests without local NAT/event-loop bottlenecks.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open `/compare/socket-io` at desktop width (1440 px) — confirm sticky right column, dotted background, hero card layout
- [ ] Scroll through each pillar — confirm tables stay visible while reading the left column
- [ ] Click each section anchor link — confirm scroll position respects the 60 px header offset
- [ ] Open and close FAQ items — confirm `+/−` indicator, red title color on open
- [ ] Resize to 390 px (iPhone width) — confirm hero stacks to single column, no horizontal overflow, H1 fits
- [ ] Click each doc-citation link in the feature comparison table — confirm 200 (no 404s)
- [ ] Verify no JS errors in console

body:
### Motivation
- Allow users to enter receipts manually without requiring an image and avoid running AI categorization for those manual entries.
- Provide the ability to attach/replace an image on an existing receipt from the receipt detail UI.
- Track receipt `source` so the backend can adjust behavior (AI categorization, category source, storage handling) based on origin.

### Description
- Client: added an `entryMode` (`scan` | `manual`) and toggle UI in `UploadReceipt`, only requiring `imageData` for `scan` mode and sending `source` in upload payload, plus minor UI/flow updates like resetting to scan mode on reset and defaulting date for manual entries.
- Client: added image attach support to the receipt detail page with `optimizeImage` usage, a hidden file input, `handleAttachImage` handler, `isAttachingImage` state, and a button to attach/replace images which calls `POST /api/receipts/:id/attach-image`.
- Server: added `receipt-flow-utils.ts` to resolve receipt sources and categorization rules, accepted `source` in `/api/receipts`, set initial `categorySource` via `resolveInitialCategorySource`, and skipped AI categorization when `shouldRunAiCategorization` returns false for `manual` sources.
- Server: added `POST /api/receipts/:id/attach-image` endpoint to validate, upload image (Azure Blob Storage with Replit fallback), update the receipt record and return the image URL and blob name.
- Tests & tooling: added `server/tests/manual-entry-flow.test.ts` unit tests and a `test:manual-flow` npm script in `package.json`.

### Testing
- Added unit tests in `server/tests/manual-entry-flow.test.ts` covering `resolveReceiptSource`, `resolveInitialCategorySource`, and `shouldRunAiCategorization` and executed them via `npm run test:manual-flow`, which passed.
- Existing upload flow adjustments were exercised by running the upload mutation locally with both `scan` and `manual` `source` payloads to confirm the server accepts `source` and only runs AI for non-manual receipts (manual verification via local dev server).

The service crashes on startup with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'aioredis'` because `vital_analyzer.py` line 5 uses `import aioredis`, a deprecated standalone package that is not installed. A previous fix (PR #3) corrected the same import in `main.py` but missed this file.

## Solution

Replaced `import aioredis` with `from redis import asyncio as aioredis` in `vital_analyzer.py`, matching the fix already applied to `main.py`. The `redis[hiredis]==5.0.1` package in `requirements.txt` provides `redis.asyncio` as a fully API-compatible drop-in replacement, so all existing type hints and method calls in the file continue to work unchanged.

author: githappens
body:
## Problem

`WatcherFSEvents::~WatcherFSEvents()` invalidates and releases the
`FSEventStreamRef`, then deletes `WatcherGen`. None of those calls
synchronously drain callbacks already dispatched onto the stream's
`dispatch_queue_t`. An in-flight `FSEventCallback` running on a GCD
worker thread can still be reading `DirsChanged`, `WatcherGen`,
`Listener`, etc. while the destructor is freeing them — a data race
that manifests as a use-after-free / heap corruption crashing inside
`libsystem_platform`'s `_platform_memmove` / `_platform_memset` when
unrelated heap operations later run.

## Reproduction

Caught with ThreadSanitizer in our application's filesystem-watching
integration tests on macOS arm64 (built with clang 21,
`-fsanitize=thread`, runtime swapped to Apple's CLT TSan dylib due to
an unrelated nix compiler-rt issue on macOS 26).

TSan report (abbreviated):

```
WARNING: ThreadSanitizer: data race
  Read of size 8 by main thread:
    #0 efsw::WatcherFSEvents::~WatcherFSEvents()  WatcherFSEvents.cpp
    #1 efsw::FileWatcherFSEvents::removeWatch(long)  FileWatcherFSEvents.cpp
    ...

  Previous write of size 8 by thread T1:
    #0 efsw::WatcherFSEvents::process()  WatcherFSEvents.cpp
    #1 efsw::FileWatcherFSEvents::FSEventCallback(...)  FileWatcherFSEvents.cpp
    #2 implementation_callback_rpc      (FSEvents.framework)
    #3 _dispatch_client_callout         (libdispatch.dylib)

  Thread T1 is a GCD worker thread
```

Across 30 stress iterations of our test suite (each running 5–9
real-disk filewatcher tests under TSan), the race fired **93 times**
on the unpatched code, plus three runtime SEGVs in
`_platform_memmove`. With this patch applied: **0 hits, 0 SEGVs**.

## Fix

Apple's documented FSEventStream shutdown sequence on a dispatch
queue is `Stop → Invalidate → drain queue → Release`. `Invalidate`
prevents *new* callbacks from being scheduled but does not wait for
ones already in flight, so a `dispatch_sync(queue, ^{})` barrier is
required before releasing the stream and tearing down state the
callback may still be reading.

This patch:

- Stores the dispatch queue created in `init()` as a member
  (`DispatchQueue`) so the destructor can reach it.
- Inserts a `dispatch_sync(DispatchQueue, ^{})` barrier between
  `FSEventStreamInvalidate` and `FSEventStreamRelease`.
- Releases the queue itself via `dispatch_release` after the stream
  is gone (we own one reference from `dispatch_queue_create`).

No behavioural change for callers; just plugs the teardown race.

author: erwanviot
body:
## Summary
Reduce friction when logging the same meals over and over. Opening the entry modal now surfaces up to **3 horizontally-scrolling cards** with what the user has eaten most often for that meal type over the last 30 days.

- **Tap the card** = quick add, modal closes, optimistic update lands the meal in `DailyFeed`. Undo is the standard ✕ button on the resulting `MealCard` — no new toast system needed.
- **Tap ✏️** = prefill the manual tab so the user can adjust before adding.

## Implementation (Phase 1, no new table)
- `src/utils/recurringMeals.ts` — pure logic. Groups `meal_logs` by `reference_id` (CIQUAL/OFF) or normalized name; scores each group by `count + 0.5 × recency`; requires ≥ 2 occurrences in the 30-day window so first-time users see no noisy block.
- `src/hooks/useRecurringMeals.ts` — React Query, scoped to user × mealType × window-start, 60 s `staleTime`.
- `src/components/nutrition/RecurringMealsBlock.tsx` — horizontal scroll cards with the latest used name + kcal + quantity + occurrence count.
- `MealEntryForm` — block sits between the header and the tab row; renders nothing when loading or empty.
- `useDailyNutrition.addMeal/deleteMeal` — invalidate the `recurringMeals` cache so the "X× this month" counter reflects the live state.

## Review feedback already addressed
- Removed the redundant "+" button on each card (was a duplicate `aria-label` against the clickable card → WCAG violation)
- Added an explicit error message when quick add fails (was failing silently)
- Centralized the error display so manual/search panes no longer duplicate it
- Dropped `snap-mandatory` to avoid touch-axis conflicts with the modal's vertical scroll on iOS Safari

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run lint` — clean
- [x] `npm run check:i18n` — 16 namespaces, 2035 keys aligned
- [x] `npm test` — 344/344 green (incl. 9 new tests for grouping/scoring)

author: billdenney
body:
Adds the third top-level message type to the IPC vocabulary, after ClientRequest (client→agent) and AgentResponse (agent→client, in reply to a request). AgentEvent is agent→client, *unsolicited* — the agent's mechanism to notify subscribed clients about state changes without a matching ClientRequest.

Two cases today:

- `badgeChanged(BadgeChangedPayload)` — a path's badge changed. Sent to every client that subscribed to a root containing the path. Carries the `subscriptionId` (so a client with multiple active subscriptions routes to the right handler), the absolute path, and the new badge identifier. `badge: nil` means "now clean — clear any cached badge for this path."

- `subscriptionEnded(SubscriptionEndedPayload)` — the agent is terminating a subscription unilaterally. Sent on agent shutdown, watched repo removed, volume unmounted, permissions revoked, etc. Carries the subscriptionId + a wire-stable `reason` string clients can pattern-match on (`agent_shutdown`, `repo_removed`, `volume_unmounted`, `unauthorized`, `internal`).

Why a separate type, not just more cases on AgentResponse --------------------------------------------------------- Responses correlate to requests by id; the receiver's request- response correlator looks them up and fulfills the pending continuation. Events have a fresh id (for log dedup) but no correlation expected — they go through the subscription handler. Splitting at the type level lets the receiver dispatch immediately without inspecting the discriminator first.

Tests check that the `kind` namespaces don't collide either — decoding a `badgeReply` shape as AgentEvent fails with unknownMessageKind, and vice versa. Required because both message types share the same wire transport; we want a stale receiver to loudly reject mistyped messages rather than silently misinterpret.

Tests (6 total)
---------------
- `badgeChanged` round-trip with non-nil badge.
- `badgeChanged` round-trip with nil badge (now-clean signal).
- `subscriptionEnded` round-trip with reason code.
- Unknown event kind raises `IPCError.unknownMessageKind`.
- AgentEvent and AgentResponse `kind` namespaces are distinct (cross-decode rejects).
- Wire-shape regression guard pinning exact byte layout.

Verified: ./script/test passes (build + 6 new tests + lint+format).

Refs ADR 0048 §12.6. Cross-references
docs/architecture/shell-integration.md "Shared model — agent + thin extension" (the push side of the agent ↔ extension stream).

body:
### Issues Fixed

Balena disk-image deploy for Raspberry Pi 4 was failing because the workflow targeted a non-existent fleet (`screenly_ose/anthias-pi4-64`).

### Description

The matrix board value (`pi4-64`) was interpolated directly into the balena fleet name in `balena preload` and `balena os configure`, producing `screenly_ose/anthias-pi4-64`. The actual fleet is `screenly_ose/anthias-pi4`.

Mapped each matrix board to an explicit `FLEET_SLUG` env var alongside the existing `BALENA_IMAGE` mapping. `pi4-64` now maps to `anthias-pi4`; the others (`pi2`, `pi3`, `pi5`) keep their current 1:1 names.

author: fred78290
body:
### Summary

Addresses memory leaks and improves resource management by breaking retain cycles, streamlining shared state observation, and refining object deallocation across core components.

### Motivation and Context

Previously, several components held strong references to `VirtualMachineDocument` instances and other view-related objects, leading to potential retain cycles and memory leaks when virtual machines were closed or the application state changed. This effort focuses on resolving these issues to ensure proper object deallocation and a more robust application lifecycle, especially as identified by the "fix-unclosed-documents" branch.

### Changes Made

- **Retain Cycle Prevention:**
    - Switched `NSVNCView`'s `connection`, `CPUUsageMonitor`'s `document`, `ExternalVirtualMachineView`'s `terminalView`, `InternalVirtualMachineView`'s `document`, and `VirtualMachineDocument`'s `vncView` to `weak` references to prevent strong reference cycles.
    - Added explicit `self.terminalView = nil` in `InteractiveShell.closeShell` for cleanup.
- **AppState Management Refinement:**
    - Transitioned `AppState` from being passed as `@Binding` or owned by `@State` in many views to being an `@ObservedObject` referencing a shared singleton (`AppState.shared`), simplifying state propagation and reducing ownership complexities.
    - Enforced `private(set)` for `AppState`'s `@Published` properties, centralizing state modification through dedicated internal `set` methods.
    - Improved `AppState`'s `closeVirtualMachineDocument` and `HomeView`'s `onReceive` logic to ensure `currentDocument` is properly reset upon document closure or state changes.
- **Navigation and UI Lifecycle:**
    - Refactored `NavigationModel` to centralize category selection logic in `newSelectedCategory` and introduced `resetSelections` for clearing UI state when `AppState` changes.
    - Changed `VirtualMachineView`'s `vm` property to a `@Binding` to allow parent views (`VirtualMachinesView`) to manage the document's ownership more effectively.
    - Updated `CakerMenuBarExtraScene` and `MainApp` to directly observe `AppState.shared`.
- **Debugging & Reliability:**
    - Introduced `#if DEBUG TrackDealloc` in key views (`CakerMenuBarExtraScene`, `HomeView`, `VirtualMachineView`, `VirtualMachinesView`) to assist in identifying and verifying object deallocation.
    - Simplified remote service connection logic in `ServiceListView` by making `checkIfServiceIsReachable` synchronous.
    - Corrected a typo in `ConsoleDevice.swift` ("binded" to "bound").

### Impact

- Significantly reduces the likelihood of memory leaks and improves memory footprint.
- Ensures more predictable and correct object deallocation, particularly for virtual machine instances and their associated UI.
- Enhances the overall stability and responsiveness of the application, especially during VM lifecycle events (start, stop, open, close).
- Simplifies state management within SwiftUI views by centralizing `AppState` observation.

### Testing

- Existing unit tests and manual UI testing confirmed proper VM lifecycle behavior.
- Debug deallocation tracking provided real-time feedback on object release.

### Release Notes

- Improved application stability and memory usage, especially when managing virtual machines.

author: copilot
body:
Alpine's SLURM constants were being injected via a generated local override config at dispatch time rather than living in the repo's `alpine` profile. Additionally, `store_dir` pointed to `/scratch/alpine/...` which is periodically purged, causing database re-downloads on every run.

## Changes

**`nextflow.config` — `alpine` profile:**
- Added `process.executor = 'slurm'`, `process.queueSize = 200`, `process.time = '24h'` (explicit time limit is required — Alpine's scheduler rejects jobs without one)
- Changed `params.store_dir` to `/projects/seda0001_amc/cmgd/store` (persistent path; old scratch path was being purged)
- Updated `singularity.runOptions` bind mount to match the new `store_dir`
- Removed stale `// process.executor = 'slurm'` comment

**`manifest.version`:** `1.4.0` → `1.5.0`

```groovy
alpine {
    process.executor  = 'slurm'
    process.queueSize = 200
    process.time      = '24h'
    params.store_dir  = '/projects/seda0001_amc/cmgd/store'
    singularity.runOptions = "--bind /projects/seda0001_amc/cmgd/store:/keep/store/"
    // ...
}
```

`process.clusterOptions` is intentionally omitted — it contains a runtime log path and is still injected by the dispatch system.

### Motivation
- Expose worker-facing endpoints to fetch assignment-specific details and to allow workers to pause or cancel their assignment without embedding module logic in the controller. 
- Return a unified `MobileBaseTaskDto` with the module-specific `TaskDetails` payload so clients receive a consistent contract for task details. 
- Route `pause`/`cancel` through the execution aggregator to keep module-specific behavior in providers rather than in controllers. 
- Keep existing module-unique endpoints (like `scan-pick`, `scan-place-bulk`, `report-missing`) in `OrderAssemblyController` unchanged.

### Description
- Added new endpoints to `WorkerTasksController`: `GET {taskId}/details?workerId=...`, `POST {taskId}/pause?workerId=...`, and `POST {taskId}/cancel?workerId=...`, and aligned error JSON to `{ Message = ... }` style used by `start/complete`.
- Extended `ITaskExecutionAggregator` with `PauseTaskAsync` and `CancelTaskAsync`, and implemented these in `TaskExecutionAggregator` to dispatch to the proper provider by `taskType`.
- Extended `ITaskExecutionProvider` with `TryPauseTaskAsync` and `TryCancelTaskAsync`, and implemented them in `OrderAssemblyExecutionProvider` to perform assignment pause/cancel operations.
- Added `GetTaskDetailsAsync(taskId, workerId)` to `TaskWorkloadAggregator` which aggregates provider `GetAvailableTasksAsync` results and returns a `MobileBaseTaskDto` (including `TaskDetails`).

- Attempted to run a build with `dotnet build TaskControl.sln -nologo`, but the container lacks the `dotnet` CLI, so compilation/automated tests could not be executed here.

author: nrohilla-fibonacci
body:
## Summary

Branch started as **WS1+WS2+WS3** (tier requirements, integrate.md, slim README) and grew through the design conversation into a full adoption-friction realignment plus a heavy browser-wizard polish pass. 17 commits, all addressing one theme: *make this toolkit easy to adopt without reading 1900 lines of docs*.

## What's in the PR

### Onboarding & docs
- **Tiered requirements** — `requirements-{core,db,runtime,drift,advanced}.txt`. New users do `pip install -r requirements-core.txt` (~50MB, no compile) and the full pipeline runs against SQLite. Heavy deps (LLM SDKs, drift_monitor, spaCy, Flask, Neptune) are opt-in. `pyproject.toml` extras realigned to match.
- **`docs/integrate.md`** — single-screen "5-minute SQLite path / 30-minute existing-DB path / what to ignore" guide.
- **README slimmed** to ~80 lines (onboarding + demos + doc index). 50-row capability matrix moves to `features.md` as a tiered map.
- **install.md cleaned** — pipeline-internal jargon (Phase 1, Phase 4, `--phase log/security/conflict`) gone from onboarding-facing sections.
- **`features.md` split into focused docs** under `docs/`: `artifacts.md`, `metadata.md`, `tmf.md`, `runtime.md`, `advanced.md`, `extending.md`. `features.md` becomes a ~95-line index.
- **Deleted** `gates.md` (governance scorecard auto-generated by `--phase test`; thresholds preserved as a 5-line subsection of `features.md`) and 6 obsolete root-level roadmap docs (~2,850 lines removed).
- **Browser wizard instructions** added to install.md §2 with runnable commands.

### Examples + housekeeping
- New `examples/wizard/` — Smart Building Operations demo end-to-end (7 entities + 5 events + 11 relationships + 8 CQs); proves the wizard is genuinely domain-agnostic.
- Test plan markdowns moved under `tests/` (root cleanup).
- All references updated: `MANIFEST.in`, `README.md`, `install.md`, `docs/integrate.md`, both test plans.

### Browser wizard polish
- **Template-picker fix** — `telecom/healthcare/finance/manufacturing/retail` were advertised but 404'd (loader only handled YAML). Now the wizard imports `INDUSTRY_TEMPLATES` from `onboard.py` and serves all 10 (5 builtin + 5 YAML).
- **Per-box help** — every wizard card across all 9 pages has a `box-help` block (what's shown / why it matters / how to read).
- **Relationships → Graph tab** — Neo4j-style force-directed view via vis-network (MIT, CDN). Entity/event nodes, drag-to-rearrange, zoom, fit. Reveals orphan entities and topology issues a flat list hides.
- **Compliance dashboard scoped to current domain** — each regulation now declares `applies_to`; healthcare projects see HIPAA + EU AI Act, finance sees Basel IV + EU AI Act, telecom sees Ofcom + EU AI Act. "Show all" toggle for multi-jurisdiction reviews.
- **Domain pill in step titles** — once a domain is selected, every step heading carries a small accent pill so users always know which project they're in.
- **Per-domain examples in Vector Retrieval** — clickable example chips with flavor + class expression + question + rationale, scoped per industry. Prefills the form on click.
- **Three themes** (Light / Dark / Mono) with persistent picker + system-pref default. vis-network re-themes via `_cssVar()` reads.
- **Sidebar nav** — consistent 1–9 numbering with an "After generation" divider between core flow and post-pipeline tools; font sizes bumped.
- **Pre-flight check + relocated Run Pipeline button** — the always-on "Run Pipeline" sidebar button became "Go to Generate →" (navigation only). Step 6 now has a Pre-flight checklist (required: domain name + entities; recommended: base IRI + CQs + events) with the actual run button disabled until required prereqs pass.

### Theme refresh
Two iterations to land on Linear/Vercel-style elevation: layered light surfaces, soft borders, lifted cards on hover, indigo accent (#4f46e5), Inter + JetBrains Mono, modal backdrop blur, custom scrollbars. All component CSS uses tokens, so adding a fourth theme is one `[data-theme="..."]` block.

### Future work tracked
- [#15](../issues/15) — wizard: connect-to-existing-database path on Step 1
- [#16](../issues/16) — wizard: import schema from .json or .sql file (with validation + comment extraction)

body:
## Summary
- Split `Metalama.Framework.DesignTime.Contracts` into a frozen v1 (original GUIDs) and a fresh v2 (rotated GUIDs) so Metalama 2026.0 and 2026.1 can coexist side-by-side in one VS extension; adds `IDesignTimeNotificationService` for cross-version pipeline notifications.
- Diagnoses the cross-binding scenario at two layers with rich exception messages: `TemplateDriver.InvokeTemplate` pre-flight and `SerializableTransitiveAspectInstance.ToAspectInstance` early guard.
- Anchors `TransitiveAspectsManifest.Deserialize` Door 1 (build-time `PortableExecutableReference`) to the upstream's `CompileTimeProject` looked up from `CompileTimeProjectRepository` by `AssemblyIdentity`.
- Adds `IUpstreamCompileTimeProjectProvider` so a downstream pipeline's `CompileTimeProjectRepository.Builder` reuses the upstream pipeline's already-built `CompileTimeProject` when the upstream is a `CompilationReference` at design time. Both pipelines then share the same physical projection, eliminating the welding-site mismatch where `IAspectClass.Type` and the live `IAspect` came from two different physical projections of the same logical upstream.

## Issues Fixed
- Closes #1605 - Add version-invariant notification contract in Metalama.Framework.DesignTime.Contracts
- Closes #1611 - Cross-pipeline mismatch: SerializableTransitiveAspectInstance welds A-typed aspect with B-typed AspectClass when upstream CT projection diverges between doors

### Motivation
- Unify common mobile workflows (list/details/start/pause/cancel/complete) behind a single `WorkerTasksController` to simplify client integration and centralize execution logic.
- Keep legacy `InventoryController` and `OrderAssemblyController` endpoints available during a transition period but mark them as deprecated to allow phased migration of mobile clients.
- Provide an explicit transitional behaviour that either proxies calls to the new aggregator paths or returns a deprecation warning header for visibility.
- Document the URL mapping and the plan to remove legacy endpoints in a later release after the mobile client migration completes.

### Description
- Marked legacy endpoints in `InventoryController` and `OrderAssemblyController` with `[Obsolete]` and added DEPRECATED notes to swagger XML summaries for each deprecated action.
- Added an `AddDeprecationWarning(string replacement)` helper in both `InventoryController` and `OrderAssemblyController` that sets `Warning: 299 - Deprecated API...` and `X-Api-Deprecated: true` response headers and invoked it from each deprecated endpoint.
- Extended `WorkerTasksController` to cover unified flows: `GET /{workerId}/pending`, `GET /{taskId}/details`, `POST /{taskId}/start`, `POST /{taskId}/pause`, `POST /{taskId}/cancel`, and `POST /{taskId}/complete`, and wired it to both inventory and assembly services (added `IInventoryProcessService` to constructor injection).
- Added `docs-api-migration.md` containing a legacy-to-unified URL mapping table and a short deletion plan for a separate removal release after client migration.

author: realbasirujallow
body:
## Summary
- Wires three more dashboard cards into the View Transitions API morph established in R41 (#65): **Budget Overview**, **Recent Transactions**, and **Upcoming Bills**. Tapping any of them flies the card into the matching KPI grid on the detail page rather than instant-navigating.
- Makes `HeroLink`'s \`heroName\` optional. When the link sits INSIDE a parent that already carries the source-side \`viewTransitionName\` (e.g. an outer card with two inline "Manage budgets →" links), setting the same name on the inner link creates a duplicate \`view-transition-name\` and the browser silently aborts the transition. Omitting it keeps the wrapped \`router.push\` while letting the parent own the morph target.

## Pattern
- **Source**: \`<div style={{ viewTransitionName: 'foo-hero' }}>\` on the outer card. Preserves all interactive content (progress bars, transaction rows) without forcing the whole card into a single Link.
- **Destination**: same \`viewTransitionName\` on the detail page's KPI grid — the visual mass that matches the source card.
- The named timing (320ms ease-out) was already wired in \`globals.css\` for budget-hero / bills-hero / transactions-hero in R41, so no CSS changes here.

## Test plan
- [x] \`npx tsc --noEmit\` clean
- [x] \`npx vitest run\` — 51/51 pass

author: sadatmalik
body:
This PR --
- Implements Spring Data JPA auditing for all candidate-provided data tables

**What was built**

- Introduced `AbstractCandidateDataDomainObject`, a new `@MappedSuperclass` that wires `@EntityListeners(AuditingEntityListener.class)` which declares the four audit fields (`createdBy`, `createdDate`, `updatedBy`, `updatedDate`) as Spring Data `@CreatedBy` / `@CreatedDate` / `@LastModifiedBy` / `@LastModifiedDate` properties
- All candidate-data entities now extend this class: `Candidate`, `CandidateAttachment`, `CandidateCertification`, `CandidateCitizenship`, `CandidateDependant`, `CandidateDestination`, `CandidateEducation`, `CandidateExam`, `CandidateJobExperience`, `CandidateLanguage`, `CandidateNote`, `CandidateOccupation`, `CandidateReviewStatusItem`, and the `@MappedSuperclass` bases `CandidateVisaCheckBase` and `CandidateVisaJobCheckBase` (covering `CandidateVisaCheck`, and `CandidateVisaJobCheck`)
- Added `JpaAuditingConfig` to enable `@EnableJpaAuditing` with a custom `AuditorAware` bean and `OffsetDateTime` provider
- Added Flyway migration `V2_12` to add the four audit columns to the tables that previously had none

**AuditorAware**

- Implemented `SpringSecurityAuditorAware` to supply the current auditor: returns the logged-in user for authenticated requests; falls back to the system admin for anonymous or system-triggered writes
- The fallback avoids loading the full system-admin `User` entity (which would trigger eager association fetches and cause a `JpaSystemException` during flush). Instead, `SystemAdminConfiguration` caches the system admin's ID at startup and the auditor returns a lightweight shell `User` carrying only that ID — sufficient for Hibernate to write the FK

**Service cleanup**

- Removed all manual `setAuditFields(...)` calls from the candidate service implementations now that the listener handles this automatically

**Tests**

- `CandidateDataAuditingIntegrationTest` covers create and update auditing for all entities, for both admin and candidate-user flows

author: harineko0
body:
## Summary
- Visiting `https://url.gdgs.jp/` while signed in on `account.gdgs.jp` redirected through `https://clerk.url.gdgs.jp/v1/client/handshake?...`, a hostname that doesn't resolve. Clerk derives the satellite FAPI host as `clerk.<domain>` when only `domain` is configured, but we never set up `clerk.url.gdgs.jp`.
- Replaces `domain` with `proxyUrl: https://url.gdgs.jp/__clerk` in tinyurl's `clerkMiddleware` and backend `AuthOptions`. Adds a same-origin proxy in the tinyurl Worker that forwards `/__clerk/*` to the existing `clerk.gdgs.jp` FAPI, strips `Domain=` from `Set-Cookie` so cookies bind to `url.gdgs.jp`, and rewrites upstream `Location: https://clerk.gdgs.jp/...` headers back to `https://url.gdgs.jp/__clerk/...` so the handshake chain stays inside the proxy.
- `auth-lib`'s `AuthOptions` gains a `proxyUrl?: string` field that's threaded into `client.authenticateRequest`.

## Out-of-repo follow-up (required before this is end-to-end)
- In Clerk Dashboard, set the `url.gdgs.jp` satellite's proxy URL to `https://url.gdgs.jp/__clerk`, otherwise primary-issued handshake URLs will still point at `clerk.url.gdgs.jp`.
- No DNS changes needed.

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` (all 4 workspaces)
- [x] `pnpm --filter @gdgjp/tinyurl test` (37/37)
- [x] `pnpm lint`
- [ ] After deploy + Dashboard config: signed-in user visiting `https://url.gdgs.jp/` lands on `/links` with no DevTools requests to `clerk.url.gdgs.jp`; the Clerk session cookie shows Domain `url.gdgs.jp`.
- [ ] Fresh incognito visit to `https://url.gdgs.jp/links` still redirects to the accounts signin form and, after sign-in, returns to `url.gdgs.jp/links`.

author: ianistor
body:
### Motivation
- Improve reliability and resource cleanup for the projects row auto-scrolling behavior and avoid duplicate initializations.
- Make scroll stepping behave more consistently across pointer types and ensure smooth integer pixel updates.
- Ensure event listeners and timers are removed when the page is hidden to prevent leaks and double intervals.

### Description
- Introduce a `projectsAutoScrollController` returned by `initProjectsAutoScroll()` with a `destroy()` method to encapsulate lifecycle and cleanup logic.
- Replace the previous `body.dataset` init-guard with the controller pattern and add `runProjectsAutoScroll()` / `stopProjectsAutoScroll()` to start/stop scrolling on `pageshow`/`pagehide` events.
- Convert anonymous handlers to named functions and register/remove them explicitly, and use `{ passive: true }` for touch/scroll listeners to improve performance.
- Adjust scroll stepping to use `Math.max(1, Math.round(stepPx))` and update `stepPx`/`intervalMs` values to smooth scrolling on coarse pointers; return `null` early when no row exists.

author: notcome
body:
## Summary

Adds HTTP-level WebSocket upgrade handshake support (RFC 6455 §4.2.2) to wuhu-serve.

## Changes

### New public API

- **`UpgradeResult`** enum — `.response(Response)` for normal HTTP, `.websocket` to request an upgrade
- **`Serve.serveUpgradable()`** — like `serve()` but the handler returns `UpgradeResult`; on `.websocket` it validates the upgrade headers, writes the 101 response, and **returns the raw connection** without closing it
- **`ServeError`** — two new cases: `.invalidUpgrade` and `.invalidWebSocketKey`

### Handshake validation

- `Upgrade: websocket` (case-insensitive)
- `Connection: Upgrade` (case-insensitive, contains "upgrade" token)
- `Sec-WebSocket-Key`: non-empty
- `Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13`
- Computes `Sec-WebSocket-Accept` via `base64(sha1(key + magic))`

### Tests (9 new)

- ✅ Successful upgrade path with known RFC 6455 test vector
- ✅ Missing `Upgrade` header → 400
- ✅ Wrong `Upgrade` value → 400
- ✅ Missing `Sec-WebSocket-Key` → 400
- ✅ Empty `Sec-WebSocket-Key` → 400
- ✅ Missing `Connection: Upgrade` → 400
- ✅ Wrong `Sec-WebSocket-Version` → 400
- ✅ Case-insensitive header handling
- ✅ Normal HTTP response via `serveUpgradable` (non-upgrade path)

## Verification

- `swift build` ✅
- `swift test` — all 49 tests pass (25 ServeTests including 9 new + existing suites) ✅

author: deniz-lgtm
body:
## Summary

Step 4 of Theme 1 schedule unification. Adds the **write half** of the unified `/api/deals/[id]/schedule` API.

## New routes

| Verb | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/api/deals/[id]/schedule` | Create a phase / milestone / task |
| `PATCH` | `/api/deals/[id]/schedule/[phaseId]` | Update an existing row |
| `DELETE` | `/api/deals/[id]/schedule/[phaseId]` | Remove a row |

All three use `requireDealEditAccess` (so view-only shares can't mutate) and the `[phaseId]` handlers use the deal-scoped `*InDeal` query variants from #150 — i.e. the URL's deal id constrains the WHERE clause, not just the auth check.

## POST validation

- `kind` ∈ `{phase, milestone, task}` (defaults to `'phase'`)
- `track` ∈ `{acquisition, development, construction}` (defaults to `'development'`)
- `label` required, non-empty
- When `parent_phase_id` is set, the row inherits the parent's track. Prevents a child task from dangling on a different track from its parent.

## Behind the scenes

- **`devPhaseQueries.create`** now accepts the unified-model columns directly: `kind`, `assignee_user_id`, `completed_at`, `source_legacy_*`. Eliminates the two-step insert that earlier WIP needed. `is_milestone` stays synced with `kind` for back-compat readers.

- **`devPhaseQueries.updateInDeal`** accepts the same new columns. Auto-stamps `completed_at` the first time a row transitions to `status='complete'` (existing completion timestamps are preserved). `is_milestone` follows `kind` on update so the two stay in lockstep.

- **`recomputeSchedule`** extracted to `src/lib/schedule-recompute.ts` so the GET/POST module and the `[phaseId]` PATCH/DELETE module can share it without route handlers importing each other's `route.ts` (which Next.js's route conventions don't love).

## Files

- `src/app/api/deals/[id]/schedule/route.ts` — POST handler added
- `src/app/api/deals/[id]/schedule/[phaseId]/route.ts` (new) — PATCH + DELETE
- `src/lib/schedule-recompute.ts` (new) — shared CPM recompute helper
- `src/lib/db.ts` — `devPhaseQueries.create`/`updateInDeal` accept the new columns

## Test plan

- [ ] `POST /api/deals/<id>/schedule { kind: "task", label: "Call title co", end_date: "2026-05-15" }` → 201 with the new row, `kind='task'`, `is_milestone=false`.
- [ ] `POST` with `kind: "milestone"` → row has `kind='milestone'` AND `is_milestone=true`, `duration_days=0`.
- [ ] `POST` with `parent_phase_id` of a development-track parent → new row inherits `track='development'`.
- [ ] `POST` with invalid `kind` or `track` → 400.
- [ ] `PATCH /api/deals/<id>/schedule/<phaseId> { status: "complete" }` → row updated, `completed_at` stamped to now, `pct_complete=100`.
- [ ] PATCH with `predecessor_id` that creates a cycle → 400, no mutation.
- [ ] PATCH on a phase id from a *different* deal → 404 (deal-scoped query).
- [ ] DELETE clears predecessor + parent links pointing at the row, then deletes it. CPM recomputes; downstream phases re-anchor.
- [ ] As a view-only share user, all three verbs return 403.

## Phase 1 sequencing

1. ✅ Schema columns + backfill (#153)
2. ✅ Legacy data migrated (#154)
3. ✅ Unified GET endpoint + Upcoming reads one source (#155)
4. ✅ **This PR** — POST/PATCH/DELETE on `/schedule`
5. Convert legacy `/milestones`, `/tasks` routes to compat wrappers (so the existing UI flows write into `deal_dev_phases` and surface in Upcoming)
6. Move legacy `deal_milestones`, `deal_tasks` to `_legacy` schema

body:
## Summary

Complete Telegram bot built with **Pyrogram** combining features from [SimpleCookie](https://github.com/QuasarRBX/SimpleCookie) and [MeowTool](https://github.com/h1kken/MeowTool) repos. Clean modular architecture with comprehensive Roblox cookie management capabilities.

### Features Implemented
- **Full Cookie Checker** — 40+ data points (Robux, RAP, billing, premium, email, 2FA, PIN, phone, rare items, badges, gamepasses, groups, friends, sessions, privacy settings, bundles, playtime, country, age verification, and more)
- **Game-Specific Checks** — 30+ Roblox games with badge/gamepass verification (Adopt Me, Blox Fruits, BedWars, MM2, Jailbreak, etc.)
- **Cookie Validator** — Bulk validity checking with concurrent threads
- **Cookie Refresher** — Mass cookie refresh via auth ticket method
- **Cookie Sorter** — Merge multiple files and deduplicate
- **Cookie Splitter** — Split into individual files (100 per file)
- **Proxy Manager** — Multi-protocol support (http/https/socks4/socks5), auto-rotation, bulk checker
- **Transaction Analysis** — Yearly + all-time donation tracking
- **VIP System** — Telegram Stars / CryptoBot USDT payments, priority queue
- **Referral System** — 3 bonus checks per referral
- **Admin Panel** — Ban/unban, broadcast, stats, proxy management, VIP grants, DM users
- **Configurable Settings** — Per-user toggle for each data point, output format (TXT/ZIP)
- **Queue System** — Priority-based (VIP > Regular) with progress tracking
- **Discord Webhooks** — Notification integration

### Architecture
```
rob_bot/
├── config.py          — Configuration & constants
├── database.py        — JSON-based user database
├── handlers/          — Telegram command/callback handlers
│   ├── start.py       — /start, menu, help
│   ├── cookie_check.py — Full cookie checking
│   ├── game_check.py  — Game-specific checks
│   ├── tools.py       — Validator, refresher, sorter, splitter, proxy, transactions
│   ├── profile.py     — Profile, settings, VIP, referral
│   └── admin.py       — Admin commands
├── utils/             — Core utilities
│   ├── roblox_api.py  — 30+ Roblox API endpoints
│   ├── proxy_manager.py — Proxy loading, rotation, checking
│   ├── cookie_tools.py — Bulk operations & result formatting
│   └── helpers.py     — Formatting, Discord webhook
└── plugins/           — Queue & VIP systems
    ├── queue.py       — Priority queue
    └── vip.py         — VIP & CryptoBot payments
```

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human
- [ ] Set up `.env` with your API_ID, API_HASH, BOT_TOKEN, and ADMINS (copy from `.env.example`)
- [ ] Run `pip install -r requirements.txt` and `python main.py` to verify bot starts
- [ ] Test the `/start` command and menu navigation in Telegram
- [ ] Upload a `.txt` file with cookies to test the cookie check flow
- [ ] Test admin commands (`/ban`, `/stats`, `/broadcast`) with your admin ID

### Notes
- The bot requires Telegram API credentials (API_ID, API_HASH from my.telegram.org) and a bot token from @BotFather
- All user data is stored as JSON files in `data/users/` (gitignored)
- Proxy support is optional — the bot works without proxies but rate limits may apply
- CryptoBot payments require a separate API key from @CryptoBot

🚀 Pull Request: GitHub Actions — Staging Deploy Pipeline
🎯 Objetivo
Implementar a infraestrutura de automação para o ambiente de Staging, garantindo que todas as atualizações na branch developer passem por um processo rigoroso de teste, build e armazenamento de artefatos.

🛠️ O que foi implementado?

1. Workflow de Entrega Contínua (staging-deploy.yml)
Criação do pipeline automatizado que gerencia tanto o Backend quanto o Frontend.
Gatilho configurado para a branch developer (com suporte a execução manual via workflow_dispatch).

2. Backend (Docker & CI)
Garantia de Qualidade: Execução automatizada de testes com pytest antes da geração do build.
Containerização: Geração da imagem Docker via backend/Dockerfile.
GitHub Container Registry (GHCR): Armazenamento da imagem no registro oficial do GitHub com a tag :staging, permitindo que qualquer servidor puxe a versão mais estável.

3. Frontend (Flutter Web)
Compilação Automatizada: Setup do Flutter e build da versão Web (release).
Gestão de Artefatos: O build final é disponibilizado como um artefato do GitHub Actions para download imediato, facilitando a validação por parte do time de produto/design.

4. Preparação para o Deploy Final
A estrutura foi desenhada para ser "plug-and-play": assim que o servidor de hospedagem for definido, o pipeline está pronto para realizar o deploy final via SSH ou Webhook.

✅ Verificação Técnica
O build do Flutter Web foi testado localmente e finalizado com sucesso (Built build\web), garantindo que a árvore de dependências e o código atual estão íntegros para o ambiente de staging.

📋 Requisitos para Ativação (Manual no GitHub)
Secrets: Adicionar OPENAI_API_KEY nas configurações de Secrets do repositório.
Permissions: Em Settings > Actions > General, garantir que a opção "Read and write permissions" esteja ativada para permitir o push para o GHCR.

## Summary
- Verifies the surrogate-driven Stage 06G strict-score recipes against the v2 frozen-OP physics via FD, refreshes the surrogate with **2,900 new FD rows + 17 06E disagreement rows**, and reports both FD acceptance and the rescore behaviour of the new surrogate.
- Five parts:
  | Part | Scope | Runs |
  |---|---|---|
  | 1 | top-100 06G nominal FD | 100 |
  | 2 | top-10 06G FD MC, 100 variations each | 1,000 |
  | 3 | 6 representatives FD MC, 300 variations each | 1,800 |
  | 4 | surrogate refresh on 06C ∪ 06E disagreement ∪ 06H FD = 8,311-row train pool (04C 1,074 holdout removed) | — |
  | 5 | re-score 06G top-100 with the new 06H surrogate | — |
- Policy preserved: `v2_OP_frozen=true`, `published_data_loaded=false`, `external_calibration=none`. Closed Stage 04C / 04D / 06C joblibs and label datasets are untouched.

## Surrogate-vs-FD on 06G top-100 nominal
| | |
|---|---|
| Spearman strict_score | **+0.110** (≥ 0 → spec 1 PASS) |
| Spearman LER | +0.646 |
| Spearman CD_error | +0.033 |
| CD_fixed MAE / RMSE | 0.694 / 0.877 nm (n=100) |
| LER_locked MAE / RMSE | 0.029 / 0.035 nm (n=100) |
| P_line_margin MAE / RMSE | 0.025 / 0.030 (n=100) |
| top-1 / 3 / 5 / 10 overlap | 0/1, 0/3, 0/5, 1/10 |

## 06G top-10 FD MC + 6 representatives × 300 MC FD
- 10 / 10 with `robust_prob ≥ 0.99` (spec 3 PASS)
- 4 / 10 with `strict_pass_prob ≥ 0.5`
- Spearman strict_score MC: **−0.370** (saturation anti-corr — same artefact as 06E)

| rep_kind | recipe_id | robust_prob | **strict_pass_prob** | std_CD | std_LER |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **margin-best** | G_4299 | 1.000 | **0.467** | 0.395 | 0.018 |
| strict-best | G_3691 | 1.000 | 0.430 | 0.491 | 0.018 |
| balanced-best | G_1226 | 1.000 | 0.297 | 0.413 | 0.019 |

All six are FD-robust (`robust_prob = 1.0`). **margin-best (G_4299)** wins on stability (highest probability of also clearing the strict CD ±0.5 nm / LER ≤ 3.0 nm at FD level) — slightly above strict-best. CD-best is excellent at the nominal point but loses MC stability because the CD_error mean sits close to the strict tolerance.

## 06H surrogate refresh metrics (test = 04C 1,074 holdout rows)

|---|---|
| classifier balanced_acc | 0.691 |

## Summary

- Ersetzt EWMA (`ewm(alpha=1/period)`) durch Wilder's ursprünglichen Algorithmus: SMA-Seed über die ersten `period` Differenzen, danach rekursive Glättung `avg_new = (avg_old * (n-1) + x) / n`
- Für `period=2` (RSI2-Strategie) sind beide Methoden mathematisch identisch — keine Verhaltensänderung für bestehende Strategien
- Für `period>2` (z.B. Standard-RSI14) liefert Wilder's korrektere Initialisierung, da EWMA den ersten Beobachtungswert als Seed nutzt statt des SMA

- Zu kurze Serien (`n <= period`) geben sofort `[NaN] * n` zurück

**`tests/test_rsi_regression.py`**

body: ## Summary Fixes the issue where nothing happens after signing in with Google — the page stays stuck on the sign-in screen. **Root cause:** `signInWithRedirect` silently fails in modern browsers (Chrome, Safari, Firefox) due to third-party cookie/storage restrictions. After the Google redirect completes, `getRedirectResult` returns `null` and `onAuthStateChanged` never fires with a user. **Fix:** Switched to `signInWithPopup`, which uses a popup window instead of a full-page redirect, avoiding the cross-origin storage issue entirely. Changes in `JunkLister-4.html`: - Replaced `signInWithRedirect` + `getRedirectResult` imports with `signInWithPopup` - Removed the "Checking sign-in…" loading spinner on page load (no longer needed without redirect flow) - Simplified the sign-in button handler to use popup auth - Added `esc()` helper to HTML-escape Firestore data before `innerHTML` insertion (XSS fix) - Fixed blob URL memory leak in image picker preview - Fixed stale spinner showing after sign-out (call `setGateLoading(false)` on sign-out) - Added `selectedIds` pruning after Firestore snapshot to prevent stale selection counts ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] Open `JunkLister-4.html` in Chrome — click "Continue with Google" and verify a popup opens, you can sign in, and the app loads after sign-in - [ ] Test in Safari — verify the same popup flow works (this was the browser most affected by the redirect issue) - [ ] Verify sign-out works correctly and the button restores to "Continue with Google" ### Notes - The popup approach may be blocked by aggressive popup blockers; if so, users will see an error message in the UI rather than a silent failure - The existing modular app code in `src/` already uses `signInWithPopup` and is unaffected by this change - Storing base64 data URLs directly in Firestore (pre-existing design) risks exceeding the 1 MiB document limit — this is out of scope for this PR but worth addressing in a future refactor Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/a162d5f6d91048f390f9b4b883ae93dd Requested by: @optobath-creator ---

body:
Re-opened (PR #44 closed when its base branch was deleted by the squash-merge of #43).

When DAPPS gives up on a message — TTL expired in queue, etc. — the row was hard-deleted and the operator had no way to see what got thrown away. New shape: messages soft-delete into a dedicated `dropped_messages` table and surface in the dashboard.

## What landed

- **`DbDroppedMessage`** — new table mirroring `DbMessage` plus `DroppedAt` and `Reason`.
- **`Database.SoftDeleteMessage(id, reason)`** — copies row across, hard-deletes from `messages`. Idempotent on a missing row.
- **`Database.GetRecentDroppedMessages(limit)`** — newest-first.

**Drop sites switched**:
- `OutboundMessageManager.DoRun` TTL drop → `SoftDeleteMessage(id, "ttl-expired")`.
- `TtlSweeperService → Database.DeleteExpired` — messages soft-delete; offers still hard-delete (protocol scaffolding, no audit value).

**Surface**: `GET /Events/dropped` (cookie-authed JSON, 50 most recent) and a dashboard "Recently dropped" panel above the SSE feed (id, destination, source, bytes, ttl, lifetime, drop time, reason pill). Polled every 5s with the same DOM-swap pattern as queue/health.

## Tests

`SoftDeleteTests` — 4 unit tests (move-with-reason, missing-row no-op, GetRecent newest-first + limit, DeleteExpired soft-delete path). Existing fixtures got `CreateTable<DbDroppedMessage>()` added alongside `CreateTable<DbMessage>()`.

**287 tests pass** (was 283; +4).

author: trek-e
body:
## Enhancement PR

## Linked Issue

Closes #2955

> Linked issue has the `approved-enhancement` label ✅

---

## What this enhancement improves

Patch-release flow: `.github/workflows/hotfix.yml` (canonical) and `.github/workflows/release-sdk.yml` (active stopgap while `@gsd-build/sdk` token is unavailable).

## Before / After

**Before:**
- `hotfix.yml create` only branched + bumped version. Operator had to manually cherry-pick every fix from main — no audit trail.
- `hotfix.yml finalize` published via plain `npm publish`: no `install-smoke` gate, no `sdk-bundle/gsd-sdk.tgz` (so a hotfix tarball was missing the recoverable SDK artifact every other release ships with), `next` re-point swallowed errors.
- `release-sdk.yml` had no hotfix capability — the active publish path could not ship a patch release at all.

**After:**
- A hotfix `vX.YY.Z` is defined as: everything in `vX.YY.{Z-1}` plus every `fix:`/`chore:` commit on `main` since that base. Each tag becomes the next hotfix's anchor — `git cherry $BASE_TAG main` reveals exactly the unshipped delta, so cycles are self-documenting.
- `hotfix.yml create` auto-cherry-picks `fix:`/`chore:` from `main` (oldest-first, patch-equivalents skipped via `git cherry`, `feat:`/`refactor:` excluded, conflicts halt with the offending SHA, summary lists every included SHA).
- `hotfix.yml finalize` runs `install-smoke` cross-platform gate, bundles `sdk-bundle/gsd-sdk.tgz`, hardens the `next` re-point, adds `--latest` to `gh release create`. SDK `package.json` bumped in lockstep with CC.
- `release-sdk.yml` gains `action: publish | hotfix` + `auto_cherry_pick` boolean. New `prepare` job runs same cherry-pick logic; `install-smoke` and `release` consume its output ref. Idempotent — if `hotfix/X.YY.Z` already exists from `hotfix.yml create`, prepare reuses it and the cherry-pick is a no-op.

## How it was implemented

- `.github/workflows/hotfix.yml` — added `auto_cherry_pick` input, cherry-pick step in `create`, lockstep SDK version bump, `install-smoke` reusable-workflow `needs:` for `finalize`, mirrored `release-sdk.yml`'s SDK-bundle pipeline (build → pack → bundle → whitelist injection → tarball verification).
- `.github/workflows/release-sdk.yml` — added `action`, `auto_cherry_pick` inputs; new `prepare` job (validates patch version, branches from `BASE_TAG`, cherry-picks, bumps version, pushes); rewired `install-smoke` and `release` to consume `prepare.outputs.ref`; hotfix mode forces dist-tag `latest` and opens merge-back PR.
- `VERSIONING.md` — patch-release section rewritten to document the cumulative-tag invariant and both workflow paths.

Conventional-commit filter (shared between both workflows): `^(fix|chore)(\([^)]+\))?!?: ` — handles optional scopes and the `!` breaking marker.

## Testing

### How I verified the enhancement works

- `python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(...)"` on both workflow YAMLs — parses clean.
- Manually traced the cherry-pick logic against representative `git log` ranges: `BASE_TAG=v1.27.0`, `target=1.27.1` correctly resolves to highest `v1.27.*` < `v1.27.1`. The `git cherry HEAD origin/main | awk '/^\+/'` filter then `grep -F` against `git log --reverse` gives oldest-first ordering.
- Idempotency: if `hotfix/X.YY.Z` already exists on origin, `prepare` checks it out; `git cherry HEAD origin/main` then returns nothing (everything already applied or patch-equivalent), so the cherry-pick step no-ops.
- Conflict path: cherry-pick failure aborts via `git cherry-pick --abort` and `exit 1` with `::error::` annotation including the offending SHA.

### Platforms tested

- [x] N/A (workflow YAML — runs on `ubuntu-latest`; install-smoke matrix already covers macOS/Windows/Linux)

### Runtimes tested

- [x] N/A (release-process change, not runtime-specific)

---

## Scope confirmation

- [x] The implementation matches the scope approved in the linked issue — no additions or removals
- [x] If scope changed during implementation, I updated the issue and got re-approval before continuing

---

## Checklist

- [x] Issue linked above with `Closes #2955`
- [x] Linked issue has the `approved-enhancement` label
- [x] Changes are scoped to the approved enhancement — nothing extra included
- [x] All existing tests pass (`npm test`) — workflow YAML only, no source changes
- [x] New or updated tests cover the enhanced behavior — N/A, workflow YAML; verified via YAML parse + manual trace of the cherry-pick logic against representative git ranges
- [ ] CHANGELOG.md updated
- [x] Documentation updated if behavior or output changed — `VERSIONING.md` patch-release section rewritten
- [x] No unnecessary dependencies added

## Breaking changes

None. `release-sdk.yml`'s `tag` input changed from `required: true` to `required: false` with `default: latest` — pre-existing operator invocations that always passed `tag` continue to work. The new `action` input defaults to `publish` so existing dispatches behave identically.
