author: dhaern
body:
## Summary

This PR improves the Grok Web executor so it behaves more reliably in OpenAI-compatible tool-calling environments.

The implementation is based on observed Grok Web behavior from real traffic captures, including structured `toolUsageCard` events, reasoning fields, render cards, and streaming payloads. The goal is not to emulate Grok Web perfectly, but to make OmniRoute's Grok Web integration more stable and extensible.

Further improvements and corrections are welcome, especially from anyone with additional Grok Web traces or provider-specific edge cases.

## What changed

### Tool calling

- Add support for caller-runtime tools through a transient `CLIENT_TOOLS` manifest.
- Keep the manifest ephemeral: it is only sent to Grok Web for the current request and is not persisted in chat history.
- Preserve explicit `<tool_call>{"name":"...","arguments":{...}}</tool_call>` calls from Grok and validate them against the actual `body.tools` list.
- Respect explicit `tool_choice` by exposing only the forced tool in the manifest.
- Sort client tools dynamically using generic capability signals from tool names, descriptions, and schemas.
- Prefer direct user-facing tools over meta/infrastructure tools by default.
- Avoid selecting memory/context tools for public web search intent.
- Keep context/memory tools available and prioritize them only when the request explicitly asks for context, memory, or history.
- Track completed tool calls only within the current user turn to avoid blocking fresh repeated requests in later turns.
- Avoid repeated equivalent tool calls within the same turn while still allowing different tools to run in a chain.

### Native Grok tool bridge

- Preserve Grok Web native `toolUsageCard` support as a conservative bridge.
- Map observed native Grok tool intents to compatible caller-runtime tools when possible:
  - `webSearch` → public web search, unless the user explicitly asks to fetch/read a URL-like target;
  - `browsePage` → URL/page fetch;
  - `readFile` → compatible caller file-read tools;
  - `bash` → compatible caller shell/terminal tools.
- Harden native bridge scoring so web search does not resolve to context/memory tools.
- Avoid mapping native shell/read/search signals to unrelated infrastructure tools.
- Preserve explicit tool-call arguments, while normalizing native Grok metadata through the destination tool schema.
- Handle URL-like fetch requests conservatively, including bare domains, `www.` domains, HTTP URLs, trailing punctuation, and websocket URLs as a negative case.

### Prompt/context handling

- Move the transient tool manifest close to the decision point so Grok sees the caller-runtime tool interface immediately before choosing tools.
- Strip injected runtime reminders such as `<internal_reminder>...</internal_reminder>` from the prompt sent to Grok Web.
- Forward current-turn tool results back to Grok in a structured way.
- Keep old tool results from earlier user turns from suppressing new tool calls.

### Streaming and parsing

- Parse Grok structured reasoning separately from visible assistant content.
- Route `isThinking` / structured reasoning fields to `reasoning_content`.
- Suppress noisy generic thinking headers.
- Avoid emitting `raw_function_result` and internal Grok render/tool cards as final assistant content.
- Improve streaming markup filtering across chunk boundaries.
- Avoid prematurely flushing partial `<tool_call>` markup in streamed responses.

### Tests

Adds and updates focused unit coverage for:

- Grok Web executor registration and model mapping;
- structured reasoning extraction;
- native `toolUsageCard` mapping;
- arbitrary client tool calls via manifest markup;
- current-turn completed tool-call dedupe;
- dynamic client-tool ordering;
- context/memory vs public-web tool ranking;
- explicit `tool_choice`;
- URL-like fetch routing;
- internal reminder stripping;
- streaming markup filtering.

## Notes

This is an incremental hardening pass based on observed Grok Web behavior. It improves the current executor significantly, but Grok Web's private protocol may still change or expose additional edge cases. Follow-up fixes and simplifications are welcome.

## Validation

```bash
node --import tsx/esm --test tests/unit/grok-web.test.ts
npm run typecheck:core
npm run typecheck:noimplicit:core
git diff --check
```

All checks pass locally.

author: sburdges-eng
body:
## Summary

Phase 3 inventory closed-loop receiving (S, internal-only, no external deps).
Accepted deliveries with a captured `received_qty` + `received_unit` now also
write an `inventory_updates` row in the **same transaction** as the
`receiving_log` INSERT, so on-hand stays in sync with the back-door truck and
COGS% becomes trustworthy.

The closed loop is **opt-in per row** — bare-form deliveries with no qty
captured behave exactly as before; the receiving row still lands.

## Schema delta

`receiving_log` gains two columns via `migrateLegacyColumns()`:

| col | type | nullable | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `received_qty` | REAL | yes | quantity actually received; >0 when present |
| `received_unit` | TEXT | yes | freeform unit string (lb / case / ea / gal / ...) |

Both NULLable so pre-Phase-3 rows + opt-out rows remain valid. Both added to
`assertCriticalSchemas` so a partial deploy fails loudly at init.

## API contract — `POST /api/receiving`

New optional body fields: `received_qty` (number) and `received_unit` (string).

Behavior matrix (status comes from existing rule module):

| status | qty present + valid | unit present + valid | item present | inventory_updates written? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| accepted | yes | yes | yes | **yes** (direction=`in`, delta=`"${qty} ${unit}"`) |
| accepted_with_note | yes | yes | yes | **yes** |
| rejected | yes | yes | yes | no (product not in building) |
| any | no | no | any | no (graceful skip) |
| any | qty only / unit only | (mismatch) | any | **400** |
| any | qty <= 0 | yes | yes | **400** |

When the closed-loop write fires it emits a paired `audit_events` row with
`entity='inventory_updates'`, `actor_source='receiving_closed_loop'`,
`note='receiving_log:<id>'`. If either the inventory INSERT or its audit row
fails (e.g. table missing on a partial deploy), the **entire transaction
rolls back** — no ghost-delivery + drifted-on-hand state. Caller sees a 500.

Validator extension: new `closed_loop_error: string | null` field on
`ValidateReceivingResult` (range-checks qty/unit). Surfaced as 400 — distinct
from 422 `needs_corrective_action` which is reserved for HACCP rule decisions.

## UI

Two optional fields added to `ReceivingBoard`:
- `How much?` — number input, blank-friendly
- `Unit` — text input with datalist suggesting `lb / case / ea / gal / oz / kg`

Kitchen-voice copy per `docs/UI_COPY_RULES.md` (no jargon, optional, both blank → server skips closed loop).

## Test counts

- `tests/js/test-receiving-api.mjs`: **32 pass** (23 existing + 9 new)
- New cases:
  1. happy path: accepted + qty + unit writes BOTH rows + 2 audits
  2. accepted_with_note + qty + unit also credits
  3. rejected + qty + unit does NOT credit (status, audit, counts)
  4. accepted without qty/unit — graceful skip
  5. accepted with qty but no unit → 400
  6. accepted with item missing → graceful skip
  7. validator rejects negative qty as 400
  8. validator rejects zero qty as 400
  9. transactional rollback: forced inventory_updates DROP mid-test → receiving_log + audit rows roll back
- `npm run test:rules` — 370 pass
- `npm run test:schema` — 45 pass
- `npm run typecheck` — clean

## Test plan

- [ ] CI runs `test-receiving-api.mjs`, `test:rules`, `test:schema`, `typecheck`
- [ ] Smoke: open `/food-safety/receiving`, log a real delivery with qty+unit, confirm a fresh row in `inventory_updates` paired by note
- [ ] Smoke: log a delivery WITHOUT qty/unit, confirm no `inventory_updates` row (graceful skip)
- [ ] Smoke: log a rejected delivery WITH qty/unit, confirm no inventory credit
- [ ] Run `npx gitnexus analyze` to refresh the knowledge graph (index is stale, additive change so impact is bounded but worth re-indexing)

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Adds new DB columns and a transactional write path that inserts into `inventory_updates` alongside `receiving_log`, which could impact data integrity if schema/migrations or validation gates are wrong. Risk is contained by opt-in fields, schema-drift checks, and expanded tests, but it touches persistence and inventory accounting.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds *closed-loop receiving*: `POST /api/receiving` now accepts optional `received_qty` + `received_unit` and, for accepted/accepted-with-note lines with an `item`, writes a matching `inventory_updates` credit **in the same DB transaction** (with a paired audit event).
> 
> Extends the receiving validator to type/range-check the new qty/unit fields via `closed_loop_error` (surfaced as HTTP 400) and adjusts route decision ordering so HACCP rejections still return 422 for missing corrective notes. Updates schema/migrations to add `received_qty`/`received_unit` on `receiving_log`, adds `inventory_updates.receiving_log_id` with a partial unique index to prevent double-crediting per source row, updates the UI form to capture qty/unit, and adds comprehensive API/rules tests for crediting, skip/400 cases, and rollback behavior.
>

author: cyberdogs7
body:
Fixes a severe UI lag issue caused by frequent, global React re-renders.

### Issue
The task list in the War Room (and other dragging/scrolling operations) felt very laggy. This was traced to a `setInterval` in `App.jsx` that updated the `currentTime` state every second for the top navigation bar's live clock. Because the state lived in the root `App` component, the entire React component tree was forced to re-render every second, interrupting drag operations and bogging down the main thread.

### Solution
- Created `src/components/AppLiveClock.jsx` to encapsulate the clock's `Date` state and `setInterval` logic.
- Removed the `currentTime` state and interval from `src/App.jsx`.
- Imported and rendered `<AppLiveClock />` in place of the inline clock JSX.

This change isolates the per-second rendering cycle strictly to the clock component itself, completely eliminating the global re-renders and restoring smooth performance to the rest of the application.

author: vscarpenter
body:
Phase 2 of the redesign per [`tasks/redesign-plan.md`](tasks/redesign-plan.md) and the new [ADR-0012](docs/adr/0012-redesign-color-system.md). Flips the saturated quadrant palette to muted earth tones and cascades the swap to every consuming surface (matrix, dashboard donut, time-analytics chart, command-palette chips, about-page illustration, brand mark).

> **Heads-up before review:** there is one known WCAG AA contrast regression — four light-mode quadrant labels at 11px bold. **Resolution is Phase 5 (quadrant header redesign).** I'd like your call on the resolution before I start Phase 5 — see "Open question" below.

## Summary

| Token | Old | New | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--quadrant-accent-q1` | orange `#c2410c` | sage `#7A8B7E` | Do First — calm, not alarming |
| `--quadrant-accent-q2` | blue `#1d4ed8` | dusty blue `#7B8FA3` | Schedule |
| `--quadrant-accent-q3` | green `#15803d` | warm taupe `#9D8B7A` | Delegate |
| `--quadrant-accent-q4` | ochre `#854d0e` | slate gray `#8A8C8E` | Eliminate |
| `--accent` | indigo `#4338ca` | muted indigo `#5B6B8F` | Primary actions |
| `--foreground-muted` | cool gray `#71717a` | warm gray `#6B6865` | Body secondary |
| `--card-background` | `#fbfaf6` | `#FEFDFB` | Slight lift |
| `--terracotta` | (new) | `#A86F5F` | Warning / overdue |
| `--border-strong` | (new) | `#D5D2CC` | Elevated surfaces |

Skipped tokens whose channel deltas were < 3/255 (imperceptible) — see ADR-0012 §Decision.

## Cascade

- `components/dashboard/quadrant-distribution.tsx` — donut Cell fills now driven by `quadrantAccent('q1'..'q4')`
- `components/dashboard/time-analytics.tsx` — quadrant bar fills via helper
- `components/command-palette/task-item.tsx` — quadrant badge chips via helper
- `components/about/matrix-section.tsx` — illustration uses `borderColor: quadrantAccent(rdKey, 0.4)`, `backgroundColor: quadrantAccent(rdKey, 0.05)`
- `components/matrix-simplified/index.tsx` — overdue caption color: `#c2410c` → `rgb(var(--terracotta))`

## Two logo variants — pick one

Both shipped in [`components/gsd-logo.tsx`](components/gsd-logo.tsx):

- **`GsdLogo` (Variant A, default)** — Mosaic. Same 4-square layout reskinned to the new palette via tokens. Q1 (sage) is solid; others at 0.32 opacity. Preserves the multi-color identity.
- **`GsdLogoMonochrome` (Variant B)** — Duotone. Three squares in foreground at 0.20 opacity + Q1 in `--accent` (muted indigo). Reads as a single editorial mark.

To switch: change `<GsdLogo />` to `<GsdLogoMonochrome />` inside `GsdLogoLockup`. Try both locally and tell me which.

## Verification

Done locally on the dev server, light + dark mode, via in-page DOM contrast probe (CSP blocks CDN axe-core; in-page calculator stands in).

### Light mode — only the four quadrant labels fail AA

| Element | fs/wt | Ratio | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q1 label "DO FIRST" sage on canvas | 11/700 | **3.31:1** | fail AA normal, pass AA Large |
| Q2 label "SCHEDULE" dusty on canvas | 11/700 | **3.06:1** | fail AA normal, pass AA Large |
| Q3 label "DELEGATE" taupe on canvas | 11/700 | **3.00:1** | fail AA normal, pass AA Large (boundary) |
| Q4 label "ELIMINATE" slate on canvas | 11/700 | **3.09:1** | fail AA normal, pass AA Large |
| Quadrant hint text | 12/400 | 5.07:1 | pass |
| Quadrant count badge | 11/500 | 4.73:1 | pass |
| Empty state italic | 14/400 | 5.07:1 | pass |
| Task card title | 15/600 | 17.43:1 | pass |
| Capture bar input | 14.5/400 | 17.43:1 | pass |
| Add button (white on accent) | 13/500 | 16.24:1 | pass |

11px bold doesn't qualify as "AA Large" under WCAG (need ≥18.6px or ≥14pt-bold), so AA normal (4.5:1) applies — and they fail it.

### Dark mode — all clean

| Element | Ratio |
|---|---|
| Q1 label sage | 5.42:1 |
| Q2 label dusty blue | 5.87:1 |
| Q3 label warm taupe | 5.97:1 |
| Q4 label slate gray | 5.79:1 |
| Hint text | 7.63:1 |
| Task title | 16.74:1 |

The advisor's "copy light into dark, axe-drive derivations" call paid off — no dark-specific quadrant variants needed.

## Open question — resolve before I start Phase 5

How do you want the four light-mode quadrant labels treated?

- **(α) Honor the spec.** Keep accent-colored labels at 11px bold; accept the AA-normal fail. Spec example (§5 of `GSD_REDESIGN_INSTRUCTIONS.md`) explicitly shows accent-colored label text. Quadrant title is also exposed via `aria-label` on the section, so screen readers aren't affected.
- **(β) Bump to AA Large.** Switch labels to ≥18.6px (e.g., `text-base font-bold`) — qualifies for the 3:1 threshold and would pass. Trades visual hierarchy (labels become more prominent than spec wants).
- **(γ) Two-color treatment** (my default proposal). Deep charcoal text + accent-colored dot prefix. Restores AA normal contrast cleanly, keeps quadrant identity, doesn't bulk up typography.

Recommendation: **γ**. Documented in ADR-0012 §"Open question for the user".

## Test plan

- [x] `bun typecheck` clean
- [x] `bun lint` — 0 errors (5 pre-existing warnings unchanged)
- [x] `bun run test` — 1,789 / 1,795 pass (6 pre-existing failures unchanged from main)
- [x] Dev server smoke (light + dark): `/`, `/dashboard`, `/about`
- [x] Contrast measurements via in-page DOM probe (see Verification table)

Manual smoke (recommended before merge):
- [ ] Pull branch, `bun dev`, eyeball matrix + dashboard + about in light + dark
- [ ] Try both logo variants — flip `GsdLogo` ↔ `GsdLogoMonochrome` in `GsdLogoLockup`, decide
- [ ] Decide α/β/γ on the quadrant label question

## Follow-up

Phases 3–7 of `tasks/redesign-plan.md` ship in subsequent PRs:
- Phase 3: capture bar elevation (sticky desktop, lifted bg, Zap icon, solid Add)
- Phase 4: unified matrix container (one outer border, gap-3, divider)
- Phase 5: quadrant header redesign (resolves the AA fail per α/β/γ)
- Phase 6: task card typography + accent checkboxes + terracotta overdue
- Phase 7: icon stroke weights + final spacing pass + WCAG sweep

Version: 8.8.3 → 8.9.0 (minor — visible identity change).

author: davysn-cloud
body:
## Summary

This PR implements automatic provisioning of a minimal agency setup when new users sign up, preventing the dashboard from getting stuck in a loading state with `currentAgencyId=null`. It also adds robust error handling and recovery mechanisms for stale authentication tokens from previous Supabase projects.

## Key Changes

**Database Migration (00024_handle_new_user_trigger.sql)**
- Creates a `handle_new_user()` trigger function that automatically provisions:
  - An agency (with customizable name/slug from signup metadata)
  - An agency member record with owner role
  - A default workspace ("Primeira marca")
  - A workspace member record
  - A brand profile for the workspace
- Includes a backfill script to provision setup for existing users who lack agencies

**Onboarding Flow (OnboardingPage.tsx)**
- Adds `persistStep()` function to update agency/workspace data as user progresses through onboarding
- Step 1: Updates the auto-created agency name and slug based on user input
- Step 2: Updates the default workspace with client name/handle and upserts brand profile with Instagram handle
- Adds loading state (`saving`) to prevent multiple submissions during persistence
- Gracefully handles persistence failures without blocking onboarding completion

**Auth Store Improvements (useAuthStore.ts)**
- Adds 8-second safety timeout in `initialize()` to prevent spinner from hanging indefinitely
- Validates session on startup and detects stale tokens from previous Supabase projects
- Implements server-side token verification via `getUser()` when agencies list is empty
- Handles `TOKEN_REFRESHED` and `SIGNED_OUT` events to clear state appropriately
- Adds 1-second delay after signup to allow trigger to create agency before fetching
- Uses in-memory user ID instead of `getUser()` in `fetchAgencies()` to avoid network calls with stale tokens
- Adds error logging and graceful fallbacks throughout

**Dashboard & Auth Guard (DashboardPage.tsx, AuthGuard.tsx)**
- Adds `NoAgencyState` component with retry and session-clearing options for users without agencies
- Shows helpful troubleshooting instructions including migration execution steps
- AuthGuard displays warning after 6 seconds of loading with option to clear session and restart login
- Prevents dashboard from showing "Carregando..." indefinitely when agency is missing

## Notable Implementation Details

- Slug generation uses timestamp + random suffix to ensure uniqueness without collisions
- Metadata (agency_name, agency_slug, display_name) can be passed during signup via `options.data`
- Workspace slug is only updated if it still has the auto-generated "ag-" prefix
- All database operations use `SECURITY DEFINER` to bypass RLS during user provisioning
- Error handling is non-blocking: persistence failures don't prevent onboarding completion
- Token validation catches both client-side JWT validity and server-side project mismatch

author: minsky-ai[bot]
body:
## Summary

Closes mt#1110 SC #1 (trivial-PR REQUEST_CHANGES rate) and SC #3 (larger-PR baseline within ±10%) via empirical measurement against the deployed mt#1188 + mt#1189 prompt on main. Adds measurement coverage for the direct-contradiction class observed in PR #881 R3.

**Headline numbers:**
- SC #1 — trivial-PR rate: **91.7% REQUEST_CHANGES** (55/60), target ≤30%. **NOT MET.**
- SC #3 — larger-PR baseline: **93.3% REQUEST_CHANGES** (14/15) vs ~80% historical. **+13.3pp drift, NOT MET** (target ±10%).
- Direct-contradiction class: **67% line-number reproduction** (PR #881 R3, line 452 hit on attempts 1+2 of 3).

## Motivation & Context

mt#1110 is the reviewer-bot calibration umbrella. mt#1188 (scope-aware rigor for trivial PRs) and mt#1189 (prior-review history ingest) are both DONE and deployed to production main. mt#1110's three SCs were calibration measurements pending post-rollout verification — this task closes them.

mt#1465 (severity-monotonicity prototype + replay) covered SC #2. mt#1493 covers SC #1 + SC #3 plus measures the direct-contradiction class observed in PR #881 R3 (calibration data row 55) — distinct from severity-inflation, distinct from PR #792 R5↔R7 contradiction.

## Design / Approach

Built `services/reviewer/scripts/measure-calibration.ts` as a sibling to mt#1465's `replay-severity.ts`. Three modes: `--mode=trivial|larger|contradiction`. Each mode invokes the same `runReview` path the harness uses, records `event` (REQUEST_CHANGES/COMMENT/APPROVE) per attempt + per-finding severity counts.

Key implementation details:
1. **GraphQL trivial-PR enumeration**: original REST `pulls.list` + per-PR `pulls.get` fetches (because REST list doesn't include `additions`/`deletions`) burned the user's PAT rate limit (5001/5000) on first dry-run. Refactored to single GraphQL query returning 100 PRs with line counts inline. Reduced from 50-100 REST calls to 1-3 GraphQL calls per dry-run. Filed mt#1502 for the structural fix (harness should use a dedicated bot identity, not user PAT).
2. **Free-text fallback parser** (mt#1496 R5 mitigation): if `output.toolCalls` is empty AND `output.text` contains structured `[BLOCKING]` markers, parse them via `parseFindingsFromBody`. Records `findingSource` per attempt for auditability.
3. **Resilience patches**: 20-min per-call timeout (gpt-5 with 4-7K reasoning + 5-10K completion can take 5-10 min); maxRetries 3 at SDK level; per-attempt try/catch in `runAttempts` so a single timeout no longer aborts the run.

## Key Changes

- `services/reviewer/scripts/measure-calibration.ts` (new, ~1080 lines): three-mode measurement script with corpus enumeration, prior-review fetch, OpenAI replay, JSON results output, summary tables.
- `services/reviewer/scripts/replay-severity.ts` (copied from mt#1465's `task/mt-1465` branch since PR #920 not yet merged): the underlying replay primitive the measurement script reuses.
- `services/reviewer/src/replay-summary.ts` (extended from mt#1465's branch): adds `parseFindingsFromBody`, `detectSeverityInflation`, `FlatFinding`, `SeverityInflationResult` exports.
- `services/reviewer/src/replay-summary.test.ts` (copied from mt#1465's branch): 25 unit tests covering parser + inflation detector.
- `services/reviewer/scripts/measure-calibration-{trivial,larger,contradiction}-results.json`: live measurement output from the 78-call run (~$30 OpenAI spend).
- 3 calibration data rows in private memory `project_mt1110_calibration_data.md` documenting each measurement's setup, raw results, and calibration insight.

## Testing

- `bunx tsc --noEmit -p .` clean.
- 3 dry-runs (`--mode=trivial|larger|contradiction --dry-run`) verified all corpus + prior-review fetches resolve before authorizing live spend.
- Live runs: 78 attempts total, 1 timeout (handled by resilience patch — run continued, placeholder result recorded), 0 unrecoverable errors.
- All 3 results JSONs validated against schema (5 known fields per attempt).

## Calibration insight (third-fold of the mt#1429/mt#1465 pattern)

mt#1188's scope-aware-calibration prompt is in production main but is NOT effectively biting on trivial PRs. The prompt section explicitly tells the reviewer to reserve BLOCKING severity for security/data-loss/scope-creep/license categories on trivial PRs and prefer COMMENT over REQUEST_CHANGES — these instructions consistently fail to override the Critic Constitution's adversarial framing.

Pattern is now confirmed across **three** classes:
1. `conclude_review` emission (mt#1413 — solved via mt#1471 forced tool_choice)
2. Severity-monotonicity (mt#1429 → mt#1465 prompt restructure → mt#1496 structural recovery)
3. **Trivial-PR rigor (mt#1493 — this task)**

The structural fix shape is consistent: composition-side enforcement, not prompt-level directives. **Recommended follow-up**: file a sibling task to mt#1496 that ships scope-aware-rigor enforcement structurally — post-process: if PR is classified trivial-or-docs / test-only AND all BLOCKING findings are non-security-non-data-loss-non-license, downgrade them to NON-BLOCKING and reset the conclude_review event to COMMENT. Same architectural shape as mt#1413, mt#1471, mt#1496.

The direct-contradiction class (PR #881 line 452 reproduction) is similarly out of mt#1496's scope (file-only match keyed on prior NON-BLOCKING/PRE-EXISTING; this is BLOCKING-vs-prior-BLOCKING). Sibling task warranted after mt#1496 lands.

## Out of scope

- Implementation of any new prompt or structural fix. Measurement-only. Three follow-up implementation tasks should spawn from this measurement (trivial-PR scope enforcement, contradiction-class recovery, larger-PR drift investigation).
- Cross-model comparison (gpt-5 only).
- Severity-inflation class (mt#1465's territory).

🤖 Drafted by Claude after running the 3-mode replay; spent ~$30 in gpt-5 calls authorized by the user.

author: stupideity
body:
## Summary

- Eliminates the sig-escape retry pattern observed in ENG-44's dogfood (6 mutated-sig duplicate Linear comments on a single ticket: `…-trial`, `…-v3`, `…-v9`, `…-v12`, `…-v13`).
- Pure prompt instruction, no runtime change. `add-or-update-comment` is already idempotent — same sig + new body overwrites in place. Agents just didn't believe it.

Closes [ENG-57](https://linear.app/twinning/issue/ENG-57). Obsoletes ENG-53 sub-issue #11 pattern (b).

## What changed

- **`AGENT_PROMPTS.md`** preamble (Comment dedup block): explicit "retry overwrites in place — never mutate the sig" clause with the dogfood as evidence.
- **`AGENT_PROMPTS.md`** per-stage Tool-allowlist paragraph: extend the universal ENG-53 #11 paragraph (replicated across §§1-9) with the same-sig retry rule. One edit propagates via replace_all.
- **`bin/agent-prompts-content-test.sh`**: 18 new ENG-57 assertions (9 stages × 2 — "contains retry rule" + "never mutate warning paired with forbidden-suffix list"). Plus a tweak to the existing ENG-53 #11 header assertion to allow the new "ENG-53 #11 / ENG-57" attribution.

## What's intentionally NOT in this PR

The ticket also proposed (Part 1) a `bash bin/linear.sh validate-body` scanner that would flag bodies containing literal `$VAR` / backticks / `$(cmd)` and (Part 3) server-side mutated-sig detection.

**Skipping Part 1** — after ENG-55 (PR #37), agents construct multi-line bodies via stdin-piped quoted heredocs (`<<'EOF'`). In that path, literal `$VAR` in the body is *preserved on purpose* — that's the contract. A scanner can't distinguish "agent forgot to quote the heredoc" from "agent legitimately wants `$HOME` to appear in the body as text." The false-positive risk outweighs the leftover value, especially since the same-sig retry rule (Part 2) addresses the dominant production pattern.

**Skipping Part 3** — server-side mutated-sig rejection is a guard rail in case the prompt is ignored. Defer until the same-sig rule shows it's insufficient in practice. Adding server-side regex parsing of sig structure has its own design choices (what counts as "canonical" vs "mutated"; how to handle legitimate sig versioning if we ever introduce one) that aren't worth working through speculatively.

If wild data shows the rule alone isn't enough, both deferred parts can ship in a focused follow-up.

## Test plan

- [x] `bash bin/linear-test.sh` — 101 passing (no change)
- [x] `bash bin/run-stage-test.sh` — 81 passing (no change)

# Description

<!-- Please include a summary of the changes and the related issue. Please also include relevant motivation and context. -->

In SCS, over Fp2, Schoolbook multiplication (4M+2A=6 gates) is better than Karatsuba (3M+5A=8 gates). This applies to BLS12-377.

## Type of change

# PR Summary

Sci/Tech Reviewer: <!-- SR id, filled by author when ready for review (e.g. @octocat) --> @P-Burns 
Code Reviewer: <!-- CR id, filled by SSD/CCD (e.g. @octocat) --> @Pierre-siddall 

Add a new option for free_atm_mix to calculate a vertically smoother mixing length.  Under the existing options, the mixing length is constant within turbulent layers (defined as where the Richardson number is subcritical), except as it approaches the surface where it tends towards the height above the surface.  This reduction represents the suppression of the scale of vertical mixing by the physical presence of the boundary.  In this new option we apply the same principle to the top and bottom boundaries of every turbulent layer, thereby making smoother transitions in the mixing length between layers of the atmosphere.

Equivalent changes in the UM at vn14.1: [vn14.1_smooth_lambda](https://github.com/MetOffice/um/compare/main...MichaelWhitall:um:vn14.1_smooth_lambda)

author: philipaconrad
body:
### What changed, and why?

This PR adds an implementation for the [`client_tls` bundle service credentials option](https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/configuration#client-tls-certificate) through the new
`ClientTLSAuthPluginLoader` bundle loader type.

This change forced a number of refactors in how `HTTPClient` instances are handled, and we now rebuild them on every bundle fetch. This is correct, but grossly inefficient. We have the option of caching clients in the future until configs change, which may present a decent optimization for some users.

-----

In the test suite, we've collapsed all of the disparate test bundle servers together into just one server implementation with many configuration options.

The tests also now use a flag env variable to detect when OpenSSL is available: `SWIFT_OPA_OPENSSL_TESTS`. When set to `1`, the tests are enabled. The Makefile and CI workflows auto-enable it where relevant. This saves us from committing certs into the repository, avoiding tests breaking when those certs expire.

### How to test

 - New test suites were added under `Tests/RuntimeTests`. These are picked up by `make test` automatically.

author: liliankasem
body:
Resolves #4897

## Summary

Adds the workload loader: turns persisted manifest entries (from #4893, now in `vnext`) into runnable `IWorkload` instances, each loaded into its own collectible `AssemblyLoadContext` so dependency versions don't collide across workloads.

The discovery/scanner side (`[assembly: ExportCliWorkload<T>]`) is intentionally deferred to a follow-up install-pipeline PR.

## What this PR adds

- **`IWorkloadLoader` / `WorkloadLoader`** — pure: takes `IReadOnlyList<InstalledWorkload>`, returns `IReadOnlyList<LoadedWorkload>`. No I/O on the manifest, no DI surface yet — the composition root reads from `IGlobalManifestStore` and hands entries here.
- **`WorkloadLoadContext`** — per-workload **collectible** `AssemblyLoadContext`. Resolves probe-path dependencies (`AssemblyDependencyResolver`) and **delegates a small allow-list of host assemblies** (`Azure.Functions.Cli.Abstractions`, `Microsoft.Extensions.*`, `System.*`, `Microsoft.Win32.*`, `netstandard`, `mscorlib`) to `Default` so type identity for `IWorkload` and DI primitives is preserved across the boundary.
- **`LoadedWorkload`** — pairs the activated `IWorkload` instance with its `WorkloadInfo`.
- **Test fixture project** (`Func.Cli.Tests.Fixtures.Workload`) — real on-disk assembly the loader tests load through the ALC; not referenced by the test project at compile time.

## Design decisions

- **Sync, pure API.** `LoadInstalled` is synchronous and accepts an in-memory list rather than the store. Reflection/`Activator.CreateInstance` is CPU-bound, and decoupling from the store keeps loader tests free of filesystem fixtures.
- **Collectible ALCs.** `isCollectible: true` enables future unload/hot-reload (e.g. `func workload uninstall` while the host is alive). Cost is small; the option can't be added later without a breaking change to ALC identity.
- **Explicit shared-assembly allow-list** instead of `AssemblyLoadContext.Default.Assemblies.Any(...)`. The latter accidentally shares any assembly the host happens to have loaded; the allow-list makes the contract explicit and reviewable.
- **All-or-nothing loading.** A failure on any entry throws `GracefulException` — no partially-loaded workload set. Errors are prefixed `[<package-id>]` and include `InstallPath` per spec §6.3 / §7.

## Tests

- `LoadInstalled_ReturnsEmpty_WhenNoEntries`
- `LoadInstalled_HydratesEntry_FromAssemblyOnDisk`
- `LoadInstalled_Throws_WhenAssemblyFileMissing` / `WhenTypeNotFoundInAssembly` / `WhenTypeDoesNotImplementIWorkload`
- `LoadInstalled_LoadsEachWorkloadInOwnAssemblyLoadContext`
- `LoadInstalled_LoadContextIsCollectible`
- `LoadInstalled_DelegatesAbstractionsAssemblyToDefaultContext` — pins the type-identity contract; if the ALC ever loaded its own copy of `Azure.Functions.Cli.Abstractions`, the cast in `WorkloadLoader` would fail.

## Out of scope (follow-up PR)

- `[assembly: ExportCliWorkload<T>]` attribute + scanner
- `func workload install / uninstall / list` commands
- Composition root wiring (DI registration, command parser bridge)

## Spec
[`docs/workload-spec.md`](https://github.com/Azure/azure-functions-core-tools/blob/liliankasem/docs/workloads/docs/workload-spec.md)

Replace direct lightserver JSON-RPC reads with the stable, finalized-only
Finalis Explorer REST API (`GET /api/status, /api/address/<addr>,

is derived at runtime from the explorer base URL via rpcUrlFromExplorerUrl().

data/lightserver:

  - balance/UTXOs → GET /api/address/<addr>

  - tx detail     → GET /api/tx/<txid>

body:
## Summary
- `DoobieBillRepository.upsertPlaceholder` was stamping `update_date = NOW()` on insert, assuming the column was `NOT NULL`. Both `title` and `update_date` are nullable on the schema, and that wall-clock stamp poisoned the metadata pipeline's `incoming.updateDate > stored.updateDate` comparison: the writer's NOW() is by definition newer than any real Congress.gov updateDate, so every placeholder row got routed to the "Bill unchanged" branch forever after.
- Defense-in-depth detection landed in PR #102 (placeholder branch in `BillMetadataProcessor.evaluateAndProcess` matches by field-set shape, ignores `update_date`). This PR is the **root-cause** fix.
- Insert only `(congress, bill_type, number, title)` and let every other column take its declared default — NULL for `update_date` / `update_date_including_text` / every detail Option column, `now()` for `created_at` / `updated_at` (DB row metadata, not API content). `title` stays `''` because `BillDO.title` is non-Option `String` and Doobie's `Read` decoder would crash on NULL.
- Two new integration tests pin the new contract: `update_date` + `update_date_including_text` must be NULL post-insert, and the resulting row must satisfy `BillPlaceholder.isPlaceholder` (the canonical detector pinned to `HasPlaceholder[BillDO].placeholder(...)` via the invariant-lock test in `BillPlaceholderSpec`).

## Existing-data fix (one-shot, separate from this PR)
A SQL script outside the repo (`~/source/repos2024/repair-placeholder-update-date.sql`) NULLs out `update_date` and `update_date_including_text` on existing placeholder rows in dev DBs (~161,721 rows in our local AlloyDB). Predicate matches `BillPlaceholder.isPlaceholder` exactly (title='' AND every detail column IS NULL), so real bills are never touched.

## Test plan
- [x] Local `sbt billsCommon/test` (153 non-Docker tests pass)
- [ ] CI: `build`, `doc-generator`, `e2e-gcp` (DockerRequired tests run on Linux CI; locally they require a fixture-spawned postgres which the Windows env can't launch)
- [ ] Codecov patch coverage on `DoobieBillRepository.scala` should stay above 90%
- [ ] After merge: run `repair-placeholder-update-date.sql` against dev AlloyDB, restart metadata pipeline 10y backfill, verify placeholder rows surface through the date-comparison branch (not just the defense-in-depth placeholder branch)

## Summary

- Lower AVIF image compression quality from 85 → 30 in the production backup script
- AVIF quality 85 was near-lossless, producing backup files heavier than the previous WebP output

author: sirraide
body:
Currently, `ASTUnit::LoadFromCompilerInvocation()` just calls the constructor of `ASTUnit`, which default-constructs a `CodeGenOptions` instance. The options from the `CompilerInstance` are never actually saved in the `ASTUnit`. As a result, serialising the `ASTUnit` ends up serialising the default-constructed `CodeGenOptions` rather than the _actual_ `CodeGenOptions`.

This is problematic if you attempt to do the following:
1. Call e.g. `buildASTFromCodeWithArgs()` to build an `ASTUnit`
2. Serialise that `ASTUnit`.
3. Call e.g. `buildASTFromCodeWithArgs()` again with the exact same arguments and add use the first `ASTUnit` as a PCH using `-include-pch`.

This causes Clang to error because the `CodeGenOptions` we deserialised for the first `ASTUnit` (the default-constructed ones) are incompatible with the `CodeGenOptions` implicitly created for the second TU (which were created by the `CompilerInstance` and potentially modified due to command-line argument parsing)... despite the fact that we basically just attempted to build two TUs with the same arguments.

To fix this, copy the `CodeGenOptions` from the `CompilerInstance` into the `ASTUnit`.

author: ridopark
body:
## Summary

- New `RESTClient.GetOptionDayBars(ctx, dataURL, []OCC, date)` chunks the input into batches of 100 OCCs per `/v1beta1/options/bars` request and returns one merged `map[Symbol]*MarketBar`. The single-OCC `GetOptionDayBar` now delegates to it.
- `AlpacaService.CaptureDate` collects every contract's OCC into one slice and fires one batched call instead of N sequential round-trips. A typical 600-strike (symbol, date) collapses from 600 round-trips to 6.
- `omo-backfill -source alpaca` reads underlying daily bars from `repo.GetMarketBars` instead of re-fetching from Alpaca. The bars table already has 1d entries (`datarefresh.RefreshAll` writes them in production).

## Why

Phase 2 (#78) shipped a one-OCC-per-call bar fetcher and re-fetched underlying spots from Alpaca live API. On the 34-symbol universe across 2024-02 → 2026-05, that would have taken ~10 days of wall time — unworkably long for an operational backfill. The plan's 2.5h estimate quietly assumed batched bar fetches; this PR closes the gap.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Per-OCC bar calls | ~11M (1/contract) | ~110K (100 OCCs/batch) |
| Spot lookup calls | ~9.5K Alpaca calls | 0 (DB read) |
| **Wall time** | **~10 days** | **~2.5 hours** |

If 1d underlying bars aren't present in the local bars table for a symbol, we WARN and skip that symbol's dates rather than silently returning zero — operator runs `omo-data` once (`datarefresh.RefreshAll` writes 1d) or `omo-backfill -timeframe 1d` to populate.

## Evidence

```
$ go test ./internal/adapters/alpaca/ -run "TestGetOptionDayBar"
=== RUN   TestGetOptionDayBar_HappyPath                              --- PASS
=== RUN   TestGetOptionDayBar_NoBarReturnsNil                        --- PASS
=== RUN   TestGetOptionDayBar_EmptyOCCRejected                       --- PASS
=== RUN   TestGetOptionDayBars_ChunksAt100AndMergesResponses         --- PASS
=== RUN   TestGetOptionDayBars_EmptyInputReturnsEmptyMap             --- PASS
=== RUN   TestGetOptionDayBars_PartialMissingBarsAreOmittedFromMap   --- PASS
=== RUN   TestGetOptionDayBar_HTTPErrorBubbles                       --- PASS
PASS
```

`TestGetOptionDayBars_ChunksAt100AndMergesResponses` builds 250 OCC symbols and asserts the server sees exactly 3 requests (100 + 100 + 50), pinning the chunk size and the merge contract.

`TestGetOptionDayBars_PartialMissingBarsAreOmittedFromMap` pins the skip-don't-default rule: when the API returns no bar for one of the requested OCCs, the map omits that key (callers test with `bars[occ]` returning nil rather than getting a zero-valued bar).

`go test ./internal/app/optionsimport/...` — 21 tests, all pass after the AlpacaService refactor to use the batched method. `go test ./internal/...` — 65 packages, all pass. `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` clean.

## Plan

Follow-up to PR #78 (Phase 2). Same overall plan: `_workspace/alpaca_options_backfill_plan.md`. Doesn't change Phase 2's acceptance criteria — it just makes the operational backfill feasible.

## Sub-agents consulted

None — diff is mechanical (single → batched refactor + repo wiring substitution).

## Test plan

- [ ] `cd backend && go test ./internal/adapters/alpaca/ ./internal/app/optionsimport/...`
- [ ] Manual: confirm `omo-backfill -source alpaca` no longer needs Alpaca credentials at the spot-lookup phase if the DB has 1d bars (only the `/v1beta1/options/bars` endpoint hits Alpaca)
- [ ] Post-merge live smoke: `omo-backfill -source alpaca -from 2026-04-01 -to 2026-04-05 -symbols AAPL,TSLA` → expect ~5 trading days × 2 symbols = 10 (sym, date) pairs, each writing a few hundred chain rows. Wall time should be seconds, not minutes.
- [ ] Full backfill: `omo-backfill -source alpaca -from 2026-02-05 -to <today>` — expected wall time ~2.5h for the 34-symbol universe.

author: queueeee
body:
## Why "CONNECTING" hängt

Live: TS6-UI bleibt bei `CONNECTING` stehen, ICE läuft nie auf `connected`. Die ganze Zeit haben wir diese Warning in den Logs ignoriert:

```
RTCPeerConnection addIceCandidate called without remote description
RTCPeerConnection addIceCandidate called without remote description
RTCPeerConnection addIceCandidate called without remote description
RTCPeerConnection addIceCandidate called without remote description
RTCPeerConnection addIceCandidate called without remote description
```

Die ist **nicht** harmlos. aiortc REJECTED die `addIceCandidate`-Calls wenn `setRemoteDescription` noch nicht durch ist — das Candidate ist weg. Wir haben in jedem Versuch alle 5 ersten ICE-Candidates verloren.

Race-Condition: `_on_signaling_message` spawnt sowohl die Answer-Task (`_apply_answer` → `setRemoteDescription`) als auch jede ICE-Candidate-Task (`_apply_ice_candidate` → `addIceCandidate`) als unabhängige `asyncio.create_task`s. Die ICE-Tasks laufen typisch VOR der Answer-Task durch.

## Fix

Per-Viewer `asyncio.Event` (`remote_set`). Wird gesetzt wenn `setRemoteDescription` durch ist. `_apply_ice_candidate` awaitet das Event (10 s Cap als Safety) bevor es `addIceCandidate` ruft. Damit kommen ICE-Candidates byte-genau an, egal in welcher Reihenfolge sie reinkommen.

## Bonus

- `STUN_URL` / `TURN_URL` / `TURN_USERNAME` / `TURN_PASSWORD` als ENV-Variablen. Default-STUN bleibt `stun.l.google.com:19302`. Wenn das echte ICE-Problem trotz dieses Fixes weiterläuft (symmetric NAT / CGNAT), kann der Operator einen freien TURN-Server eintragen ohne Code-Änderung:

```ini
TURN_URL=turn:openrelay.metered.ca:80
TURN_USERNAME=openrelayproject
TURN_PASSWORD=openrelayproject
```

## Tests

- 11 publisher tests grün, inkl. **neue Regression** die ICE-Candidate VOR Answer schickt und prüft dass `addIceCandidate` nicht aufgerufen wird bis Answer da ist.
- ruff + mypy strict + 219 tests overall.

## Operator commands

```bash
cd /opt/ts6-stream-bot
git pull
docker compose down
docker compose build --no-cache
docker compose up -d
docker compose logs -f
```

Dann im TS6-Client den Bot-Stream beitreten. Erwartet:

```
viewer_offer_sent clid=…
viewer_pc_state state=connecting
viewer_ice_state ice=checking
viewer_ice_state ice=completed       ← KEINE "addIceCandidate without remote description" Warnings mehr
viewer_pc_state state=connected
parec_audio.started
```

UI wechselt auf CONNECTED und du siehst Bot's Chromium (initial leerer Screen — `POST /play <url>` machen für Inhalt).

## Summary
- Bumps the `repcheck-ingestion-common` dep from **0.1.23** → **0.1.27**, which contains the SortOrder URL-encoding fix shipped in https://github.com/Eligio-Taveras/repcheck-ingestion-common/pull/29.
- That PR changed `SortOrder.UpdateDateAsc.queryValue` from `"updateDate+asc"` → `"updateDate asc"` (and Desc similarly). The literal `+` was getting URL-encoded by http4s to `%2B`, decoded by Congress.gov server back to a literal `+`, which the API doesn't recognize as a separator — so the server silently fell back to a non-`updateDate` order. Every paginated bill sweep across every pipeline that uses this enum has been running with broken sort.
- No source changes in this repo. Just a version bump.

## Empirical verification (from upstream PR #29)
```
sort=updateDate%2Bdesc&fromDateTime=2016-05-03  -> 105-HCONRES-9 (2016-10-26)  // broken (old behavior)
sort=updateDate%20desc&fromDateTime=2016-05-03  -> 119-HR-4214  (2026-05-01)  // fixed
```

- [ ] After merge: rebuild `cross-bill-embed-bill-metadata-pipeline` image, stop the currently-running broken-sort backfill, restart with the fixed image, verify first page returns 119th-Congress 2026-dated bills (not 105-Congress 2016-dated bills as we observed earlier today)

body:
## Summary

PR #5211 added a `recover()` helper to the live-regression suite that runs `gsd recover` between fixture write and `gsd headless query`. That call fails in CI because the interactive `/gsd recover` slash command is gated behind a TTY check (`src/cli.ts` `printNonTtyErrorAndExit`):

```
gsd recover should succeed for fixture, got 1: [gsd] Error: Interactive mode requires a terminal (TTY) but stdin and stdout are not a TTY.
```

This adds `gsd headless recover` as the non-interactive parallel, mirroring the existing `gsd headless query` and `gsd headless doctor` shape (read/write, no RPC child, no TTY required). Switches the live-regression `recover()` helper to call the new subcommand.

## What's in the PR

- **`src/headless-recover.ts`** — new entrypoint that loads the GSD extension via jiti (same agent-dir-or-bundled fallback used by `headless-query.ts`) and orchestrates the same pipeline the interactive command runs:
  - `ensureDbOpen` → opens an existing DB or creates an empty authoritative one
  - `transaction(() => { clearEngineHierarchy(); migrateHierarchyToDb(basePath) })` → atomic clear + repopulate from `ROADMAP.md` / `PLAN.md` / `SUMMARY.md` projections
  - `invalidateStateCache()` → ensures the next derive uses fresh DB rows
  - emits `gsd-recover: recovered <m>M/<s>S/<t>T hierarchy` on stderr (matches the existing success-path marker at `commands-maintenance.ts:535`)
- **`src/headless.ts`** — wires `options.command === 'recover'` at the same level as `'query'` / `'doctor'`. Comment notes this is the one mutating headless subcommand.
- **`src/help-text.ts`** — adds the new subcommand to `gsd headless --help`.
- **`tests/live-regression/run.ts`** — switches the existing `recover(dir)` helper to call `gsd(["headless", "recover"], dir)`.
- **`src/tests/headless-recover.test.ts`** — new unit coverage:
  - success path (markdown fixture imported into milestone/slice/task rows; counts match)
  - idempotency (two consecutive recoveries produce identical counts; clear-then-import semantics)

## Why a separate PR

PR #5211 already merged with the old non-functional `gsd recover` call. Dev Verify on `main` is currently red. This PR closes that gap.

author: villepajala
body:
## Summary

Pure-logic foundation for **PR 8 (Apply preview + safety)**. Splits Phase 4 into three smaller PRs the same way Phase 1 was 5a/5b/5c/5d/5e and Phase 3 was 7a/7b/7c/7d:

| PR | Scope | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **8a (this)** | Diff calculator + tests (pure logic) | ⏳ |
| **8b** | PlanningApplyPreview component + PlanningEditor wiring + per-game opt-out | next |
| **8c** | 30-second post-Apply undo banner | after 8b |

## What this PR adds

\`src/utils/applyPreview.ts\` — pure functions that compute the per-game diff between a saved game's current state and the editor's draft.

\`\`\`ts
export function computeApplyDiff(
  gameId: string,
  game: AppState,
  draft: PlanDraft,
  preset: FormationPreset,
): ApplyDiff;

export function countDiffChanges(diff: ApplyDiff): number;
\`\`\`

The \`ApplyDiff\` shape carries six change categories:

- **\`lineupAdded\`** — player not on the saved game's field, but in \`draft.startingXI\`
- **\`lineupRemoved\`** — player on the field but missing from the draft (going to bench)
- **\`lineupMoved\`** — same player, different role
- **\`subsAdded\`** — scheduled sub in the draft, not in the saved game (matched by id)
- **\`subsRemoved\`** — sub in the saved game, not in the draft
- **\`subsModified\`** — same id, different fields (excluding the draft-omitted \`outPlayer\`)

Plus \`isEmpty\` for the preview UI's "skip this game" logic.

## Design choices worth flagging

- **Coord-based current-role inference.** The saved game stores \`playersOnField\` with \`relX\`/\`relY\`. The diff uses \`roleForCoord(preset, …)\` to map back to role names, so legacy coord drift falls through to no-role and is treated as "removed" if the player isn't in the draft. Same pattern \`PlanningEditor\` uses for hydration.
- **\`outPlayer\` ignored on the modify check.** \`DraftScheduledSub\` doesn't carry \`outPlayer\` — it's computed at Apply time via \`getRoleSegments\`. Treating an outPlayer-only delta as a "modify" would surface every saved sub as changed even when the draft is identical to what's stored.
- **No matching-by-content for subs** — match strictly by id. A draft sub and a saved sub with the same time/role/inPlayer but different ids are correctly reported as one removal + one add. The id is the lifecycle identifier; same-content+different-id usually means the user deleted and recreated.

## Tests

10 cases under \`computeApplyDiff\`:
- Empty diff when game ≡ draft
- Player added / removed / role-moved
- Combined add + remove + move in one call
- subsAdded / subsRemoved / subsModified each in isolation
- outPlayer-only delta is NOT a modify (the contract above)
- \`countDiffChanges\` sums every category

## Out of scope (PR 8b/c)

- The preview component itself (rendering / opt-out checkboxes / Confirm).
- Wiring PlanningEditor's Apply button to show the preview before committing.
- The 30-second undo banner with restore-from-snapshot.

body:
## Summary
- Redesigns the Windows dashboard around a clear AntiJitter connection control plus Normal and Gaming mode selection.
- Adds the requested Starlink blue, mobile green, and bonded teal color system to the Windows UI.
- Adds per-path latency/jitter probes and a live latency trend chart for Windows.
- Maps Normal mode to primary uplink/downlink to protect mobile data, and Gaming mode to all-path redundancy for live matches.
- Adds a lightweight local Starlink dish reachability probe and exposes the first dish status hook in the Windows UI.

## Notes
- The Starlink panel is intentionally a first hook: it checks local dish stats reachability at `192.168.100.1:9200`; deeper obstruction/dropout history can be layered on next.
- Normal mode is currently primary-path-first. True automatic stall/failover policy can be refined in a follow-up once we define thresholds.
- This PR does not change Android, backend API, deployment, or the bonding wire protocol.

## Validation
- `go test ./...` from `client/`
- `npm.cmd run build` from `client/frontend/`
- `wails build` from `client/`

All three passed locally. Initial sandboxed runs hit Windows cache/spawn permission blocks, then passed with normal local build permissions.

author: talamuyal
body:
## What

- Rename the project from "awrit" to "glimpse-tty" across the entire codebase as part of forking the discontinued upstream project
- Preserve original BSD-3-Clause license and copyright (Chase Colman), add fork maintainer copyright (Tal Amuyal)
- Add fork attribution in README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md linking back to the original [chase/awrit](https://github.com/chase/awrit)
- Update all package identifiers (package.json, Cargo.toml, napi config), GitHub URLs, XDG config paths, CSS class prefixes, shell scripts, CI/CD workflows, and documentation
- Add config migration logic so existing users with `~/.config/awrit/config.js` are seamlessly transitioned to `~/.config/glimpse-tty/config.js`
- Split the single CI.yml (which was purely a release pipeline) into CI.yml (build verification on PRs) and CD.yml (releases on master push)
- Fix pre-existing bug: CI branch trigger pointed to stale `electron` branch instead of `master`

## Why

- The original awrit project by Chase Colman is no longer actively maintained
- Forking under a distinct name avoids user confusion, potential trademark issues, and complies with BSD-3-Clause clause 3 (no endorsement without permission)
- The CI/CD split ensures PRs get automated build verification, which was previously missing entirely
- Config migration prevents existing users from silently losing their configuration after upgrading

body: ## Summary Fixes five bugs that prevent Execute and Inject from working: ### Execute fixes (UI crash) 1. **`ExecuteBtn_Click` — missing top-level try/catch**: Since this is an `async void` event handler, any unhandled exception propagates to the WPF SynchronizationContext and **crashes the entire app**. Wrapped the full method body in try/catch. 2. **`ExecuteBtn_Click` — direct API calls without SafeApiCall**: Both `AttachAPI` (re-attach) and `ExecuteScript` were called directly without `SafeApiCall`, meaning `TypeLoadException`/`TypeInitializationException` from the SpashAPIMadium library would crash the app. Wrapped in `SafeApiCall` + `Task.Run` (consistent with `ExecuteOnInstanceAsync` pattern). 3. **`ExecuteOnSelected_Click` — same missing try/catch**: Another `async void` handler with no top-level guard. ### Inject fixes 4. **`TryInjectAsync` — passing `string.Empty` instead of actual PID**: `AttachAPI` was called with `string.Empty` instead of the Roblox process ID, so the API couldn't target the correct process. Now passes `roblox.Id.ToString()`. 5. **`InjectBtn_Click` — no fallback when Loader.exe missing**: When `Loader.exe` wasn't found, the inject button silently returned. Now falls back to API-based injection via `TryInjectAsync`. ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] Verify Execute button works without crashing: open Roblox, inject, type a script, click Execute - [ ] Verify Inject button works when `Loader.exe` is present (should behave as before) - [ ] Verify Inject button falls back to API injection when `Loader.exe` is missing - [ ] Check console log for any `[ERROR]` messages — errors should now be logged instead of crashing ### Notes All fixes follow the existing `SafeApiCall` + `Task.Run` pattern already used in `TryInjectAsync` and `ExecuteOnInstanceAsync`. No new dependencies or patterns introduced. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/09b1804de1f74f8f8a6f56efc4ed5605 Requested by: @sg465c5fv2-droid ---

author: snapfast
body:
This PR optimizes the city suggestion caching logic for the Nominatim API in the `ChartGeneration` component.

### Changes:
- **Map-based Cache:** Replaced the plain object `SUGGESTIONS_CACHE` with a `Map` for better performance and a cleaner API.
- **Case-Insensitive Normalization:** Search queries are now lowercased before lookup and insertion, preventing redundant API calls for casing variations (e.g., "London" vs "london").
- **Session Persistence:** The cache is now synchronized with `sessionStorage`. This allows users to receive instant suggestions even after refreshing the page or navigating back to the form.
- **Memory Management:** Added a `MAX_CACHE_SIZE` of 100 entries with a FIFO eviction strategy to ensure the cache remains lightweight.
- **Robustness:** Included SSR checks (`typeof window !== 'undefined'`) and error handling for `sessionStorage` quota limits.

### Impact:
- **Reduced Latency:** Instant results for previously searched cities, even across sessions.
- **Fewer Network Requests:** Eliminates redundant calls to the Nominatim API.
- **Improved UX:** Snappier autocomplete experience on the "Free Horoscope" tool.

author: tobymurray
body:
Without this fix, pressing the exit key (key 4 / R2 / BACK) crashes the simulator on shutdown:

```
  pure virtual method called
  terminate called without an active exception
  Aborted (core dumped)
```

The cause: AppCore::run() called app.handleTickEvent() from the kernel background thread after taskEntry() had already returned on the main thread. handleTickEvent() dispatches through FrontendApplication into the TouchGFX screen/presenter virtual chain — but those objects are already torn down at that point, so the call hits pure-virtual stubs.

Remove both handleTickEvent() calls and the now-unused FrontendApplication include. The queued COMMAND_APP_GUI_SUSPEND and COMMAND_APP_STOP messages are drained by ~DualAppComm()::clearAllQueues() during normal shutdown.

author: railway-app[bot]
body:
## Problem

The bot was hanging for 340+ seconds during Spotify token refreshes because `requests_timeout=30` was set on the `spotipy.Spotify` client but not on the `SpotifyOAuth` auth manager. The auth manager makes its own HTTP requests to Spotify's token endpoint using a separate session with no timeout, so when that endpoint was slow or unreachable the bot blocked indefinitely, starving the Discord heartbeat and crashing the connection.

## Solution

Added `requests_timeout=10` to the `SpotifyOAuth(...)` constructor. Spotipy passes this value through to the auth manager's internal requests session, so token refresh calls will now fail fast after 10 seconds instead of hanging indefinitely. The existing `requests_timeout=30` on the `Spotify` client is kept as-is since it governs the separate API call session.

### Changes
- **Modified** `bot.py`

## Summary

## Why
`TimeoutError` is a `BaseException` subclass in Python 3.11+ — it is not caught by `except Exception`. The bot_chat handler was only catching `Exception`, so planning session timeouts propagated through the ASGI stack and killed the WebSocket connection with no user-facing message.

author: otoua046
body:
## Overview
This PR introduces a suite of new features, UI refinements, and critical stability fixes to the FocusRead app. The primary focus is on enhancing the Library bookshelf experience and resolving core memory and reading engine bugs.

## Features & Improvements
* **Library Controls Menu:** Added a native Apple Books-style `LibraryControlsMenu` providing multi-selection, view modes (Grid and List), and sorting options (Recent, Title, Author, Manual). State is persisted across app launches via `AppStorage`.
* **List View Layout:** Implemented `LibraryListView` and `LibraryListRow`, presenting a clean, flat list aesthetic devoid of heavy shadows and card containers. Rows include thumbnails, titles, authors, and reading progress, separated by subtle alignment-aware dividers.
* **Author Metadata Extraction:** Extended `SavedRead` and `ImportedDocument` to support an optional `author` property. Upgraded `EPUBTextExtractor` and its internal `OPFXMLParser` to seamlessly extract `creator` metadata from EPUB files.
* **Select Mode:** Built a comprehensive multi-select mode with "Select All" / "Deselect All" options and a safe, dynamically worded confirmation dialog for bulk deletions.
* **Menu Action Polish:** Enforced explicit `.red` foreground styling on destructive item-level actions (e.g., the Delete button inside the individual read three-dot menus) and added corresponding SF Symbols for all actions.

## Bug Fixes
* **Paragraph Break Tokenization:** Fixed a critical flaw in `TextTokenizer` where paragraph breaks (`

`) were erroneously applied to the *first word* of the next paragraph. Breaks are now correctly applied retrospectively to the *last word* of the preceding paragraph. This fixes awkward RSVP pause timings and broken sentence rewind behaviors.
* **Memory Leaks & Retain Cycles:** Conducted a deep codebase review and resolved severe memory leaks across `ReaderViewModel`, `GoToViewModel`, and `DocumentImportViewModel`. Fixed infinite execution loops by correctly capturing `[weak self]` inside `Task` blocks, ensuring ViewModels and their underlying `RSVPReadingEngine` tasks deallocate cleanly upon view dismissal.
* **Duplicate Menu Rows:** Fixed a UI bug causing duplicate "Grid" entries and mismatched icons in the library view mode toggle by replacing manual buttons with native `.inline` Swift `Picker` components.

## Verification & Testing
* Added a comprehensive set of unit tests in `TextTokenizerTests` covering paragraph break retroactivity, weak punctuation upgrades, section boundaries, and sentence rewind stability.
* The entire `FocusReadTests` suite ran and passed successfully on the iPhone 17 Simulator (iOS 18).
* Built and validated the application with `xcodebuild`, confirming zero compilation errors or active compiler warnings related to the changes.
* Visual verification of Layout shifts and SF Symbol alignment.

## Summary

This PR adds full macOS (Apple Silicon / M-chip) support, a bookmark sidebar panel, and fixes two functional bugs.

### macOS Support
- **`start.py`**: fix `kill_port()` to use `lsof -ti` instead of Windows `netstat`; use `python3` command on macOS/Linux; remove `shell=True` on non-Windows
- **`electron/main.js`**: resolve platform-specific backend binary name (`.exe` only on Windows); add `osascript` elevation dialog for packaged-app backend on macOS
- **`package.json`**: add `dist:mac` script and macOS DMG build config targeting `arm64`
- **`.gitignore`**: exclude `backend/dist/` and `backend/build/` (PyInstaller output)
- **`frontend/build/icon.png`**: resized to 512×512 for macOS DMG requirements

### Bookmark Sidebar
- Left-side collapsible panel listing saved coordinate bookmarks
- Toggle button in top-right corner to show/hide
- Integrated with all existing bookmark operations (add, delete, fly-to, pin on map)

### Bug Fixes

**一鍵還原 (Restore real GPS) was silently skipped**
- `DvtLocationService.clear()` and `LegacyLocationService.clear()` had an early return when `_active=False`
- `_active` only tracks whether `set()` was called *in the current session*, so opening the app fresh and pressing Restore did nothing — even if the device still had a spoofed location from a previous run
- Fix: always attempt `clear()` regardless of `_active`

**定位到目前位置 (Locate current position) failed on macOS**
- The `locate-pc` IPC handler always tried Windows PowerShell (`powershell.exe`), which fails immediately with `ENOENT` on macOS
- Fix: check `process.platform === 'win32'` first; on macOS/Linux skip straight to the IP-geolocation fallback chain (`ipwho.is` → `ipapi.co` → `freeipapi.com`)

- [ ] Build DMG with `npm run dist:mac` — installs and launches on Apple Silicon
- [ ] Connect iOS 17+ device, teleport to a location, quit app, relaunch → press Restore → real GPS resumes

author: eliasericsson
body:
## Summary

Final phase of the on-device AI migration. `ChatService` now routes through a `LanguageModelSession` when the user picks the on-device provider, with the same `CoachTools` (get_data_summary, get_weight_history, get_body_fat_history, get_calorie_totals, get_food_entries) exposed as `FoundationModels.Tool` conformances.

**Stacked on top of #5.** With this PR merged, the entire AI tier — text input, food photos, nutrition labels, USDA grounding, and Coach chat — has an on-device path.

## What changes

### `Services/CoachFoundationModelsTools.swift` (new, 161 lines)
- Bridges the existing `CoachTools` executor (name + JSON args → JSON string) into five individual `Tool` conformances
- **One Tool per name, not a single parametric tool**: each tool's `@Generable Arguments` schema gives the model precise constrained-decoding hints — "expects an ISO date string" is much more useful than "any string"
- Tool descriptions are pulled from the shared `CoachTools.toolDescriptions` map so all four tiers (FM, Gemini, Anthropic, OpenAI-compatible) see identical guidance — no drift risk

### `Services/ChatService.swift`
- New `.foundationModels` case in the `apiFormat` switch
- New `callFoundationModels()` helper: builds a `LanguageModelSession` with the FM tools and the existing `systemPrompt` as `instructions`, sends one `respond(to:)` call
- New `prompt(history:newUserMessage:)` helper: folds multi-turn history into a single user-shaped prompt with explicit "Conversation so far:" / "New user message:" headers
- `.foundationModels` skips the `noAPIKey` check at the top of `sendMessage` so it can surface its own `.unavailable` error (which the UI knows to translate to "turn on Apple Intelligence")

## Why fold history into the prompt

`LanguageModelSession` builds its transcript via successive `respond()` calls — there's no public init for pre-baked transcripts on iOS 26. Replaying history by re-calling `respond()` for each prior user message would have the model regenerate its own past replies, which is wrong. The plaintext-fold approach loses some of the cloud APIs' message-array nuance but is the most reliable pattern available.

## Migration is feature-complete after this PR

| Phase | What | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Service scaffold | ✅ #1 |
| 1 | Text path with @Generable | ✅ #2 |
| 2 | USDA Tool plumbing | ✅ #3 |
| 3 | Vision OCR for nutrition labels | ✅ #4 |
| 4 | Multimodal food photos | ✅ #5 |
| 5 | Coach chat | ✅ this |

Phase 6 (settings filter for unsupported devices, copy updates in APPSTORE.md / privacy policy / About screen, default-provider flip) was scoped out of this stack — it's polish that touches non-AI code paths and is better as its own PR after the on-device tier proves out in real-device testing.

## Known gaps (deferred to Phase 6 / follow-up work)

- The default `selectedProvider` is still `.gemini`. Flipping the default to `.foundationModels` for Apple-Intelligence-eligible devices is a Phase 6 product call.
- Settings provider picker still shows `.foundationModels` on all devices. `providersWithSavedKeys()` doesn't filter by device eligibility yet.
- No automated chat regression tests yet — would want a small fixture-based harness once a couple of test conversations are checked in.

## Test plan

- [ ] Build on Xcode 16 / iOS 26.2 SDK (verify the `Tool` / `@Generable Arguments` conformances compile)
- [ ] On Apple-Intelligence-eligible device, set provider to "On-Device (Apple Intelligence)", open Coach
- [ ] Ask "How's my weight tracking?" — verify the model answers from the system prompt's forecast section without invoking tools
- [ ] Ask "What did I eat last Tuesday?" — verify the model invokes `get_food_entries` with sensible from/to dates and uses the result
- [ ] Ask a question requiring multiple tool calls (e.g., "summarize my last 30 days") — verify the session handles the round-trip
- [ ] Multi-turn: ask a follow-up that depends on prior context — verify the "Conversation so far:" rendering preserves enough state
- [ ] On non-eligible device, attempt to chat — verify the `.unavailable` error message is user-friendly

author: ek-labs-fr
body:
## Summary
Consolidates the folder-casing drift between Git's index (`Documents/`, capital) and the on-disk reality (`documents/`, lowercase). Single lowercase folder going forward.

Also lands the two architecture/model docs that were sitting untracked locally.

## Why this needed fixing
Windows is case-insensitive (`core.ignorecase=true`); the physical folder was already `documents/` lowercase, but Git's index still had all 21 files tracked at `Documents/` (capital). New files added in recent sessions started showing up at the lowercase path → split-folder state in git status, even though there's only one physical folder.

## How the rename was done
A standard `git mv Documents documents-tmp` failed with a Windows file-lock. Used the index-only approach instead: `git rm --cached -r Documents/` followed by `git add` at the lowercase paths. Git's rename detection (default 50% similarity threshold) auto-attached for all 21 unchanged files, so blame/history is preserved — see the `rename` lines in the commit, all `(100%)`.

## What's in this PR
- **21 file renames** from `Documents/<x>` to `documents/<x>` (no content changes)
- **`documents/technical-architecture.md`** (new): full system architecture across data ingestion, processing, training, inference, MLOps, and front-end. Includes Mermaid diagrams and tech-choice justifications.

## Summary

- Adds `daft repo remove [<path>]` — removes a Git repo (bare git dir + every checked-out worktree), running `worktree-pre-remove`/`worktree-post-remove` hooks for each worktree before tearing it down. Works on any Git repo, daft-managed or vanilla; resolves the bare via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` (CLI) or `gix::discover` (gitoxide backend) so it accepts a path to the project, a worktree, or a child directory.
- Introduces a new `daft repo` subcommand category for repo-level operations (groundwork for the catalog work in #357).
- Updates the development sandbox: new `mise-tasks/sandbox/clean-repos` walks the sandbox `test/` tree and tears down every git repo it finds via `daft repo remove`, so test repos with side effects (docker containers/volumes, mounts) are cleaned up properly rather than `rm -rf`'d.

Other notable bits delivered alongside:
- Hook failure policy: best-effort per-worktree, warned-only runs exit 0, abort-mode failures bump exit code (matches `daft prune`).
- Layout-safe parent walk: never removes the directory containing the project root, even when empty (regression fix from field testing).
- Inline TUI for parallel multi-worktree removal; sequential output for single-task and empty-worktree cases (avoids the empty-table-with-headers visual glitch).
- Pre-push `cargo check --all-targets` lefthook hook so post-rebase compile breakage gets caught before push.

## Coverage

- 1525 unit tests passing, including state-machine pinning of the full event flow, gix/CLI parity tests for both backends, parent-preservation guard, head-metadata population.
- 11 bats integration tests in `tests/integration/test_repo_remove.sh` covering basic, dry-run, hooks, non-git rejection, run-from-various-paths, parent preservation (data-loss regression), bare-only repo, and the sandbox `clean-repos` helper.
- 7 YAML manual scenarios in `tests/manual/scenarios/repo/`.
- Man page, VitePress CLI reference page, help-text categorization, shell completions for bash/zsh/fish/Fig.

author: arigatoexpress
body:
## Rationale — Best Agentic Project differentiator

Sapphire Sentinel's existing payment screen is policy-shaped: mandate, budget,
domain allow-list, prompt-injection, secret-egress. Powerful, but chain-blind.
This PR adds a **chain-health axis** — Sentinel now refuses to pay for alpha
that references chain state currently in distress (USDM depegging, Aave reserves
paused at high utilisation, etc.).

The pitch for London judges: an autonomous RWA agent doesn't just need *policy*
safety, it needs *market-state* awareness. Paying $0.012 of USDC for a private
TSLA-basket signal is wasted spend if the underlying chain's stable is breaking
peg right now — the alpha can't be acted on. Sentinel + the MegaETH protocol-
access layer (PR #543) compose into a multi-chain-aware payment firewall.

See: [docs/hackathon/sapphire-sentinel-london-2026.md](../tree/feat/sentinel-megaeth-gate/docs/hackathon/sapphire-sentinel-london-2026.md).

## What changed

**New files:**
- `lib/hackathon/chain_health_gate.py` (~250 lines) — `ChainHealthGate` +
  `ChainHealthVerdict` + `default_gate()` factory. Composes
  `MegaETHProtocols.stable_health()` and `lend_overview()` into a
  `HEALTHY` / `WARNING` / `BLOCK` classification.
- `tests/unit/test_chain_health_gate.py` — 10 unit tests + 1
  `SAPPHIRE_MEGAETH_INTEGRATION=1`-gated live-mainnet test.

**Surgical edits to `lib/hackathon/sentinel.py`:**
- New optional kwargs on `evaluate_attempt()`: `gate=` and `target_chain_id=`.
  Existing callers that don't pass `gate=` get the legacy policy-only path
  unchanged — no test in `test_sentinel_hackathon.py` needed adjustment.
- `SentinelDecision` gains optional `chain_health: ChainHealthVerdict | None = None`.
- New `chain_state_degraded` risk flag + reason string.
- ~25 lines diff total in sentinel.py (verified via `git diff --stat`).

## Live mainnet evaluation (captured during this session)

```
$ SAPPHIRE_MEGAETH_INTEGRATION=1 python3 -c "from lib.hackathon.chain_health_gate import default_gate; v = default_gate().evaluate_chain(4326); print(v)"

chain_id:               4326
chain_name:             MegaETH
severity:               WARNING
peg_divergence_bps:     4.94891268882781423692158141416744721939471262486425786193851
aave_paused_reserves:   []
reasons:
  - Aave reserves frozen: ['wrsETH']
```

Real reading: USDM peg is healthy (~5 bps spread, well within the 25 bps
HEALTHY threshold), but Aave V3 has `wrsETH` listed as `frozen`, so the gate
returns WARNING. Sentinel surfaces the reason but does NOT block — exactly
the WARNING/BLOCK distinction the design calls for.

## Tests

- 10 unit tests pass (`pytest tests/unit/test_chain_health_gate.py`)
- 4 existing Sentinel tests pass unchanged
  (`pytest tests/unit/test_sentinel_hackathon.py`)
- 3 existing contract tests pass unchanged
  (`pytest tests/unit/test_sentinel_contract.py`)
- 1 live-mainnet integration test passes when `SAPPHIRE_MEGAETH_INTEGRATION=1`
- Total: **17 passed, 1 skipped** in 0.5 s

## Severity ladder

| Severity | Trigger |
|---|---|
| BLOCK | `stable_health.severity` ∈ {BREAK_100BP, CRISIS_500BP, CIRCUIT_BREAKER}, OR any Aave reserve paused with utilization > 80% |
| WARNING | `stable_health.severity` == WARNING_50BP, OR any Aave reserve frozen |
| HEALTHY | otherwise |

Fail-open by default: RPC timeout / transport error returns HEALTHY with a
'rpc unavailable' reason, so a flaky demo-day RPC doesn't block legitimate
payments. `allow_when_unavailable=False` flips this to fail-closed.

## Dependency

This branch sits on top of `feat/megaeth-wave-b3-integration` (PR #543).
**PR #543 and its parent chain need to merge before this PR.** The dependency
is the `lib/chains/megaeth/protocols.py` module — `MegaETHProtocols.stable_health()`
and `MegaETHProtocols.lend_overview()` are imported directly.

author: rm-camp-17
body:
## Summary

Implements the two handlers from the HubSpot Year-Unification project, behind a single signed webhook receiver. Reuses the existing config patterns, hubspotClient, getAssociatedIds, and the X-HubSpot-Signature-v3 verifier from PR #37.

- **Handler A** — \`mirrorChildYearForDeal\` ([lib/child-year-mirror.ts](referral-builder/vercel-api/src/lib/child-year-mirror.ts)): Child.Year = max(Deal.Year) over deals associated with the child, filtered to active stages, sticky when none qualify, idempotent.
- **Handler B** — \`spawnRenewalForDeal\` ([lib/renewal-spawner.ts](referral-builder/vercel-api/src/lib/renewal-spawner.ts)): on Program Selected, reads camp \`commission_logic_type\`, creates a next-year deal at **New Lead** when eligible. Dedups via deal_key search.
- **Webhook receiver** — POST [/api/webhooks/hubspot/deal](referral-builder/vercel-api/src/app/api/webhooks/hubspot/deal/route.ts): HMAC-verified, dispatches to both handlers, returns per-event outcomes, never poisons one event with another's failure.

161 tests passing (21 new across 3 suites).

## Assumptions for you to verify in HubSpot before deploying

1. **\`Year (Client Year - Access)\` internal name on the Children custom object.** I've defaulted to \`year\` (env-overridable as \`HS_CHILD_YEAR_PROP\`). Verify in HubSpot: *Settings → Properties → object filter \"Children\" → Year (Client Year - Access) → check \"Internal name\"*. If it differs, set the env var on Vercel.

2. **Stage IDs.** Centralized in [config.ts](referral-builder/vercel-api/src/lib/config.ts):
   - New Lead = \`appointmentscheduled\`
   - Intro Call Completed = \`qualifiedtobuy\`
   - Recommendation Plan Presented = \`presentationscheduled\`
   - Program Selected – Tuition Undecided = \`1282923123\`
   - Program Selected (Won) = \`decisionmakerboughtin\`
   - Closed Lost = \`closedlost\`
   - Active pipeline = \`default\`

3. **Renewal-eligible \`commission_logic_type\` values** (Company property): \`yearly\`, \`second_year\`, \`third_year\`, \`tfs\`, \`full_summer_delta\`. Sourced from \`ce-billing/src/services/sync/hubspot-pull.ts:41-50\`.

4. **\`HUBSPOT_CLIENT_SECRET\` is set on Vercel.** Same secret the unified card's auth middleware uses. Without it the webhook returns 500. (You set this earlier when wiring up STRICT_DEAL_AUTH.)

5. **Webhook subscriptions** to register in HubSpot Private App settings for the Camp Referral Builder app:
   - subscriptionType: \`deal.creation\`
   - subscriptionType: \`deal.propertyChange\`, propertyName: \`dealstage\`
   - subscriptionType: \`deal.propertyChange\`, propertyName: \`year1\`
   - subscriptionType: \`deal.propertyChange\`, propertyName: \`associated_child_id\`
   - Target URL: \`https://referral-builder1122026.vercel.app/api/webhooks/hubspot/deal\`

## Loop safety

Spawned renewals land at \`appointmentscheduled\` (New Lead), which is **excluded** from \`ACTIVE_DEAL_STAGES\`. The new deal will trigger a mirror webhook, but the mirror sees no active-stage deal change and exits as \`no-active-deals\` (sticky). No webhook loop.

## Divergences from spec

- The spec said "Handler A excludes New Lead and Closed Lost" — I excluded those AND validated pipeline = active, so Historic 2015-2025 deals are also excluded. Otherwise a 2018 historic deal could win the max.
- The spec said "Idempotent — should not write if value unchanged" — implemented via a pre-write read of the child's current Year. Adds one read per webhook firing; the cost is bounded.
- The spec did not specify how to handle the case where \`associated_child_id\` property is empty but a Deal→Child association exists. I added a fallback that uses the association in that case.
- The spec said "Workflow C is already handled by auto-clone-wait-year, don't rebuild" — I did not touch that.

## Test plan

- [ ] Vercel auto-deploys API
- [ ] Verify \`HS_CHILD_YEAR_PROP\` env var (if Child.Year internal name differs from \`year\`)
- [ ] Register the four webhook subscriptions in HubSpot Private App settings
- [ ] On a test deal: change stage to Tuition Undecided. Confirm Vercel logs show the mirror firing (\`updated\` or \`unchanged\`).
- [ ] On a test deal where the camp's \`commission_logic_type\` is \`yearly\`: move to Program Selected. Confirm a new deal is created at New Lead with year+1.
- [ ] On a test deal where the camp is \`one_time_only\`: move to Program Selected. Confirm no spawn (\`company-not-eligible\` in webhook outcomes).
- [ ] Idempotency: trigger the same webhook twice in a row. Second run should report \`unchanged\` (mirror) and \`already-exists\` (spawn).

### Motivation
- Improve stability and observability by capturing uncaught Flutter and platform errors and reporting them consistently.
- Prevent runtime crashes from malformed route arguments by validating route IDs and showing a user-friendly fallback page.
- Ensure behavior is covered by automated widget tests to prevent regressions.

### Description
